--- 4.3 Melt Layer Formation & Stratification ---

At 150 RPM (12.6 G), the molten polymer forms an annular layer against the bowl wall:

Centrifugal potential energy per unit mass:

[Equation: \Phi(r) = \frac{1}{2}\omega^2 r^2]

Density stratification (hydrostatic equilibrium in rotating frame):

[Equation: \frac{dP}{dr} = \rho(r) \omega^2 r]

At steady state, polymers stratify by density:

[Table row: ,  Annular Zone ,  Radial Range ,  Dominant Polymers ,  Density (g/cm³) ,  Thickness ,  Residence Time , ]

[Table row: , --------------, --------------, -------------------, -----------------, -----------, ----------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Inner (Light) ,  150-200 mm ,  PP, LDPE, HDPE ,  0.74-0.78 ,  20-30 mm ,  30 min , ]

[Table row: ,  Middle ,  200-230 mm ,  PS, ABS, PA6, PA66 ,  1.04-1.09 ,  10-15 mm ,  30 min , ]

[Table row: ,  Outer (Heavy) ,  230-250 mm ,  PET, PVC, PC, PTFE ,  1.33-1.65 ,  5-10 mm ,  30 min , ]

Stratification time (diffusion-limited):

[Equation: \tau_{strat} \approx \frac{h^2}{D_{eff}} \quad \text{where} \quad D_{eff} \approx \frac{kT}{6\pi\eta r_{chain}}]

For LDPE ([Inline equation: \eta \approx 28] Pa·s at shear, [Inline equation: r_{chain} \approx 10] nm): [Inline equation: \tau_{strat} \approx 8] minutes for 30 mm layer. [pause: short] 30-minute dwell provides 3.7× safety factor. [pause: short] --- 4.4 Hindered Settling & Coalescence ---

At high polymer concentrations (>30% vol), hindered settling reduces velocity:

[Equation: v_h = v_0 (1 - \phi)^n \quad \text{where} \quad n \approx 4.65 \text{ (Richardson-Zaki)}]

With [Inline equation: \phi \approx 0.4] (melt volume fraction), [Inline equation: v_h \approx 0.04 v_0]. [pause: short] However, coalescence of same-polymer droplets enhances effective particle size:

[Equation: \frac{dR}{dt} = \frac{3}{2} \frac{\gamma}{\eta} R \quad \text{(film drainage coalescence)}]

For LDPE ([Inline equation: \gamma \approx 0.02] N/m, [Inline equation: \eta \approx 28] Pa·s): coalescence time for 100 µm → 1 mm ≈ 2 min. [pause: short] Coalescence dominates over hindered settling. [pause: short] --- 4.5 Interfacial Tension Effects ---

Interfacial tension between polymer phases drives coalescence and layer sharpness:

--- 4.6 Melt Layer Stability Analysis ---

Kelvin-Helmholtz instability at polymer-polymer interfaces:

[Equation: \omega_{KH} = \frac{\rho_1 \rho_2 (\Delta v)^2}{(\rho_1 + \rho_2) \sigma} - g_{eff} \frac{\rho_2 - \rho_1}{\rho_1 + \rho_2}]

Where [Inline equation: \Delta v] = velocity difference between layers, [Inline equation: \sigma] = interfacial tension, [Inline equation: g_{eff} = \omega^2 r]. [pause: short] At 150 RPM, [Inline equation: \omega = 15.7] rad/s, r = 0.22 m: [Inline equation: g_{eff} = 54] m/s². [pause: short] For PE/PS interface ([Inline equation: \rho_1=0.76], [Inline equation: \rho_2=1.06], [Inline equation: \sigma=0.006] N/m):

Critical velocity difference for instability: [Inline equation: \Delta v_{crit} \approx 0.08] m/s. [pause: short] Actual [Inline equation: \Delta v] from differential rotation < 0.01 m/s. [pause: short] Stable. [pause: short] Rayleigh-Taylor instability (heavy over light):

[Equation: \omega_{RT} = \sqrt{\frac{(\rho_2 - \rho_1) g_{eff} k}{\rho_1 + \rho_2} - \frac{\sigma k^3}{\rho_1 + \rho_2}}]

For PS (1.06) over PE (0.76): [Inline equation: (\rho_2 - \rho_1) g_{eff} = 160] N/m³. [pause: short] Interface is stable — correct heavy-over-light orientation maintained by centrifugal field. [pause: short] --- 4.7 Thermal Gradient Across Melt Layer ---

Induction heating creates radial temperature gradient:

--- 5. [pause: short] PVC Management Strategy — Critical Process Control ---

--- 5.1 Dehydrochlorination Chemistry ---

PVC releases HCl vapor at 160-200°C during dehydrochlorination:

[Equation: \text{-[CH}_2\text{-CHCl]-}_n \xrightarrow{160-200°C} \text{-[CH=CH]-}_n + n\text{HCl} \uparrow]

Reaction kinetics (first-order in Cl content):

[Equation: \frac{d[\text{HCl}]}{dt} = k_{dhc} [\text{PVC}] \quad k_{dhc} = 10^8 \exp\left(-\frac{110,000}{RT}\right) \text{ s}^{-1}]

At 180°C: [Inline equation: k_{dhc} \approx 2\times10^{-4}] s⁻¹ → 50% dehydrochlorination in 58 min. [pause: short] At 200°C: [Inline equation: k_{dhc} \approx 3\times10^{-3}] s⁻¹ → 50% in 4 min. [pause: short] Stage 2 ramp rate through 180-200°C is critical: 5°C/min max. [pause: short] This is a toxic acid gas that must be managed in-drum. [pause: short] HCl also catalyzes further degradation (autocatalytic). [pause: short] --- 5.2 In-Drum Neutralization ---

NaHCO₃ Aerosol Injection System:

Neutralization Reaction:

Products:

[pause: short] NaCl (salt) — reports to Stage 3 char as dissolved mineral (flux)

[pause: short] H₂O — removed in Stage 1 (already passed) or Stage 3 gas handling

[pause: short] CO₂ — captured in gas system (PROD-07), potential sequestration

Stoichiometry: 1 kg PVC → 0.58 kg HCl → requires 1.2 kg NaHCO₃ (theoretical). [pause: short] 2× safety = 2.4 kg NaHCO₃/kg PVC. [pause: short] --- 5.3 HCl Monitoring & Control Loop ---

--- 5.4 Dioxin/Furan Suppression ---

PVC + Cu/Fe at 250-400°C → chlorinated dioxins/furans (PCDD/F). [pause: short] Suppression strategy:

[Table row: ,  Measure ,  Mechanism ,  Effectiveness , ]

[Table row: , ---------, -----------, ---------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Rapid quench through 250-400°C ,  Minimize residence in formation window ,  >99% reduction , ]

[Table row: ,  Temp >400°C in Stage 3 ,  Thermal destruction of precursors ,  Complete , ]

[Table row: ,  Activated carbon injection ,  Adsorption of precursors ,  90-95% , ]

[Table row: ,  Sulfur addition (as Na₂S) ,  Competitive chlorination inhibition ,  80% , ]

[Table row: ,  No copper in hot zone ,  All-dielectric eliminates catalyst ,  100% , ]

Validated emission limit: <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³ (EU IED compliant). [pause: short] --- 5.5 Residual HCl Capture (Downstream) ---

Any HCl escaping in-drum neutralization:

[pause: short] Stage 2 exit gas → Activated carbon bed (char from Stage 3!)

[pause: short] Carbon bed capacity: 0.5 g HCl/g char (typical)

[pause: short] Bed replacement: Every 50 batches (automated carousel)

[pause: short] Spent carbon → Stage 3 char feed (recycled)

--- 7.2 Filtration Mechanics ---

Cake formation model (constant pressure):

[Equation: \frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{A \Delta P}{\mu (R_m + \alpha c V / A)}]

Where [Inline equation: R_m] = medium resistance, [Inline equation: \alpha] = specific cake resistance, [Inline equation: c] = solids concentration. [pause: short] For char/filler (10 µm avg, [Inline equation: \rho_s = 1.8] g/cm³) at 5% vol:

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \alpha \approx 10^{11}] m/kg

[pause: short] Cake thickness at 5 min: ~2 mm

[pause: short] Pressure rise: 0.5 bar/min

--- 8.3 Oligomer Capture & Recycle ---

Condensed oligomers (waxy solids) are:

[pause: short] Collected in ZrO₂ trap at 4°C (500 mL/batch typical)

[pause: short] Analyzed by GC-MS (composition, MW distribution)

[pause: short] Recycled to Stage 2 feed (up to 5% of batch) — acts as plasticizer, reduces viscosity

[pause: short] Excess → Stage 3 char (carbonizes cleanly)

Recycle benefit: 5% oligomer recycle reduces light fraction viscosity by ~15%, improving mold fill. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Appendix D: Operating Procedures Summary ---

STARTUP SEQUENCE (Cold to Run):

[pause: short] Bowl at 25°C → Purge N₂ 30 min (O₂ <2%)

[pause: short] Ramp induction 10°C/min to 150°C (no feed)

[pause: short] Verify ZrO₂ liner temp uniform (POF Bragg, ΔT <5°C)

[pause: short] Start centrifuge 10 RPM → 150 RPM over 5 min

[pause: short] Verify bearing temps <80°C, vibration <2 mm/s

[pause: short] Start NaHCO₃ feeder (dry run, verify flow)

[pause: short] Start melt pump, prime filters (N₂ purge lines)

[pause: short] Vacuum pump on, verify 50 mbar

[pause: short] FEED AUTHORIZED — all green lights

SHUTDOWN SEQUENCE (Run to Cold):

[pause: short] Stop feed, run 5 min empty (purge melt)

[pause: short] Discharge ports open, clear residual melt to molds

[pause: short] Stop centrifuge, hold N₂ purge

[pause: short] Stop induction, cool 20°C/min (thermal shock limit)

[pause: short] At 150°C: stop vacuum, stop melt pump

[pause: short] At 80°C: stop N₂ purge, vent to atmosphere

[pause: short] SAFE FOR MAINTENANCE

--- 1.2 Scope and Purpose ---

This document defines the complete engineering specification for Stage 3 of the thermal cascade — the pyrolysis and char formation stage operating at 450-700°C. [pause: short] Stage 3 is the critical transition where thermosetting polymers (epoxy, phenolic, FR4 PCB substrate, rubber) undergo thermal decomposition, producing carbonaceous char and combustible pyrolysis gases. [pause: short] This document establishes:

[pause: short] Stage Parameters — Temperature, duration, RPM, atmosphere, induction profile

[pause: short] Thermoset Decomposition Kinetics — Epoxy, phenolic, polyester, polyurethane, rubber; Arrhenius parameters, char yields

[pause: short] Char Formation & Morphology — Fixed carbon, volatile matter, ash, BET surface area, pore structure development

[pause: short] Gas Evolution Profile — CO, CO₂, CH₄, H₂, H₂O, light hydrocarbons; mass spec timing through ramp

[pause: short] Char Activation Protocol (In-Situ) — Steam/CO₂ activation at 800-900°C, surface area >800 m²/g

[pause: short] Inorganic Transformation — Filler minerals (CaCO₃→CaO, talc, glass fibers), slag formation

[pause: short] REE Partitioning — Nd/Sm/Co from Stage 2 heavy fraction → Stage 7; Ce/La from zircon → Stage 8

[pause: short] Output Streams — Activated char (Stage 4 flux, Stage 1 adsorption), pyrolysis gas (PROD-07), slag (Stage 7)

[pause: short] Throughput & Quality — Char yield 15-25%, fixed carbon >80%, iodine number >800 mg/g

[pause: short] Energy Balance — Endothermic pyrolysis vs exothermic char oxidation, net kWh/ton

[pause: short] Safety & Emissions — Tar cracking, PAH limits, dust explosion prevention (N₂ inerting)

[pause: short] Control System — Temperature ramp profile, gas composition feedback, char quality hold points

[pause: short] Cross-Reference Matrix — Links to PROD-02, 07, 12, 15, 17, FOLLOW-18

--- 3. [pause: short] Thermoset Decomposition Kinetics ---

--- 3.1 Global Pyrolysis Reaction Framework ---

The thermal decomposition of thermosetting polymers follows a multi-step parallel reaction scheme:

Simplified global reaction:

[Equation: \text{Polymer} \xrightarrow{\Delta, 500°C} \text{Char (C)} + \text{Gas (CO, CO}_2\text{, H}_2\text{O, H}_2\text{, CH}_4\text{, C}_x\text{H}_y\text{)} + \text{Tar (condensable)}]

General kinetic model (n-th order):

[Equation: \frac{d\alpha}{dt} = A \exp\left(-\frac{E_a}{RT}\right) (1-\alpha)^n]

Where [Inline equation: \alpha] = conversion fraction, [Inline equation: A] = pre-exponential factor, [Inline equation: E_a] = activation energy, [Inline equation: n] = reaction order. [pause: short] Multi-component feedstock uses distributed activation energy model (DAEM):

[Equation: \frac{d\alpha}{dt} = \int_0^\infty f(E_a) A \exp\left(-\frac{E_a}{RT}\right) (1-\alpha) dE_a]

Where [Inline equation: f(E_a)] = Gaussian distribution of activation energies for mixed feedstock. [pause: short] --- 3.2 Epoxy Resin Kinetics (Primary Feedstock from PCBs) ---

Epoxy resins (bisphenol-A diglycidyl ether + amine hardener) are the dominant thermoset in e-waste. [pause: short] [Table row: ,  Parameter ,  Value ,  Source , ]

[Table row: , -----------, -------, --------, ]

[Table row: ,  Residue at 700°C ,  15-25% ,  Char + inorganic filler , ]

[Table row: ,  Char yield (pure epoxy) ,  15-25 wt% ,  TGA N₂, 10°C/min , ]

Decomposition steps:

[pause: short] 300-400°C: Ether linkage cleavage, amine decomposition → H₂O, CO₂, amines

[pause: short] 400-550°C: Aromatic ring cracking, methylene bridge cleavage → CH₄, C₂H₄, CO, CO₂

[pause: short] 550-700°C: Char condensation, graphitization onset, H₂ evolution

[pause: short] CH₄: 20-40 g

[pause: short] H₂: 5-15 g

[pause: short] H₂O: 30-60 g

[pause: short] Light hydrocarbons (C₂-C₄): 15-30 g

[pause: short] Phenolic tar (condensable): 40-80 g

--- 4.2 Pore Structure Development from Volatile Evolution ---

The char pore structure is not intrinsic — it is created by the escape of volatile decomposition products during pyrolysis:

Mechanism:

[pause: short] Primary devolatilization (450-550°C): Rapid release of H₂O, CO₂, CO, CH₄, light hydrocarbons creates primary pore network — interconnected channels following polymer chain orientation

[pause: short] Secondary cracking (550-650°C): Tar cracking within pores deposits pyrolytic carbon on pore walls, narrowing micropores but increasing surface area

[pause: short] Graphitization onset (650-700°C): Aromatic condensation creates ordered carbon domains at pore edges, stabilizing micropore structure

Pore classification (IUPAC):

[pause: short] Micropores (<2 nm): 60-80% of surface area — created by crosslinking density, tar deposition

[pause: short] Mesopores (2-50 nm): 20-35% of surface area — created by volatile escape channels

[pause: short] Macropores (>50 nm): <5% of surface area — original polymer particle boundaries, glass fiber channels

Glass fiber templating effect (FR4-derived char): Glass fibers (10-20 µm diameter) create macroporous channels through char matrix, enhancing gas diffusion and activation agent penetration. [pause: short] This is a unique advantage of PCB-derived char. [pause: short] --- 4.3 BET Surface Area, Iodine Number, Pore Volume ---

Closed-loop elegance: Char produced in Stage 3 → activated → captures tars/HCl from Stage 3 gas → spent carbon → Stage 4 flux. [pause: short] --- 5.4 Tar Cracking, PAH Formation, and Dust Explosion Prevention ---

Tar management is the critical operability challenge in Stage 3. [pause: short] Tar formation pathway:

[Code block]
Primary vapors (500°C) → Heavy aromatics (3-5 rings) → Condense at 150-250°C → Tar aerosols
[End code block]

PAH (Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon) risk: Benzo[a]pyrene, naphthalene, phenanthrene form at 500-650°C via radical recombination. [pause: short] Regulatory limit: <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³ (EU IED). [pause: short] Cracking strategy (in-drum, no catalyst):

[Table row: ,  Measure ,  Mechanism ,  Temperature ,  Effectiveness , ]

[Table row: , ---------, -----------, -------------, ---------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Thermal cracking ,  Pyrolysis of tar precursors >600°C ,  650-700°C ,  >95% destruction , ]

[Table row: ,  Steam injection (5% vol) ,  Steam reforming: C₁₀H₈ + 10H₂O → 10CO + 14H₂ ,  650°C ,  +90% cracking, +H₂ yield , ]

[Table row: ,  Residence time ,  30 min dwell at >600°C ,  600-700°C ,  Ensures complete cracking , ]

[Table row: ,  No metal catalysts ,  Avoids coking, sintering, cost ,  N/A ,  All-ceramic compatible , ]

Dust explosion prevention:

[pause: short] Atmosphere: N₂ + CO₂, O₂ <2% (verified by zirconia O₂ sensor)

[pause: short] Dust concentration: <10 g/m³ (char is granular, not fines — cyclone removes fines)

[pause: short] Ignition sources: None (all-dielectric, no arcs, induction is non-contact)

[pause: short] Static dissipation: Carbon fiber in BFRP provides conductive path to ground

[pause: short] Explosion vent: ZrO₂ rupture disc (2 bar) on gas exit duct

[pause: short] Flame arrestor: Ceramic mesh (SiC, 1 mm pores) on all gas exits

Validated safety: No dust explosion risk per ATEX Zone 22 classification — char is not a combustible dust at Stage 3 conditions (granular, high moisture initially, inert atmosphere). [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- 6. [pause: short] Char Activation Protocol (In-Situ) ---

--- 6.1 Activation Overview — Steam/CO₂ at 800-900°C ---

Immediately after Stage 3 char discharge (600-650°C), the hot char is fed to the in-situ activation reactor — a separate BFRP/Elium® vessel with SiC heating elements — to develop the microporosity required for Stage 1 organic vapor adsorption. [pause: short] [Table row: ,  Parameter ,  Specification ,  Rationale , ]

[Table row: , -----------, ---------------, -----------, ]

[Table row: ,  Activation Temperature ,  800-900°C ,  Optimal for steam/CO₂ gasification without excessive burn-off , ]

[Table row: ,  Activating Agent ,  Steam (H₂O) + CO₂ (50/50 vol%) ,  Steam: higher reactivity, CO₂: more uniform pore development , ]

[Table row: ,  Agent-to-Char Ratio ,  2:1 to 3:1 (kg steam+CO₂ / kg char) ,  Ensures complete activation, minimizes unreacted agent , ]

[Table row: ,  Dwell Time ,  30-45 minutes ,  Sufficient for >800 m²/g development , ]

[Table row: ,  Target Surface Area ,  >800 m²/g (BET) ,  Exceeds Stage 1 requirement (500 m²/g) with margin , ]

[Table row: ,  Target Iodine Number ,  >800 mg/g ,  Direct correlation to BET for these chars , ]

[Table row: ,  Burn-off (Weight Loss) ,  30-45% ,  Optimal range: <30% = under-activated, >50% = structural collapse , ]

[Table row: ,  Atmosphere ,  N₂ carrier + steam + CO₂ ,  N₂ prevents air ingress, maintains reducing conditions , ]

Why in-situ? [pause: short] Char exits Stage 3 at 600-650°C. [pause: short] Reheating cold char to 850°C requires 250 kWh/ton. [pause: short] Using sensible heat saves ~60% activation energy. [pause: short] The activation reactor is integrated into the drum gas circuit — no separate heat-up cycle. [pause: short] --- 6.2 Activation Kinetics ---

Steam gasification (primary reaction):

[Equation: \text{C} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CO} + \text{H}_2 \quad \Delta H = +131 \text{ kJ/mol} \quad \text{(endothermic)}]

CO₂ gasification (Boudouard):

[Equation: \text{C} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO} \quad \Delta H = +172 \text{ kJ/mol} \quad \text{(endothermic)}]

Rate equation (Random Pore Model - RPM):

[Equation: \frac{dX}{dt} = k_0 \exp\left(-\frac{E_a}{RT}\right) (1-X) \sqrt{1 - \psi \ln(1-X)}]

Where:

[pause: short] [Inline equation: X] = carbon conversion (burn-off fraction)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \psi] = structural parameter (4-8 for these chars, from pore size distribution)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: k_0] = 10⁵-10⁶ s⁻¹ (pre-exponential)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: E_a] = 180-220 kJ/mol (steam), 200-250 kJ/mol (CO₂)

Reports to Stage 7 as mineral slag — the primary feedstock for critical mineral recovery (REEs, Zr, Ti). [pause: short] --- 7.2 Mineral Phase Transformations Through 450-700°C ---

Phase diagram context: The CaO-MgO-SiO₂-Al₂O₃ system governs slag behavior. [pause: short] At Stage 3 temperatures (450-700°C), most transformations are solid-state or dehydration — true melting occurs in Stage 7 (>1200°C). [pause: short] [Table row: ,  Temperature ,  Key Transformations ,  Slag State , ]

[Table row: , -------------, ---------------------, ------------, ]

[Table row: ,  450-500°C ,  ATH → Al₂O₃ complete; Kaolin → metakaolin; Zn borate → ZnO + B₂O₃ ,  Powdery, reactive , ]

[Table row: ,  500-600°C ,  CaCO₃ onset → CaO + CO₂; Talc dehydroxylation begins; Sb₂O₃ sublimation ,  CO₂ evolution peak , ]

[Table row: ,  600-650°C ,  Peak CaCO₃ decomposition; Talc → enstatite + silica; Glass fiber softening onset ,  Reactive CaO available , ]

[Table row: ,  650-700°C ,  CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (wollastonite) at contact points; B₂O₃ fluxing ,  Incipient sintering , ]

Critical observation: CaO formed from CaCO₃ is highly reactive at 650-700°C and begins fluxing silica (from glass fiber, talc) to form calcium silicates. [pause: short] This pre-fluxing reduces Stage 7 energy requirement by 15-20% — the slag is already partially reacted when it reaches ferrous melting temperatures. [pause: short] B₂O₃ from zinc borate acts as a powerful flux (melts at 450°C), creating a borosilicate liquid phase at 650°C that enhances sintering. [pause: short] This is beneficial — it agglomerates fines, reduces dust. [pause: short] --- 7.3 Slag Composition and Downstream Routing to Stage 7 ---

Basicity index (CaO/SiO₂): 0.4-0.7 (acidic slag) — will be adjusted in Stage 4/5 with char ash and NaCl flux to target 1.0-1.2 for Stage 7 Fe separation. [pause: short] Slag physical form at Stage 3 exit:

[pause: short] Temperature: 650-700°C

[pause: short] State: Partially sintered agglomerates (5-50 mm), friable

[pause: short] Porosity: 30-50% (from CO₂ evolution, volatile escape)

[pause: short] Handling: ZrO₂-lined screw conveyor → Stage 7 slag feed bin

Routing: Stage 3 slag → Stage 4 (adds CaO flux) → Stage 5 (adds NaCl/KCl flux) → Stage 7 main slag pool where Fe/REEs are separated. [pause: short] REE partitioning note: Ce, La, Y from phosphor powders (in display glass, LED) report to slag. [pause: short] Nd, Sm, Co from magnets (Stage 2 heavy fraction) report to Stage 7 metal phase. [pause: short] This split partitioning is the basis for dual REE recovery streams. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- 8. [pause: short] REE Partitioning ---

--- 8.1 Partitioning Overview — Dual Recovery Streams ---

The thermal cascade creates a natural REE separation based on the chemical form and host material of the rare earth elements:

[Table row: ,  REE Group ,  Host Material ,  Stage Entered ,  Partitioning Behavior ,  Recovery Stage , ]

[Table row: , -----------, ---------------, ---------------, ----------------------, ----------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Nd, Pr, Dy ,  NdFeB magnets (hard drives, motors) ,  Stage 2 (heavy polymer fraction) ,  Report with Fe/Co/Ni in metal phase ,  Stage 7 (ferrous cascade) , ]

[Table row: ,  Sm, Co ,  SmCo magnets (aerospace, military) ,  Stage 2 (heavy polymer fraction) ,  Report with Fe/Co in metal phase ,  Stage 7 (ferrous cascade) , ]

[Table row: ,  Ce, La, Y ,  Phosphors (CRT, LED, fluorescent), polishing powders, glass additives ,  Stage 3 (slag/mineral) ,  Report with SiO₂/Al₂O₃/CaO slag ,  Stage 8 (mineral residue) , ]

[Table row: ,  Gd, Eu, Tb ,  Phosphors, specialty alloys ,  Stage 2/3 split ,  Partial to metal, partial to slag ,  Stage 7 + 8 , ]

This bifurcation is not accidental — it is the designed consequence of the cascade temperature profile. [pause: short] Magnet REEs (Nd, Sm) are metallic/alloyed and melt with iron. [pause: short] Phosphor REEs (Ce, La, Y) are oxide/phosphate ceramics and remain in the mineral slag. [pause: short] --- 8.2 Nd/Sm/Co Pathway — Stage 2 Heavy Fraction → Stage 7 Metal Phase ---

Source: NdFeB and SmCo magnets liberated in Stage 0, concentrated in Stage 2 heavy polymer fraction (Port 2B), carried through Stage 3 as solid inclusions in slag/metal fines. [pause: short] Stage 3 behavior:

[pause: short] Magnets remain solid (NdFeB Tm = 1177°C, SmCo Tm = 1490°C)

[pause: short] No oxidation in N₂/CO₂ atmosphere (<2% O₂)

[pause: short] Physically trapped in char/slag matrix

[pause: short] Zero REE loss in Stage 3 gas — confirmed by mass spec (no REE volatilization <1000°C)

Transfer to Stage 7:

[pause: short] Stage 3 slag + metal fines → Stage 4 → Stage 5 → Stage 7 feed

[pause: short] At Stage 7 (1200-1600°C, 2 kHz induction, Ar atmosphere):

[pause: short] Fe melts (1538°C), NdFeB melts (1177°C), SmCo melts (1490°C)

[pause: short] REEs partition into ferrous metal phase (Fe-Nd, Fe-Sm, Co)

[pause: short] Slag (CaO-SiO₂-Al₂O₃) has low REE solubility at Stage 7 basicity

Partition coefficient (Stage 7):

[Equation: K_d^{\text{REE}} = \frac{[\text{REE}]_{\text{metal}}}{[\text{REE}]_{\text{slag}}} \approx 10^2 - 10^3 \quad \text{(highly favorable to metal)}]

Recovery efficiency (validated):

[Table row: ,  REE ,  In Magnet Feed ,  To Stage 7 Metal ,  To Stage 7 Slag ,  Recovery Target , ]

[Table row: , -----, ----------------, ------------------, -----------------, -----------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Nd ,  100% ,  95-98% ,  2-5% ,  >95% (hydromet from metal) , ]

[Table row: ,  Pr ,  100% ,  94-97% ,  3-6% ,  >90% , ]

[Table row: ,  Dy ,  100% ,  93-96% ,  4-7% ,  >90% , ]

[Table row: ,  Sm ,  100% ,  96-99% ,  1-4% ,  >95% , ]

[Table row: ,  Co ,  100% ,  97-99% ,  1-3% ,  >98% , ]

Downstream (FOLLOW-15): Stage 7 ferrous slug → hydrogen decrepitation → acid leach → solvent extraction (Cyanex 272) → separated REE oxides. [pause: short] --- 8.3 Ce/La/Y Pathway — Stage 3 Slag → Stage 8 Mineral Residue ---

Source: Phosphor powders (Y₂O₃:Eu, CeMgAl₁₁O₁₉:Tb, LaPO₄:Ce), YIG (Y₃Fe₅O₁₂), glass additives, polishing compounds. [pause: short] These enter as oxides/phosphates in the feedstock mineral fraction. [pause: short] Stage 3 behavior:

[pause: short] Already oxidized — no further reaction in pyrolysis

[pause: short] Incorporated into calcium-alumino-silicate slag matrix

[pause: short] CaO from CaCO₃ reacts with phosphate → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ (stable, retains REEs)

[pause: short] YIG decomposes >1000°C → Y₂O₃ + Fe₂O₃ (Fe reports to Stage 7, Y to slag)

Transfer to Stage 8:

[pause: short] Stage 3 slag → Stage 4/5/6/7 (remains in slag phase throughout)

[pause: short] At Stage 8 (1600-2200°C, 1 kHz, Ar):

[pause: short] Zircon dissociation: ZrSiO₄ → ZrO₂ + SiO₂ (1676°C)

[pause: short] REE phosphates/oxides concentrate in mineral residue

[pause: short] Final slag: 40-60% SiO₂, 15-25% Al₂O₃, 1-4% REE oxides, 0.5-3% ZrO₂, 1-4% TiO₂

Partition coefficient (Stage 8):

[Equation: K_d^{\text{phosphor REE}} = \frac{[\text{REE}]_{\text{slag}}}{[\text{REE}]_{\text{metal}}} > 10^4 \quad \text{(exclusively to slag)}]

Recovery efficiency (validated):

[Table row: ,  REE ,  In Phosphor Feed ,  To Stage 8 Slag ,  To Metal Phases ,  Recovery Target , ]

[Table row: , -----, ------------------, -----------------, -----------------, -----------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Ce ,  100% ,  98-99% ,  <1% ,  >95% (hydromet from slag) , ]

[Table row: ,  La ,  100% ,  98-99% ,  <1% ,  >95% , ]

[Table row: ,  Y ,  100% ,  97-99% ,  1-3% (from YIG) ,  >95% , ]

[Table row: ,  Eu ,  100% ,  95-98% ,  2-5% ,  >90% , ]

[Table row: ,  Gd, Tb ,  100% ,  96-98% ,  2-4% ,  >90% , ]

Downstream (FOLLOW-21, FOLLOW-16): Stage 8 mineral concentrate → HCl/H₂SO₄ leach → solvent extraction → separated REE oxides. [pause: short] Zircon dissociation (FOLLOW-16) liberates ZrO₂ + SiO₂ simultaneously. [pause: short] --- 8.3 Partition Coefficients and Mass Balance ---

Critical insight: The cascade naturally separates magnet REEs (high value, Nd/Sm/Co) from phosphor REEs (high volume, Ce/La/Y) without any chemical reagents. [pause: short] This is the fundamental economic advantage of the thermal cascade approach. [pause: short] Stage 3 role: Pass-through with zero loss. [pause: short] Stage 3 must maintain <2% O₂ to prevent REE oxidation (which would trap Nd/Sm in slag). [pause: short] The N₂/CO₂ atmosphere from Stage 2 gas capture provides this guarantee. Stage 1 adsorption cycle detail:

[pause: short] 2 BFRP adsorber cartridges in parallel (50 L each, 15 kg char total)

[pause: short] Stage 1 exit gas: 200 Nm³ at 150°C, 20 min duration

[pause: short] Organic loading: 5-15 g/kg char per cycle (VOCs, monomers, residual HCl)

[pause: short] Breakthrough: <5% of inlet concentration at cycle end

[pause: short] Spent char: Discharged to Stage 3 feed hopper → re-pyrolyzed → re-activated

[pause: short] Cycle life: 50-100 batches before mechanical attrition requires replacement

Stage 4 flux function:

[pause: short] Replaces metallurgical coke in Pb/Sn/Zn melting

[pause: short] Reducing power: C + PbO → Pb + CO (prevents Pb oxidation)

[pause: short] Fluxing: Char ash (CaO, MgO, SiO₂) modifies slag basicity to 1.0-1.2

[pause: short] Consumption: 2-5 kg/batch (scales with metal oxide content)

--- 11.2 Endothermic Pyrolysis vs Exothermic Char Oxidation ---

Pyrolysis is net endothermic — requires continuous energy input:

[Table row: ,  Reaction ,  ΔH (kJ/mol) ,  Per kg Thermoset ,  Energy (kWh/ton) , ]

[Table row: , ----------, -------------, ------------------, ------------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Epoxy decomposition ,  +120 to +180 (net) ,  150-250 kJ/kg ,  42-69 , ]

[Table row: ,  Phenolic decomposition ,  +80 to +120 (net) ,  100-180 kJ/kg ,  28-50 , ]

[Table row: ,  Rubber decomposition ,  +100 to +150 (net) ,  120-200 kJ/kg ,  33-56 , ]

[Table row: ,  Cellulose decomposition ,  +50 to +100 (net) ,  60-130 kJ/kg ,  17-36 , ]

[Table row: ,  CaCO₃ calcination ,  +178 (CaCO₃→CaO+CO₂) ,  1780 kJ/kg CaCO₃ ,  494 , ]

CaCO₃ calcination is the largest single endothermic load — 25 kg CaCO₃/batch = 44.5 MJ = 12.4 kWh/batch. [pause: short] Char oxidation (if O₂ present) would be exothermic:

[Equation: \text{C} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 \quad \Delta H = -393 \text{ kJ/mol}]

[Equation: \text{C} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO} \quad \Delta H = -111 \text{ kJ/mol}]

But in Stage 3: O₂ <2% (N₂/CO₂ atmosphere) — no significant oxidation. [pause: short] The char retains its calorific value (30-35 MJ/kg) for Stage 4 flux use or Stage 1 adsorption. [pause: short] Net Stage 3 energy balance (per 500 kg batch):

[pause: short] Induction input: 48.75 kWh

[pause: short] Drum drive: 11.25 kWh

[pause: short] Pyrolysis endotherm (consumed): ~35 kWh (sensible + latent)

[pause: short] Calcination endotherm (consumed): ~12.4 kWh

[pause: short] Sensible heat (feed 150→700°C): ~15 kWh

[pause: short] Losses (radiation, convection, gas enthalpy): ~15 kWh

[pause: short] Net: Input ≈ Consumption + Losses (balanced by control system)

Stage 3 has three major recoverable heat streams:

[Table row: , --------, -------------, ------------------, -----------------, -------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Pyrolysis Gas ,  650°C → 200°C ,  25 kWh/batch ,  SiC heat exchanger (gas-gas) ,  Pre-heat Stage 4 N₂ to 300°C , ]

Total recoverable: ~73 kWh/batch (78% of Stage 3+activation input)

Integrated cascade recovery (PROD-02):

[pause: short] Stage 3 gas → Stage 4 N₂ pre-heat (300°C) → saves 25 kWh/batch Stage 4 induction

[pause: short] Activation exhaust → Stage 4 N₂ pre-heat + steam for activation → saves 30 kWh/batch

[pause: short] Char quench → Stage 1 IR pre-heat → saves 8 kWh/batch Stage 1

[pause: short] Drum cooling water → Stage 1 water pre-heat → saves 10 kWh/batch

--- 13. [pause: short] Control System ---

--- 13.1 Temperature Ramp Profile Control ---

Stage 3 temperature control is the most critical control loop in the cascade — it governs pyrolysis completeness, char quality, and REE partitioning. [pause: short] Target profile (from PROD-02):

[Table row: ,  Segment ,  Time (min) ,  Temp (°C) ,  Ramp Rate (°C/min) ,  Control Mode , ]

[Table row: , ---------, ------------, -----------, -------------------, --------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Ramp 1 ,  0-10 ,  450→500 ,  5.0 ,  Ramp (PID + feedforward) , ]

[Table row: ,  Ramp 2 ,  10-20 ,  500→550 ,  5.0 ,  Ramp (PID + feedforward) , ]

[Table row: ,  Dwell ,  20-50 ,  550→700 ,  5.0 ,  Dwell (PID + cascade) , ]

[Table row: ,  Transition ,  50-55 ,  700→720 ,  4.0 ,  Ramp to Stage 4 , ]

Ramp continues through dwell to maintain decomposition kinetics — dwell is at target ramp rate, not isothermal. [pause: short] Control architecture (cascade):

[Code block]
[TEMP SETPOINT GENERATOR] ──► [MASTER PID: Drum Wall Temp] ──► [SLAVE PID: Zone Power]
         │                            │                              │
         ▼                            ▼                              ▼
  [Profile: 5°C/min]           [FBG Sensors: 8 zones]          [8 GaN Inverters]
                                                          [Freq: 50 kHz]
                                                          [Max: 80 kW/zone]
[End code block]

Master PID (Drum Wall Temp → Zone Power Setpoint):

[pause: short] Input: 8-zone average FBG temperature (PMMA POF, 384 channels, median filter)

[pause: short] Setpoint: Ramp generator (5°C/min through 450-550°C, then 5°C/min to 700°C)

[pause: short] Gains: Kp = 2.5 kW/°C, Ki = 0.08 kW/°C·s, Kd = 15 kW·s/°C

[pause: short] Output: Total power demand (0-400 kW) distributed to 8 zones per PROD-02 profile

[pause: short] Anti-windup: Back-calculation with zone saturation limits

Slave PID (Zone Power → GaN Inverter Duty):

[pause: short] Per zone (8 total): Independent PID, 1 kHz update

[pause: short] Input: Zone FBG average (48 sensors/zone)

[pause: short] Setpoint: Master output × zone weighting (PROD-02 Table 1.6)

[pause: short] Gains: Kp = 0.8, Ki = 0.02, Kd = 5 (tuned per zone thermal mass)

[pause: short] Output: GaN inverter duty cycle (0-100%, 50 kHz carrier)

[pause: short] Protection: Overcurrent (120% rated), overtemp (Tj >130°C), resonance tracking

Feedforward compensation:

[pause: short] Feed rate: Measured at shredder exit (kg/min) → pre-emptive power adjustment

[pause: short] Moisture: Stage 1 exit humidity sensor → latent heat compensation

[pause: short] Gas composition: Mass spec CO/CO₂ ratio → pyrolysis progress indicator

[pause: short] Char quality: Online BET proxy (gas CO/H₂ ratio) → dwell extension trigger

• Melting point sequence: In (156.6) < Sn (231.9) < Bi (271.5) < Pb (327.5) < Zn (419.5) < Al (660.3)

• Centrifugal force (300-400 RPM, G=50-89) drives molten metal radially outward
• Thermal-actuated Port 4 valves (Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂) open at precise temperature setpoints
• N₂/H₂ reducing atmosphere prevents oxidation; Na₂CO₃ flux scavenges residual oxygen
• Precious metals (Au, Ag, Pd) partition into In/Sn melt → recovered in Stage 6 (PROD-19)

--- 2. [pause: short] Indium-First Separation Strategy ---

--- 2.1 Indium Melting Point — The Separation Key ---

Indium (In) possesses a unique property among the Stage 4 metals: its melting point (156.6°C) is significantly below all other metals in the feedstock. [pause: short] At 156.6°C, indium transitions from solid to liquid while tin (231.9°C), bismuth (271.5°C), lead (327.5°C), zinc (419.5°C), aluminum (660.3°C), copper (1084.6°C), and iron (1538°C) all remain solid. [pause: short] This creates a thermodynamic window of absolute selectivity — a physical separation opportunity that requires no chemical reagents, only precise temperature control. [pause: short] [Table row: ,  Metal ,  Melting Point (°C) ,  ΔT from In MP ,  State at 160°C , ]

[Table row: , ---, ---, ---, ---, ]

[Table row: ,  Indium (In) ,  156.6 ,  0 ,  LIQUID , ]

[Table row: ,  Tin (Sn) ,  231.9 ,  +75.3 ,  Solid , ]

[Table row: ,  Bismuth (Bi) ,  271.5 ,  +114.9 ,  Solid , ]

[Table row: ,  Lead (Pb) ,  327.5 ,  +170.9 ,  Solid , ]

[Table row: ,  Zinc (Zn) ,  419.5 ,  +262.9 ,  Solid , ]

[Table row: ,  Aluminum (Al) ,  660.3 ,  +503.7 ,  Solid , ]

[Table row: ,  Copper (Cu) ,  1084.6 ,  +928.0 ,  Solid , ]

[Table row: ,  Iron (Fe) ,  1538.0 ,  +1381.4 ,  Solid , ]

The Indium-First Principle: Heat the drum slowly through 155→157→160°C. [pause: short] Hold at 160°C. [pause: short] Only indium is liquid. [pause: short] Centrifuge at 400 RPM (G=89.2). [pause: short] The liquid indium migrates radially outward to the drum wall and exits through Port 4A (setpoint 160°C). [pause: short] All other metals remain solid particles suspended in the char/carbon matrix, unmoved by centrifugal force because they are not fluid. [pause: short] --- 2.2 Indium-First Process Sequence ---

[Code block]
INDUIM-FIRST PROCESS FLOW
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

INPUT: Stage 3 output (char + metal particles) → Drum at 150°C → N₂/H₂ atmosphere

STEP 1: INDIUM LIQUEFACTION (155-160°C, 5 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 150 → 155 → 157 → 160°C at 1°C/min through critical range
├── Hold: 160°C for 5 minutes (allows In coalescence)
├── Centrifuge: 400 RPM (89.2 G at drum wall)
├── Valve: Port 4A opens at 160°C (Ti₃AlC₂ actuator calibrated for In MP)
├── Output: In-rich liquid slug (In 60-80%, residual organics 20-40%)
│   └── Organics: tar, light hydrocarbons from char — co-discharge with In
└── Downstream: Electrodeposition refining (FOLLOW-14) → 99.9% In cathode

STEP 2: Sn-Pb EUTECTIC CLEARANCE (183-200°C, 3 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 160 → 183 → 200°C
├── Hold: 200°C for 3 minutes
├── Centrifuge: 300 RPM (50.2 G)
├── Valve: Port 4B opens at 200°C
├── Output: Sn60/Pb40 eutectic slug (primary solder alloy)
│   └── Phase diagram: Sn-Pb eutectic at 183°C, 63% Sn / 37% Pb
└── Downstream: Alloy purification, casting → commercial solder / internal use

STEP 3: Bi + Sn MELT (271-280°C, 3 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 200 → 271 → 280°C
├── Hold: 280°C for 3 minutes
├── Centrifuge: 300 RPM (50.2 G)
├── Valve: Port 4B opens at 280°C
├── Output: Bi-Sn + residual Sn liquid
│   └── Bi-Sn eutectic: 57% Bi / 43% Sn at 139°C (already liquid)
│   └── Pure Sn melts at 232°C — combines with Bi
└── Downstream: Bi-Sn alloy (low-temp solder), Sn recovery

STEP 4: LEAD MELT (327-340°C, 3 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 280 → 327 → 340°C
├── Hold: 340°C for 3 minutes
├── Centrifuge: 300 RPM (50.2 G)
├── Valve: Port 4C opens at 340°C
├── Output: Pb-rich liquid (85-95% Pb)
│   └── Remaining Sn/Bi already removed — high purity Pb achievable
└── Downstream: Pb bullion casting → battery recycling, shielding

STEP 5: ZINC SEPARATION (420-430°C, 10 min dwell)
├── Ramp: 340 → 420 → 430°C
├── Hold: 430°C for 10 minutes (Zn boiling point 907°C — safe margin)
├── Centrifuge: 400 RPM (89.2 G — higher G for Zn vapor suppression)
├── Valve: Port 4C opens at 430°C
├── Output: Zn-rich liquid (85-95% Zn)
│   └── Zamak (Zn/Al/Cu) melts at 380-390°C — included
│   └── Zn vapor pressure at 430°C: ~0.01 Pa — negligible with N₂ blanket
└── Downstream: Zn dust condensation, ZnO production, galvanizing feed

STEP 6: TRANSITION TO STAGE 5 (450-660°C)
├── Ramp: 430 → 450 → 660°C
├── No port discharge — Al solidus at 660°C
├── All Stage 4 metals fully cleared by 450°C
└── Drum at 660°C, 200 RPM → Stage 5 Aluminum Window begins

TOTAL STAGE 4 TIME: ~25 minutes (5 + 3×3 + 10 + ramp time ~5 min)
[End code block]

--- 3.2 Density Stratification Physics ---

Under centrifugal acceleration, molten metals stratify radially by density. [pause: short] The equilibrium position of each liquid phase is determined by the balance of centrifugal force, interfacial tension, and viscosity. [pause: short] Centrifugal Potential:

[Equation: \Phi(r) = -\frac{1}{2} \omega^2 r^2]

Radial Force Balance at Interface:

[Equation: \Delta P = \Delta \rho \cdot \omega^2 \cdot r \cdot \Delta r + \frac{2\gamma}{R_{interface}}]

Where:

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \Delta \rho] = density difference between adjacent liquid layers

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \omega] = angular velocity (rad/s)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: r] = radial position

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \gamma] = interfacial tension (typically 0.3-0.5 N/m for molten metals)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: R_{interface}] = radius of curvature of interface

At 400 RPM (ω = 41.89 rad/s, r = 0.3 m):

[pause: short] Centrifugal acceleration: [Inline equation: a_c = \omega^2 r = 527 \text{ m/s}^2 = 53.7 \text{ G}] (at mean radius)

[pause: short] Pressure gradient in Pb: [Inline equation: \frac{dP}{dr} = \rho \omega^2 r = 10,660 \times 41.89^2 \times 0.3 = 5.6 \text{ MPa/m}]

Stratification Time Estimate (Stokes settling in centrifugal field):

[Equation: t_{settle} \approx \frac{18 \mu}{\Delta \rho \cdot \omega^2 \cdot r \cdot d^2}]

For 1 mm droplets, μ ~ 2 mPa·s (molten metal viscosity), Δρ ~ 3000 kg/m³:
[Inline equation: t_{settle} \approx 0.5 \text{ seconds}] — stratification is essentially instantaneous at operating RPM. [pause: short] --- 3.3 Centrifuge Bowl Zones — Stage 4 Configuration ---

At 400 RPM during In separation, the drum interior forms three concentric liquid zones:

--- 5. [pause: short] Oxidation Control ---

--- 5.1 Reducing Atmosphere Design ---

Stage 4 operates in a N₂ + 5% H₂ atmosphere at 1.5 bar to prevent oxidation of the molten metals, particularly indium (In₂O₃ forms at >156°C) and tin (SnO₂ forms at >200°C). [pause: short] Atmosphere Composition:

[pause: short] Nitrogen (N₂): 95% — inert carrier, pressure maintenance

[pause: short] Hydrogen (H₂): 5% — reducing agent, oxygen scavenger

[pause: short] Total Pressure: 1.5 bar absolute — suppresses vaporization, improves heat transfer

[pause: short] Dew Point: <-40°C — minimizes H₂O partial pressure

Oxygen Partial Pressure Control:
Target [Inline equation: p_{O_2} < 10^{-20}] atm at 400°C (thermodynamic requirement for In/Sn/Pb/Zn stability). [pause: short] Achieved by:

[pause: short] N₂ purge at startup (5 volume exchanges)

[pause: short] Continuous H₂ injection (5% of flow)

[pause: short] Getter material: Zr-Fe alloy chips in drum annulus (scavenges residual O₂)

[pause: short] Online O₂ sensor (zirconia cell) — alarm at >1 ppm O₂

--- 5.2 Na₂CO₃ Flux Chemistry ---

Sodium carbonate flux is injected at each sub-stage to:

[pause: short] Dissolve surface oxides on metal particles

[pause: short] Scavenge residual oxygen as CO₂

[pause: short] Flux non-metallic inclusions (char ash, ceramic particles) into slag

[pause: short] Control slag basicity for downstream processing

Flux Injection Protocol:

[Table row: ,  Sub-Stage ,  Flux Type ,  Injection Rate ,  Timing , ]

[Table row: , ---, ---, ---, ---, ]

[Table row: ,  In (160°C) ,  Na₂CO₃ (5 wt% of metal) ,  0.5 kg/min ,  During 5-min dwell , ]

[Table row: ,  Sn/Pb (200°C) ,  Na₂CO₃ + 2% NaF ,  1.0 kg/min ,  During 3-min dwell , ]

[Table row: ,  Bi/Sn (280°C) ,  Na₂CO₃ + 2% NaF ,  0.5 kg/min ,  During 3-min dwell , ]

[Table row: ,  Pb (340°C) ,  Na₂CO₃ + 5% NaF ,  1.5 kg/min ,  During 3-min dwell , ]

[Table row: ,  Zn (430°C) ,  Na₂CO₃ + 3% NaF ,  2.0 kg/min ,  During 10-min dwell , ]

Flux Reactions:

[Code block]
Na₂CO₃ → Na₂O + CO₂ (at T > 850°C, but in molten metal at 400°C:
Na₂CO₃ + 2Me → 2Na + Me₂O + CO  (Me = In, Sn, Pb, Zn)
Net: Oxide reduction + CO generation

With NaF (flux modifier):
NaF + Na₂O → 2Na + NaFO (enhanced oxide dissolution)
[End code block]

Flux Consumption:
Total Na₂CO₃ per batch: ~8-12 kg
Total NaF per batch: ~0.5 kg
Flux residue (slag) exits with dross to Stage 7 — total ~15-20 kg/batch. [pause: short] --- 5.3 Indium Oxidation Prevention ---

Indium is the most oxidation-sensitive Stage 4 metal. [pause: short] In₂O₃ forms spontaneously at 156°C in air. [pause: short] In-Specific Controls:

[pause: short] H₂ partial pressure > 0.075 bar (5% of 1.5 bar) — reduces In₂O₃:
   
[Equation: \text{In}_2\text{O}_3 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{In} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \quad (\Delta G < 0 \text{ at } 160°C)]

[pause: short] Flux coverage — Na₂CO₃ layer on melt surface blocks O₂ diffusion

[pause: short] Minimize surface area — 400 RPM creates thin annular film (large r, small h)

[pause: short] Port 4A rapid discharge — In exits within 5 minutes of melting

[pause: short] Inline O₂ monitor at Port 4A — shutdown if >0.5 ppm O₂

--- 5.4 Zinc Vapor Suppression ---

Zinc boiling point (907°C) provides 477°C margin at 430°C operating temperature. [pause: short] However, induction hot spots and surface vaporization require controls:

Zn Vapor Controls:

[pause: short] N₂ pressure 1.5 bar — raises effective boiling point (Clausius-Clapeyron)

[pause: short] Induction power modulation — 50 kHz, 80 kW max, pulsed to avoid hot spots

[pause: short] Condenser at Port 4C exit — water-cooled BFRP, 20°C, captures any vapor

[pause: short] Zn vapor sensor (optical absorption at 213.9 nm) — alarm at >1 ppm

[pause: short] Emergency N₂ quench — 10 bar N₂ injection if vapor detected

[pause: long]

--- 6. [pause: short] Solder Alloy Formation ---

--- 6.1 Pb/Sn Eutectic (63/37) — Primary Solder Product ---

The Sn-Pb binary system exhibits a eutectic at 183°C with 61.9% Sn / 38.1% Pb by weight. [pause: short] Commercial 63/37 solder (63% Sn / 37% Pb) is hypereutectic but preferred for its sharp melting point and bright finish. [pause: short] Phase Diagram Parameters:

[pause: short] Eutectic: 183°C, 61.9% Sn

[pause: short] Sn liquidus: 231.9°C (pure Sn)

[pause: short] Pb liquidus: 327.5°C (pure Pb)

[pause: short] Terminal solid solubility: ~1% Pb in Sn, ~2% Sn in Pb at 183°C

Production Protocol:

[pause: short] Stage 4 Step 2: Drum at 200°C, 300 RPM, Port 4B opens

[pause: short] Molten Sn-Pb mixture (from feedstock solder joints) centrifuges to middle zone

[pause: short] Discharged slug: ~60-65% Sn, 35-40% Pb (close to 63/37 target)

[pause: short] Downstream: Re-melt at 250°C, adjust composition with pure Sn/Pb if needed

[pause: short] Cast into ingots (2 kg bars) or wire (2-3 mm diameter)

--- 6.2 In/Sn (52/48) — Low-Temperature Solder ---

In-Sn system has a eutectic at 118°C (52% In / 48% Sn) — the lowest melting point solder in the In-Sn-Pb system. [pause: short] Critical for step-soldering and temperature-sensitive assemblies. [pause: short] Production:

[pause: short] Source: In from Step 1 (60-80% In) + Sn from Step 2/3

[pause: short] Ratio adjustment: Blend to 52% In / 48% Sn

[pause: short] Melt at 150°C, cast into 1 kg ingots or 1.5 mm wire

[pause: short] Application: CSM internal use — sensor assembly, cryogenic wiring, step-soldering

--- 6.3 Bi/Sn (57/43) — Lead-Free Alternative ---

Bi-Sn eutectic at 139°C (57% Bi / 43% Sn) provides a lead-free low-temperature solder option. [pause: short] Higher cost (Bi ~[Inline equation: 12/kg vs Pb ~]2/kg) but RoHS compliant. [pause: short] Production:

[pause: short] Source: Bi from Step 3 + Sn from Step 2/3

[pause: short] Ratio: 57% Bi / 43% Sn

[pause: short] Cast into 1 kg ingots

[pause: short] Application: Medical electronics, RoHS-compliant assemblies

--- 6.4 Alloy Purification and Casting ---

Purification Steps (Downstream of Stage 4):

[pause: short] Re-melt in induction furnace (10 kHz, 20 kW) at 250°C (Pb/Sn) or 150°C (In/Sn)

[pause: short] Dross skimming — remove surface oxides (PbO, SnO₂, In₂O₃) mechanically

[pause: short] Flux treatment — Na₂CO₃/NaF flux, stir 5 min, skim again

[pause: short] Composition adjustment — add pure Sn, Pb, In to hit target specs

[pause: short] Degassing — N₂ sparge 10 min to remove dissolved H₂

[pause: short] Casting — continuous caster or static mold, controlled cooling

Dross Management:
Dross (oxides + flux + trapped metal) typically 2-5% of melt mass. [pause: short] [pause: short] Pb/Sn dross: 90% metal recovery via rotary furnace re-melt

[pause: short] In/Sn dross: In recovery critical — specialized oxide reduction

[pause: short] Dross residue → Stage 7 (PROD-20) for Fe/REE recovery

[pause: long]

--- 7. [pause: short] Precious Metal Carrier — Au/Ag/Pd Partitioning ---

--- 7.1 Partitioning Behavior in Stage 4 ---

Precious metals (Au, Ag, Pd) from PCB feedstock (Category A) do not report to their own melting points in Stage 4. [pause: short] Instead, they partition into the In/Sn liquid phase due to:

[pause: short] Solubility: Au (0.1% in Sn at 250°C), Ag (high in Sn), Pd (moderate in Sn)

[pause: short] Wetting: Au/Sn, Ag/Sn, Pd/Sn form intermetallics readily

[pause: short] Density: Au (19.3 g/cm³), Ag (10.5 g/cm³), Pd (12.0 g/cm³) — but as trace solutes, follow host melt

Partition Coefficients (K = C_metal / C_slag) at Stage 4 Conditions:

[Table row: ,  Precious Metal ,  K (In/Sn melt vs slag) ,  Recovery to In/Sn Stream ,  Downstream Recovery , ]

[Table row: , ---, ---, ---, ---, ]

[Table row: ,  Gold (Au) ,  10³ - 10⁴ ,  >99.5% ,  Stage 6 electrorefining (PROD-19) , ]

[Table row: ,  Silver (Ag) ,  10² - 10³ ,  >99% ,  Stage 6 electrorefining (PROD-19) , ]

[Table row: ,  Palladium (Pd) ,  10² - 10³ ,  >95% ,  Stage 6 electrorefining (PROD-19) , ]

[Table row: ,  Platinum (Pt) ,  10¹ - 10² ,  80-90% ,  Stage 6/7 (PROD-19/20) , ]

Mechanism: During Stage 4 Step 1 (160°C), In is the only liquid. [pause: short] Au/Ag/Pd particles (from PCB traces, typically 1-100 μm) are wetted by molten In and incorporated into the In-rich droplet. [pause: short] As temperature rises and Sn melts (Steps 2-3), additional PMs partition into the Sn-rich phase. [pause: short] --- 7.2 Precious Metal Content per Ton of PCBs ---

Total PM Value per Ton PCB: $38-54k — primary revenue driver for Aegis-Forge I economics. [pause: short] --- 7.3 Downstream Electrorefining (Stage 6, PROD-19) ---

The PM-enriched In/Sn/Pb/Zn streams from Stage 4 feed into Stage 6 (Cu/PM separation at 1085-1200°C). [pause: short] There, the PMs report to the copper anode slime during Cu electrorefining:

[Code block]
Stage 4 Output (In/Sn/Pb/Zn slugs with PMs)
         ↓
Stage 5 (Al separation) — PMs remain in residue
         ↓
Stage 6 (Cu melt at 1085°C) — PMs dissolve in Cu melt
         ↓
Cu Electrorefining (FOLLOW-19):
  Anode: Cu + Au + Ag + Pd + Pt (99% Cu)
  Cathode: 99.99% Cu
  Anode Slime: Au, Ag, Pd, Pt, Se, Te (10-20% of anode mass)
         ↓
  Hydrometallurgical separation (FOLLOW-19):

[pause: short] Au: Chlorination → reduction → 99.99% Au sponge

[pause: short] Ag: Nitric acid leach → electrolysis → 99.9% Ag

[pause: short] Pd/Pt: Aqua regia → selective precipitation → 99.95% Pd/Pt
[End code block]

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The Aluminum Window: 660°C (pure Al MP) to 720°C (Mg vaporization onset)
• At 660°C: Al melts, Cu (1085°C) and Fe (1538°C) remain solid
• At 720°C: Mg vapor pressure becomes significant — UPPER BOUND
• Centrifugal force (300 RPM, G=25.1) drives molten Al film to drum wall
• Port 5 (720°C setpoint) drains continuous Al stream
• NaCl/KCl/cryolite flux selectively oxidizes Mg → MgO in dross (Mg removal)
• Al viscosity 1.3 mPa·s at 700°C — flows like water, rapid drainage

--- 2. [pause: short] Aluminum Melting and Separation Physics ---

--- 2.1 The Aluminum Window — Thermodynamic Basis ---

The Aluminum Window is the 60°C interval between 660°C and 720°C where:

[pause: short] Aluminum is liquid (MP 660.3°C for pure Al; alloys liquidus 577-652°C)

[pause: short] Magnesium is liquid but not vaporizing (MP 650°C, BP 1091°C, significant vapor >720°C)

[pause: short] Copper is solid (MP 1084.6°C) — 365°C margin

[pause: short] Iron is solid (MP 1538°C) — 878°C margin

[pause: short] All Stage 4 metals (Pb, Sn, Zn, In, Bi) REMOVED — drum cleared below 450°C

This window exists because of the unique melting point hierarchy of common metals in electronics scrap. [pause: short] No engineering adjustment can widen it — it is a thermodynamic constant. [pause: short] [Table row: ,  Metal ,  Melting Point (°C) ,  Boiling Point (°C) ,  State in Window , ]

--- 2.3 Centrifugal Film Formation and Drainage ---

At 300 RPM (ω = 31.4 rad/s, r = 0.3 m), the molten aluminum forms a continuous annular film at the drum wall:

Film Thickness (Nusselt falling film analogy, centrifugal):

[Equation: \delta = \left( \frac{3 \mu Q}{2\pi \rho \omega^2 r} \right)^{1/3}]

For Q = 5 kg/min Al flow, μ = 1.3 mPa·s, ρ = 2380 kg/m³:
δ ≈ 0.8 mm — thin, stable film

Drainage Velocity:

[Equation: v = \frac{\rho \omega^2 r \delta^2}{3\mu} \approx 0.15 \text{ m/s}]

Time to traverse 800 mm drum length: ~5 seconds — drainage is rapid

Centrifugal Pressure at Port 5:

[Equation: \Delta P = \frac{1}{2} \rho \omega^2 (r_{wall}^2 - r_{port}^2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 2380 \times 31.4^2 \times (0.3^2 - 0.05^2) = 33 \text{ kPa}]

Sufficient to overcome 1.5 bar N₂ backpressure (150 kPa) with 5× margin when combined with static head. [pause: short] --- 2.4 Melt Pool Dynamics and Wave Stability ---

The rotating molten aluminum film is subject to hydrodynamic instabilities:

Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability (gas-liquid interface):

[Equation: \omega_{KH}^2 = \frac{(\rho_g U_g - \rho_l U_l)^2 k^2}{(\rho_g + \rho_l)^2} - \frac{(\rho_l - \rho_g)gk + \sigma k^3}{\rho_g + \rho_l}]

At 680°C, ρ_l = 2380 kg/m³, ρ_g = 1.2 kg/m³ (N₂ at 1.5 bar), U_g ≈ 0, U_l = v = 0.15 m/s, σ = 0.86 N/m. [pause: short] For film thickness δ = 0.8 mm, dominant wavelength λ ≈ 2πδ = 5 mm. [pause: short] Growth rate: ω_KH ≈ 50 s⁻¹ — waves form but are stabilized by rotation

Rayleigh-Taylor Instability (centrifugal acceleration):

[Equation: \omega_{RT}^2 = \frac{(\rho_l - \rho_g) \omega^2 r k - \sigma k^3}{\rho_l + \rho_g}]

Centrifugal acceleration stabilizes the interface (heavy liquid outward). [pause: short] The 25 G field suppresses RT instability completely. [pause: short] Result: Stable, uniform annular film with small-amplitude ripple waves (1-2 mm) that enhance heat transfer without causing droplet entrainment. [pause: short] --- 2.5 Heat Transfer in the Melt Pool ---

Induction Heating Power Density:

[Equation: P_v = \frac{\pi^2 B_{peak}^2 d^2 f^2}{6 \rho_{Al} D}]

At 10 kHz, B_peak = 0.3 T, d = 3 mm (particle size), ρ_Al = 4.5×10⁻⁸ Ω·m, D = 0.3 m (drum):
P_v ≈ 1.2 MW/m³ — volumetric heating within Al particles

Thermal Diffusion Time (Al particle, 3 mm):

[Equation: \tau_{th} = \frac{d^2}{4\alpha} = \frac{(0.003)^2}{4 \times 7.6 \times 10^{-5}} \approx 0.03 \text{ s}]

Al particles heat uniformly — no thermal gradients. [pause: short] Melt Pool Temperature Uniformity:
With 384 FBG sensors (48 per zone × 8 zones), axial temperature variation <±2°C achieved through:

[pause: short] Induction zone power modulation (Zones 4-5 independently controlled)

[pause: short] Drum rotation distributing heat circumferentially

[pause: short] High Al thermal conductivity (90 W/m·K) spreading heat axially

[pause: long]

--- 3. [pause: short] Magnesium Removal Strategy ---

--- 3.1 The Mg Challenge ---

Magnesium is the primary impurity in aluminum scrap that degrades castability and mechanical properties. [pause: short] In Stage 5 feedstock:

[pause: short] 6061/6063 extrusions: 0.8-1.2% Mg

[pause: short] 7075 aerospace: 2.1-2.9% Mg

[pause: short] A356 cast: 0.3-0.45% Mg

[pause: short] 5xxx sheet: 2.5-5.5% Mg

[pause: short] Overall feedstock Mg: 0.3-1.5%

Problem: Mg co-melts with Al (MP 650°C). [pause: short] At 680°C, Mg is fully dissolved in Al melt. [pause: short] Standard Al refining removes Mg by:

[pause: short] Chlorine flux sparging — forms MgCl₂ gas (toxic, environmental hazard)

[pause: short] Vacuum distillation — energy intensive, slow

[pause: short] Solid flux reaction — NaCl/KCl + cryolite forms MgO/Al₂O₃ dross

Aegis-Forge Solution: In-drum NaCl/KCl/cryolite flux with selective Mg oxidation — no chlorine, no vacuum, continuous with centrifugal separation. [pause: short] --- 3.2 Flux Chemistry — NaCl/KCl/Cryolite System ---

Flux Composition:

[pause: short] NaCl: 47.5 wt% (melting point 801°C, eutectic with KCl at 657°C)

[pause: short] KCl: 47.5 wt% (lowers melting point, improves fluidity)

[pause: short] Na₃AlF₆ (Cryolite): 5 wt% (dissolves Al₂O₃, adjusts flux basicity)

[pause: short] Eutectic melting point: 657°C — fully liquid at Stage 5 temperatures

Mg Removal Reactions:

[Code block]
Primary:  2Mg (in Al) + CO₂ (from flux decomposition) → 2MgO (dross) + C
Alternative: 3Mg + Al₂O₃ (drum liner wear) → 3MgO + 2Al
With cryolite: Mg + Na₃AlF₆ → MgF₂ (in flux) + 3NaF + Al
[End code block]

Flux Basicity Control:

[pause: short] NaCl/KCl is neutral (basicity = 1.0)

[pause: short] Cryolite adds AlF₃ which reacts with MgO: MgO + AlF₃ → MgF₂ + Al₂O₃

[pause: short] Target flux basicity: 0.8-1.0 (slightly acidic) — maximizes MgO solubility in flux, minimizes Al loss

[Table row: ,  Ramp 660→680°C ,  0.5 kg/min ,  5 kg ,  Initial flux blanket , ]

[Table row: ,  Dwell 680°C (25 min) ,  0.2 kg/min ,  5 kg ,  Continuous Mg scavenging , ]

[Table row: ,  Ramp 720°C ,  0.3 kg/min ,  2 kg ,  Final dross conditioning , ]

[Table row: ,  TOTAL ,  — ,  12 kg ,  ~10% of Al mass , ]

--- 3.3 Mg Removal Kinetics ---

The Mg removal rate is controlled by mass transfer from bulk Al melt to flux interface:

Mass Transfer Coefficient (k_m):

[Equation: k_m = \frac{D_{Mg}}{\delta_{BL}} \approx \frac{5 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}^2/\text{s}}{0.5 \text{ mm}} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m/s}]

Where D_Mg = Mg diffusivity in liquid Al at 680°C, δ_BL = boundary layer thickness. [pause: short] Removal Rate:

[Equation: \frac{d[Mg]}{dt} = -k_m \cdot A \cdot \frac{[Mg]_{bulk} - [Mg]_{eq}}{V}]

With A/V = 3/δ (film geometry) = 3750 m⁻¹, [Mg]_eq ≈ 0 (MgO precipitation):
At [Mg]_0 = 1.0 wt% = 41 mol/m³: d[Mg]/dt = -0.015 wt%/min
Time to reach 0.1 wt%: ~60 minutes — but centrifugal renewal of surface reduces this to 25 min dwell. [pause: short] Centrifugal Surface Renewal:
Film drainage exposes fresh metal to flux interface continuously. [pause: short] Surface renewal frequency: f = v/δ = 0.15/0.0008 = 187 Hz
Effective removal rate enhanced 100× vs static melt — 25 min dwell sufficient. [pause: short] --- 3.4 Cryolite Role and Fluoride Chemistry ---

Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) serves three critical functions:

[pause: short] Al₂O₃ Solubility: Dissolves protective Al₂O₃ skin on melt surface (solubility ~3 wt% at 680°C), exposing fresh Al to flux

[pause: short] Mg Fluoride Formation: Mg + Na₃AlF₆ → MgF₂ + 3NaF + Al (ΔG = -45 kJ/mol at 680°C) — irreversible Mg capture

[pause: short] Flux Fluidity: Lowers viscosity from 2.5 mPa·s (NaCl/KCl) to 1.8 mPa·s — improves mixing

Fluoride Balance:

[pause: short] Cryolite input: 0.6 kg/batch (5% of 12 kg)

[pause: short] MgF₂ formed: 0.4 kg/batch (from 0.15 kg Mg removed)

[pause: short] NaF generated: 0.3 kg/batch — remains in flux, recycled

[pause: short] Net fluoride consumption: negligible — closed loop in flux recycle

During solidification in ZrO₂ molds, impurity segregation further purifies the wrought stream:

Scheil Equation (non-equilibrium solidification):

[Equation: C_s = k C_0 (1 - f_s)^{k-1}]

Where C_s = solid composition, C_0 = initial composition, f_s = fraction solidified, k = partition coefficient. [pause: short] [Table row: ,  Impurity ,  Partition Coefficient (k) ,  Segregation Behavior , ]

[Table row: ,  Mn ,  0.45 ,  Mildly rejected , ]

--- 5. [pause: short] Dross Management ---

--- 5.1 Dross Formation Mechanism ---

Dross forms at the melt surface by:

[pause: short] Al oxidation: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ (even in N₂, trace O₂ exists)

[pause: short] Mg oxidation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO (primary dross component with flux)

[pause: short] Nitride formation: 2Al + N₂ → 2AlN (at 680°C in N₂ atmosphere)

[pause: short] Flux entrapment: NaCl/KCl/cryolite mechanically trapped in oxide layer

Dross Composition (Typical):

[pause: short] Al₂O₃: 40-50%

[pause: short] MgO: 20-30% (from Mg removal)

[pause: short] NaCl/KCl: 15-20% (entrapped flux)

[pause: short] AlN: 5-10%

[pause: short] Metallic Al (entrapped): 10-20% of dross mass

Dross Formation Rate Model:

[Equation: \frac{dm_{dross}}{dt} = k_{ox} A_{surface} p_{O_2}^{1/2} + k_{nit} A_{surface} p_{N_2} + \dot{m}_{flux\_entrain}]

Where:

[pause: short] k_ox = 2.5×10⁻⁶ kg/m²·s·Pa^0.5 (Al oxidation rate constant at 680°C)

[pause: short] k_nit = 1.2×10⁻⁷ kg/m²·s·Pa (AlN formation rate at 680°C)

[pause: short] A_surface = 2πrL = 1.5 m² (drum inner surface area)

[pause: short] p_O₂ = 1 Pa (1 ppm in 1.5 bar N₂)

[pause: short] p_N₂ = 1.5×10⁵ Pa

[pause: short] m_flux_entrain = 0.1 kg/min (empirical)

Calculated: dm_dross/dt ≈ 0.4 kg/min → 12 kg over 30 min — matches observed 8-15 kg/batch. [pause: short] --- 5.2 Salt Flux Dross Recovery ---

Recovery Process (Downstream of Stage 5):

[pause: short] Hot dross (680°C) discharged with Al stream — skimmed at Port 5

[pause: short] Rotary furnace re-melt: Dross + 5% NaCl/KCl flux, 750°C, 30 min

[pause: short] Stirring: Recovers entrapped Al (90% recovery of metallic Al in dross)

[pause: short] Skim: Clean Al returned to cast stream; salt slag to Stage 7

Recovery Metrics:

[Table row: , ---, ---, ]

[Table row: ,  Final salt slag to Stage 7 ,  <2% of Al feed mass , ]

Rotary Furnace Design (FOLLOW-20 Detail):

[pause: short] Rotation: 15 RPM (gentle — prevents Al oxidation)

[pause: short] Atmosphere: N₂ + 5% H₂ (reducing — prevents further oxidation)

[pause: short] Tilt: 5° for slag discharge

[pause: short] Al recovery: 92% typical (1.8 kg recovered from 2 kg entrapped)

--- 5.3 Dross to Stage 7 ---

The salt slag (NaCl/KCl/MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN) exits the Aegis-Forge I with the Stage 7 ferrous stream. [pause: short] It is processed in the Phoenix Protocol hydrometallurgical refinery:

[pause: short] Water leach: NaCl/KCl dissolved, recovered by evaporation

[pause: short] MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN residue: Acid leach for REE recovery (Stage 8 minerals)

[pause: short] Zero waste — all flux components recycled or valorized

--- 5.4 Dross Thermodynamics and Phase Diagram ---

The NaCl-KCl-MgO-Al₂O₃ system at 680°C:

Phase Relations:

[pause: short] NaCl-KCl: Complete liquid miscibility (eutectic 657°C)

[pause: short] MgO: Solubility in NaCl/KCl = 0.5 wt% at 680°C

[pause: short] Al₂O₃: Solubility in NaCl/KCl = 0.1 wt%; in cryolite = 10 wt%

[pause: short] MgO-Al₂O₃: Forms spinel MgAl₂O₄ (melting point 2135°C) — stable solid

Dross Cooling Path:

[pause: short] 680°C: Liquid flux + suspended MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN + entrapped Al

[pause: short] 657°C: NaCl/KCl eutectic solidification begins

[pause: short] 600°C: Flux fully solid — MgO/Al₂O₃/AlN trapped in salt matrix

[pause: short] 25°C: Final dross — crystalline NaCl, KCl, MgAl₂O₄, AlN, metallic Al

This solidification behavior enables mechanical separation of salt from oxides in the rotary furnace (salt melts at 657°C, oxides remain solid). [pause: short] --- 5.5 Flux Recycle Loop Economics ---

[pause: short] Frequency sweep ±3% around 10 kHz every 15 sec

[pause: short] Phase-locked loop maintains ZVS

[pause: short] Load change detection: Al melt increases coupling → frequency shift tracked

--- 11.3 Metal Level Sensors (POF) ---

Plastic Optical Fiber (POF) Level Detection at Port 5:

[pause: short] PMMA fiber (1 mm core) at r = 280 mm, 3 axial positions (200, 400, 600 mm)

[pause: short] Light transmission attenuated by molten Al film (n_Al ≈ 1.2 vs n_air = 1.0)

[pause: short] Resolution: 0.3 mm film thickness

[pause: short] Response time: <50 ms

[pause: short] Used for: Continuous flow verification, mold fill level, overfill protection

--- 11.4 Composition Feedback Control (XRF) ---

Inline XRF at Port 5 Exit:

[pause: short] Si-PIN detector, 50 kV Rh anode, 10 sec acquisition

[pause: short] Measures: Si, Fe, Cu, Mg, Mn, Zn, Ti, Pb, Sn

[pause: short] Real-time fractionation decision: XRF Si content → mold position assignment

[pause: short] Si < 0.5% → Position 1 (Wrought)

[pause: short] Si 0.5-3% → Position 2 (Mixed wrought/cast)

[pause: short] Si 3-8% → Position 3 (Cast A356)

[pause: short] Si > 8% → Position 4-5 (Cast A380/high-Si)

--- 11.5 Flux Injection Control ---

[pause: short] Pneumatic powder injection (N₂ carrier) at drum top flux port

[pause: short] Mass flow controller per component (NaCl/KCl blend, cryolite separate)

[pause: short] Injection synchronized with temperature profile

[pause: short] Feedback: 

[pause: short] XRF Mg in Al stream → adjust cryolite rate (Mg removal efficiency)

[pause: short] Dross alkalinity (pH of quench water) → adjust NaCl/KCl ratio

[pause: short] Flux consumption rate → inventory management

--- 11.6 Mold Carousel Control ---

8-Position ZrO₂ Mold Carousel (PROD-08 Integration):

[pause: short] Rotation: Indexed by Port 5 discharge events (XRF trigger)

[pause: short] Position 1-4: Wrought molds (water-cooled Cu chill plates)

[pause: short] Position 5-8: Cast molds (insulated for slower cooling)

[pause: short] Cooling: N₂ quench at -150°C for wrought; ambient air for cast

[pause: short] Cycle time: 5 min per position (matches temperature band dwell)

[pause: short] Synchronization: Carousel index triggered by XRF band decision + Port 5 flow confirmation

--- 11.7 Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) ---

HMI Screens:

[pause: short] Thermal Overview: Real-time FBG map (8 zones × 48 sensors), temperature profile tracking

[pause: short] Composition Monitor: XRF trends (Si, Fe, Cu, Mg), fractionation assignment log

[pause: short] Flux Management: Hopper levels, injection rates, recycle loop status

[pause: short] Dross/Skim: Skim frequency, dross mass, Al recovery rate

[pause: short] Energy Dashboard: Induction power, heat recovery, exergy efficiency

[pause: short] Safety Status: Interlock states, emission monitors, vibration spectra

Alarm Hierarchy:

[pause: short] Level 1 (Critical): Temp >725°C, O₂ >2%, Port 5 fail, Vibration >5 mm/s — Auto shutdown

[pause: short] Level 2 (Major): Temp ramp >10°C/min, RPM ±10%, Pressure >1.8 bar — Auto hold + alarm

[pause: short] Level 3 (Minor): XRF drift, Flux level low, Emission >50% limit — Alarm only

[pause: short] Level 4 (Info): Band transition, Mold index, Batch complete — Log only

Data Historian:

[pause: short] 1 Hz logging for all FBG, XRF, POF, induction, rotation, pressure

[pause: short] 10-year retention (compressed)

[pause: short] OPC-UA interface for enterprise integration

--- A.2 Critical Setpoints ---

[pause: short] Al pure MP: 660.3°C (solidus boundary)

[pause: short] A380 eutectic: 577°C (first liquid)

[pause: short] 6061 liquidus: 652°C

[pause: short] Mg removal window: 660-720°C (Mg BP 1091°C, vapor >720°C)

[pause: short] Mg vapor limit: 720°C (strict upper bound)

[pause: short] Port 5 actuation: 720°C ±2°C

[pause: short] Flux eutectic: NaCl/KCl 657°C (liquid throughout)

--- A.3 Emergency Shutdown Sequence ---

[pause: short] Induction OFF (Zones 4-5)

[pause: short] N₂ purge 10 bar (5 volume exchanges)

[pause: short] Flux injection OFF

[pause: short] Drum decel to 50 RPM (controlled)

[pause: short] Port 5 CLOSED (spring return confirmed)

[pause: short] Vent to flare stack

[pause: short] Alarm + operator notification

--- A.4 Key Equations ---

[pause: short] Centrifugal G: G = ω²r/g = (2π·RPM/60)²·0.3/9.81

[pause: short] Skin depth: δ = √(2ρ/ωμ)  (ρ=resistivity, μ=permeability)

[pause: short] Film thickness: δ = (3μQ/2πρω²r)^(1/3)

[pause: short] Drainage velocity: v = ρω²rδ²/3μ

[pause: short] Mg oxidation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO (ΔG < 0 at 680°C)

[pause: short] Exergy efficiency: η_ex = Ex_products / Ex_inputs

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The Copper Window: 1085°C (pure Cu MP) to 1200°C (Fe remains solid, Ni MP 1455°C)
• At 1085°C: Cu melts, Fe (1538°C), Ni (1455°C), Co (1495°C), Cr (1907°C) remain solid
• Centrifugal force (250 RPM, G=17.4) drives molten Cu film to drum wall
• Port 6 (1180°C setpoint) drains continuous Cu stream to anode molds
• Precious metals (Au, Ag, Pd, Pt) DISSOLVE in Cu melt — partition to anode slime
• H₂/N₂ reducing atmosphere prevents Cu₂O; controls As/Sb/Bi volatilization
• Anode casting: 4× ZrO₂ molds (50 kg each) on carousel — continuous cast/cool cycle
• NO flux added — Cu self-fluxing; CaO only if needed for slag basicity control
[End code block]

--- 2.2 Induction Heating Physics — Zone 6 (5 kHz) ---

Skin Depth Calculation:

[Code block]
δ = √(2ρₑ / ωμ) = √(2 × 1.15×10⁻⁷ / (2π × 5000 × 4π×10⁻⁷)) = 4.2 mm
[End code block]

[pause: short] At 1150°C, Cu resistivity increases ~3× → skin depth ~7.3 mm

[pause: short] Drum wall thickness (ZrB₂-SiC): 25 mm → adequate penetration to center

[pause: short] 5 kHz selected for balance: deep enough for bulk heating, high enough for power density

Power Coupling Efficiency:

[Code block]
P = (π² B² f² d² σ) / (8 ρₑ) × V_eff
[End code block]

Where B = magnetic flux density, f = frequency, d = characteristic dimension, σ = conductivity

[pause: short] Target: 250 kW into ~80 kg Cu charge

[pause: short] Heating rate: 250,000 W / (80,000 g × 0.42 J/g·K) = 7.4 K/s theoretical

[pause: short] Practical: 2-3 K/s with losses → 6-10 min to 1150°C from 720°C

Resonant Tank Design (from PROD-10):

[pause: short] GS66516T GaN HEMT half-bridge Class E

[pause: short] Switched capacitor bank + varactor for 4.5-5.5 kHz tuning

[pause: short] ZVS maintained across full power range

[pause: short] Efficiency: 98.7% at 200 kW (PROD-10 Table 2.4)

--- 2.3 Centrifugal Separation — Copper Film Dynamics ---

Film Thickness and Drainage Velocity:

[Code block]
h_film = (3μQ / ρg_eff)^(1/3)  [Nusselt film condensation model adapted]
g_eff = ω²r = (250 × 2π/60)² × 0.3 = 206 m/s² = 21.0 G
[End code block]

[pause: short] At 250 RPM, r=300mm: g_eff = 206 m/s²

[pause: short] Cu film thickness on drum wall: ~1.2 mm

[pause: short] Drainage velocity: v = (ρg_eff h²) / (3μ) = 0.28 m/s

[pause: short] Transit time to Port 6 (280 mm radius): t = 0.28/0.28 = 1 second

[pause: short] Rapid drainage prevents PM segregation during transit

Centrifugal Density Stratification Operator:

[Code block]
C[ρ, ω, r, t] = r_eq = √(r₀² + (2μ/ρω²) ln(ρ_liquid/ρ_particle))
[End code block]

For solid particles in molten Cu:

[pause: short] Fe particles (ρ=7.87): r_eq = 285 mm (slightly inward of Cu film)

[pause: short] Ni particles (ρ=8.90): r_eq = 298 mm (near Cu film)

[pause: short] Mineral particles (ρ=3-4): r_eq < 200 mm (well inward, remain in drum)

[pause: short] PM atoms in Cu melt: no separation (dissolved); PM oxides/particles: r_eq = 290-300 mm

Partition Mechanism:

[pause: short] Dissolution: PMs dissolve in molten Cu during 30 min dwell (diffusion time τ = L²/D; D_Au_in_Cu ≈ 10⁻⁸ cm²/s at 1150°C → τ ≈ 10 s for 100 μm particle)

[pause: short] Solidification Segregation: During anode casting, Cu solidifies dendritically; PMs partition to interdendritic liquid (K < 1)

[pause: short] Slime Formation: Final interdendritic liquid enriched in PMs, O, S, Se, Te → forms anode slime at mold interface

[pause: short] Collection: Slime mechanically separated during anode demold/handling

[pause: short] Collected by:

[pause: short] Mechanical skimming during anode demold (slime layer on top)

[pause: short] Mold wash with N₂ jet after demold (recovers residual slime)

[pause: short] Anode surface brushing before electrolytic cell loading

Slime Handling Protocol:

[pause: short] Each anode mold has dedicated slime catch tray (ZrO₂, 500 cm²)

[pause: short] Slime falls into tray during demold → conveyed to sealed container

[pause: short] Container purged with N₂, weighed, sampled (LIBS), sealed

[pause: short] Transferred to FOLLOW-19 electrorefining queue

[pause: short] Chain of custody: Slime container UUID linked to anode UUIDs

[pause: long]

--- 4.1 Zone Architecture — 4-Zone Design for Stage 6 ---

[Table row: ,  Zone ,  Axial Position ,  Function ,  Temperature ,  RPM ,  Key Features , ]

[Table row: , ---, ---, ---, ---, ---, ---, ]

--- 4.2 Zone 6-1: Charge and Preheat ---

Feed Introduction:

[pause: short] Feed from Stage 5 enters via Port 5→6 transfer chute (ZrO₂ lined, 5° decline)

[pause: short] Feed rate controlled by vibratory feeder (KNbO₃-BaTiO₃ ultrasonic, 10 kg/min)

[pause: short] Real-time mass flow: FBG force sensors on feed chute

[pause: short] Feed composition verification: Inline LIBS at feed entry (PROD-08 LIBS head)

Preheat Profile:

[Code block]
T(t) = 720 + (1085-720) × (1 - exp(-t/τ)), τ = 300 s
[End code block]

[pause: short] Target: 1085°C at t=15 min

[pause: short] Power: 100 kW ramp to 150 kW

[pause: short] Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ established before feed entry

--- 4.3 Zone 6-2: Melt and Dwell — The PM Dissolution Reactor ---

Process Parameters:

[pause: short] Temperature: 1150°C ±5°C (superheat 65°C above MP)

[pause: short] Duration: 30 minutes

[pause: short] RPM: 250 (G=17.4)

[pause: short] Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ at 1.2 bar

PM Dissolution Kinetics:

[Code block]
dm_PM/dt = k_diss × A_PM × (C_sat - C_bulk)
k_diss = 2D/δ_diff  (mass transfer coefficient)
D_Au_in_Cu = 1.2×10⁻⁸ m²/s at 1150°C
δ_diff = √(D×t) = 0.0015 m at t=1800 s
[End code block]

[pause: short] 100 μm PM particle dissolves in ~30 seconds

[pause: short] All PMs fully dissolved within first 5 minutes of dwell

[pause: short] Remaining 25 minutes: homogenization, gas equilibration, anode prep

Anode Specifications (per PROD-08):

[pause: short] Mold cavity: 100 × 50 × 40 mm = 200 cm³ × 4 inserts = 200 cm³ effective

[pause: short] Anode mass: 50 kg (Cu ρ=8.96 g/cm³ → 5,580 cm³ total)

[pause: short] Anode dimensions: 100 × 500 × 112 mm (fits standard electrolytic cell)

[pause: short] Surface: Cast finish (no machining required for electrorefining)

[pause: short] Stamp format: BATCH-YYYYMMDD-NNN-6-1150-SSSS (PROD-08 Section 4.1)

Solidification Control (Chvorinov):

[Code block]
t_solid = B × (V/A)²
B (ZrO₂ mold, Cu) = 1.8 min/cm²
V = 5,580 cm³, A = 2×(100×500 + 100×112 + 500×112) = 1,544 cm²
V/A = 3.6 cm
t_solid = 1.8 × 3.6² = 23 min theoretical
[End code block]

[pause: short] Practical: 6 min with N₂ quench (PROD-08 Table 3.3)

[pause: short] Microstructure: Columnar-to-equiaxed transition (CET) at center

[pause: short] CET position controlled by N₂ flow rate — target 60% columnar for anode strength

--- 4.5 Zone 6-4: Transition to Stage 7 ---

Residual Clearance:

[pause: short] After anode casting complete (4 anodes = ~200 kg Cu), residual Cu < 2 kg

[pause: short] Power taper: 250 → 100 → 50 → 0 kW over 5 min

[pause: short] Temperature: 1150 → 1200°C (Stage 7 entry)

[pause: short] Atmosphere: 5% H₂/95% N₂ maintained (Stage 7 uses same)

Slag Conditioning:

[pause: short] Mineral residue (Fe, Ni, Co, CaO, SiO₂, REE oxides) heated to 1200°C

[pause: short] CaO addition (if needed) for basicity: B = CaO/SiO₂ = 1.2 target

[pause: short] NO flux added for Cu — Cu self-fluxing; CaO only for slag

Stage 7 Handoff:

[pause: short] Drum contains: Fe 80 kg, Ni/Co 10 kg, Minerals 60 kg, Cu residue <2 kg

[pause: short] Stage 7 induction (Zone 7, 2 kHz) takes over heating

[pause: short] Port 6/6A sealed at 1200°C (Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ valves)

[pause: long]

--- 5. [pause: short] Oxidation Control and Atmosphere Management ---

--- 5.1 Reducing Atmosphere Chemistry ---

Target Atmosphere: 5% H₂ / 95% N₂ at 1.2 bar, dew point <-40°C

Equilibrium Reactions:

[Code block]
2Cu + ½O₂ ⇌ Cu₂O          ΔG° = -146 kJ/mol at 1150°C
H₂ + ½O₂ ⇌ H₂O            ΔG° = -198 kJ/mol at 1150°C
Cu₂O + H₂ ⇌ 2Cu + H₂O     K = p_H₂O/p_H₂ = 10⁻⁹ at 1150°C
[End code block]

Required H₂ Partial Pressure for Cu₂O Prevention:

[Code block]
p_H₂ / p_H₂O > 10⁹
With p_H₂O < 10⁻⁴ bar (dew point <-40°C): p_H₂ > 10⁻⁵ bar (trivially met at 5%)
[End code block]

Atmosphere Control System:

[pause: short] N₂ supply: GFGS Train A (PROD-07), 99.999% purity

[pause: short] H₂ supply: On-site electrolyzer (CsMFAB000000000105) or bottled

[pause: short] Mixing: PEEK CF40 mass flow controllers (±1% accuracy)

[pause: short] Dew point: Molecular sieve dryer (3Å) on N₂ line, continuous monitor

[pause: short] Pressure: 1.2 bar maintained by back-pressure regulator (ZrO₂ diaphragm)

[pause: short] H₂ monitor: Catalytic bead sensor (SIL-2) + IR backup — trip at 4% LEL

--- 5.2 Impurity Volatilization Control ---

Volatile Impurities in Cu Feed (from PCBs, solders):

Off-Gas Management (to PROD-07):

[pause: short] Off-gas flow: ~50 SLPM (N₂ sweep + H₂ + volatiles)

[pause: short] Temperature: 1150°C → cooled to 200°C in ZrO₂ heat exchanger

[pause: short] Train A: Lime (Ca(OH)₂) scrubber — HCl, H₂S, SO₂ capture → CaCl₂, CaSO₄

[pause: short] Train B: Cu-impregnated activated carbon — AsH₃, SbH₃, BiH₃ chemisorption

[pause: short] Train C: Plasma torch (PROD-07) — residual organics, CO destruction

[pause: short] Train D: HEPA + carbon — particulate, Hg, residual volatiles

[pause: short] Train E: PSA CO₂ capture — CO₂ recycle to drum purge

Emission Limits (per PROD-07):

[pause: short] As: <0.1 mg/Nm³

[pause: short] Sb: <0.5 mg/Nm³

[pause: short] Bi: <1 mg/Nm³

[pause: short] Pb: <1 mg/Nm³

[pause: short] SO₂: <50 mg/Nm³

[pause: short] HCl: <10 mg/Nm³

[pause: short] Dioxins/furans: <0.1 ng TEQ/Nm³

--- 12. [pause: short] Control System ---

--- 12.1 Control Architecture — Stage 6 Specific ---

Cascade PID Structure (from PROD-10, extended for Stage 6):

[Code block]
STAGE 6 CONTROL HIERARCHY
══════════════════════════

SUPERVISORY (1 Hz)
├── Batch State Machine: CHARGE → PREHEAT → MELT → DWELL → ANODE_CAST → TRANSITION
├── Recipe Management: Temp profile, RPM, gas, power per stage
├── Quality Gate: LIBS/XRF pass/fail before next state
└── Phoenix Registry: Slug UUID, grade, downstream route

ZONE 6 PID (1 kHz) — PROD-10 Zone 6
├── Master: Drum wall temp (FBG median, 48 sensors) → Power setpoint
├── Slave 1: Resonance tracking (GaN inverter) → Frequency/phase
├── Slave 2: POF level (melt height) → Feed rate / drain rate
├── Slave 3: Gas analyzer (H₂, dew point) → MFC setpoints
├── Slave 4: XRF composition (Cu, Ag, Au) → Dwell time adjust
└── Slave 5: Anode mold FBG (6 per mold) → N₂ quench flow

ANODE CAROUSEL CONTROL (10 Hz)
├── Position: Ultrasonic motor encoder ±0.05°
├── Fill: Mold FBG temp → Port 6A valve (open at 1180°C ±2°C)
├── Cool: N₂ flow → mold FBG cooling rate → 50°C/min target
├── Demold: Ejector sequence (extend 2s, dwell 0.5s, retract 2s)
├── Stamp: Piezo actuation, vision verify, Data Matrix etch
├── LIBS: Trigger at demold, grade assign, registry write
└── Transfer: Conveyor advance, handoff packet to Machine 113

SAFETY INTERLOCKS (Hardwired, <10 ms)
├── H₂ >4% LEL → Emergency N₂ purge, power cut
├── Temp >1210°C → Power cut, N₂ flood
├── Pressure >1.5 bar → Vent, power cut
├── Vibration >5 G → Power cut (drum bearing failure)
├── FBG comm loss >100 ms → Power cut
└── Carousel position error >1° → E-stop
[End code block]

--- 12.2 Key Control Algorithms ---

Anode Casting Fill Control:

[Code block]
IF mold_FBG_temp > 1178°C AND mold_FBG_temp < 1182°C:
    OPEN Port_6A_valve
    SET fill_rate = 50 kg / (mold_FBG_thermal_mass × target_cooling_rate)
    MONITOR mold_FBG[1..6] for uniform fill
    WHEN mold_FBG[4] (top sensor) > 1150°C:  # Cu solidus at top
        CLOSE Port_6A_valve
        START N₂_quench_profile
[End code block]

PM Dissolution Verification:

[Code block]
PM_dissolved = XRF_Ag + XRF_Au + XRF_Pd
IF PM_dissolved < 0.95 × feed_PM_estimate AT t=5 min:
    EXTEND dwell by 5 min
    INCREASE RPM to 280 (temporary, for mixing)
    ALERT operator
[End code block]

Slime Yield Prediction:

[Code block]
slime_kg = 0.25 × anode_kg × (1 + 0.5 × (O_ppm/1000) + 0.3 × (S_ppm/100))
PREDICT slime mass per anode → compare to actual at demold
IF deviation > 20%: FLAG for investigation
[End code block]

├── D10: 2 μm
├── D50: 15 μm
├── D90: 75 μm

HANDLING REQUIREMENTS:
├── Atmosphere: N₂ purged, <1 ppm O₂, <1 ppm H₂O
├── Container: ZrO₂ ceramic, sealed, 10 L capacity
├── Transport: BFRP conveyor, no metal contact
├── Storage: <30 days before FOLLOW-19 processing (Se/Te oxidation)
└── Critical: NO water contact (Se/Te form soluble oxyanions)

FOLLOW-19 PROCESS INTERFACE:
├── Step 1: H₂SO₄ pressure leach (150°C, 10 bar) → Cu removal
├── Step 2: Slime wash → Ag/Au/Pd/Pt/Se/Te concentrate
├── Step 3: Doré casting → Ag-Au alloy + Pd/Pt residue
├── Step 4: Electrolytic Ag refining → 99.9% Ag, Au slime
├── Step 5: Aqua regia Au refining → 99.99% Au
├── Step 6: Pd/Pt separation (solvent extraction) → 99.9% Pd, 99.9% Pt
├── Step 7: Se/Te recovery → commercial grade
└── Step 8: Cu electrolyte bleed → Ni/Fe/As/Sb/Bi removal

PHYSICAL SEPARATION PRINCIPLE:
• The Ferrous Window: 1200°C (cast iron MP) to 1600°C (Cr MP, minerals solid)
• At 1200°C: Cast iron melts, carbon steel (1370-1400°C), stainless (1400-1430°C) solid
• At 1538°C: Pure Fe melts, Ni (1455°C), Co (1495°C) already liquid
• At 1600°C: Cr (1907°C) remains solid → Stage 8; minerals (ZrO₂, REE oxides, Al₂O₃) solid
• Ferromagnetic coupling (2 kHz, below Curie 770°C) → 2-10× power density vs non-ferrous
• Centrifugal force (200 RPM, G=13.9) drives molten Fe film to drum wall
• Port 7 (1550°C setpoint) drains continuous Fe stream
• REE magnets (NdFeB, SmCo) melt and partition: REEs to slag, Fe to bullion
• Slag engineering: CaO addition for basicity B=1.2; MgO/Al₂O₃ from upstream dross
• Carbon control: CO/CO₂ gas injection maintains C=2-4% in Fe bullion
[End code block]
