--- Combined Heuristic Introduction — PROD-25 Structural Analysis & FEA ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is forced into its thermomechanical FEA framework by a single irreducible principle: every load-bearing component must survive the simultaneous application of 2200°C thermal gradients, 500 RPM centrifugal loading, 10 bar pressure containment, and Carrington-class electromagnetic hostility — without a single structural metal. [pause: short] This constraint cascades into every structural decision:

[pause: short] Ceramics-only rotating drum: The ZrB₂-SiC drum (600 mm ID, 35 mm wall) is the only moving hot part. [pause: short] It must withstand 84.5 G centrifugal acceleration at ID, 5 bar internal pressure, and a 2000°C radial thermal gradient (2200°C ID → 700°C OD) — all while remaining electrically insulating (ρ > 10⁶ Ω·m) to maintain Carrington immunity. [pause: short] Any metallic reinforcement would couple GIC currents (5000 nT/s induces >100 A/km) into the structure, creating unintended heating paths and potential arc paths to the induction coils. [pause: short] [pause: short] Composite-only stationary vessel: The BFRP/Elium® vessel (900 mm ID, 18 mm wall) must contain 10 bar design pressure while thermally isolating the composite (Tg = 80°C) from the 2200°C drum across a 68 mm gap (50 mm aerogel + 18 mm BFRP). [pause: short] No metallic flanges, no metallic bolts, no metallic gaskets — the entire pressure boundary is ceramic/composite. [pause: short] The 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts and ZrO₂ gasket at the PEEK CF40 flanges are the only closure mechanism. [pause: short] [pause: short] All-dielectric port valves: The 8 material exit ports use Ti₃AlC₂ MAX phase thermal actuators and 3Y-TZP ZrO₂ pistons — entirely ceramic, no metal springs (PEEK CF40 wave springs only), no metal seals. [pause: short] The actuator operates at the drum OD (≤700°C) where Ti₃AlC₂ retains 320 MPa strength. [pause: short] [pause: short] Seismic without steel: The BFRP box beam frame must qualify to IEEE 693 High (PGA = 1.0g, ZPA = 1.5g) without any steel reinforcement. [pause: short] 6× BFRP stiffening rings + 4 vertical struts provide the required HCLPF ≥ 1.5g. [pause: short] What breaks if violated: A single steel bolt in the flange → GIC pickup → common-mode voltage on FBG interrogators → control system corruption. [pause: short] A metallic drum reinforcement → induction coupling → uncontrolled eddy currents → thermal runaway. [pause: short] A metallic port actuator → magnetic coupling at Stage 7 (2 kHz, ferromagnetic) → actuation failure at 1600°C. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap this analysis closes is the measured divergence between room-temperature structural allowables and the combined thermomechanical reality of the operating envelope. [pause: short] Three specific gaps demand this integrated FEA approach:

[pause: short] Thermal stress dominates centrifugal stress by 4×: At Stage 8, the 2000°C radial gradient generates 180 MPa thermal stress at the drum ID, while 500 RPM centrifugal loading adds only 42 MPa. [pause: short] Linear superposition (225 MPa combined) matches FEA, but the temperature-dependent material properties (E = 300 GPa, σ_f = 350 MPa at 2200°C) mean the safety factor is only 1.55×. [pause: short] Room-temperature analysis (σ_f = 620 MPa) would predict SF = 2.75× — a dangerous 78% overestimate. [pause: short] The gap: temperature-dependent strength vs. [pause: short] constant-property design. [pause: short] [pause: short] Port reinforcement requires coupled thermal-mechanical optimization: Unreinforced ports have K_t = 3.0 (σ_vm = 350 MPa at 2200°C → SF = 1.0). [pause: short] The ZrB₂-SiC sleeve + OD bulge reduces K_t to 1.6 (σ_vm = 210 MPa → SF = 1.81×). --- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I structural analysis is the divergence between single-load-case allowable stress design and the measured behavior of ceramics and composites under combined extreme thermomechanical loading. [pause: short] Three specific locks prevent traditional ASME/ASCII code-based design from closing this gap:

[pause: short] Ceramic strength is not a constant — it's a temperature-dependent distribution: ASME BPVC Section VIII uses constant allowable stress (S) with safety factors. [pause: short] But ZrB₂-SiC flexural strength drops from 620 MPa (RT) to 350 MPa (2200°C) — a 44% reduction. [pause: short] The Weibull modulus (m = 12) means failure probability is volume-dependent and stress-dependent. [pause: short] At Stage 8, the drum ID sees 225 MPa von Mises — SF = 1.55× on 350 MPa. [pause: short] But this is the mean strength; 10% of the volume sees >250 MPa (SF < 1.4×). [pause: short] The lock: constant safety factor on temperature-dependent Weibull strength. [pause: short] [pause: short] Composite failure is interactive, not separable: BFRP/Elium® vessel failure is governed by Tsai-Wu criterion (F_ijσ_iσ_j + F_iσ_i = 1), where hoop, axial, and shear stresses interact. [pause: short] At the gas port penetration under design pressure + thermal gradient, hoop = 52 MPa, axial = 35 MPa, shear = 22 MPa. [pause: short] Individual SFs: hoop 12.5×, axial 18.6×, shear 3.6×. [pause: short] But combined Tsai-Wu FI = 0.22 (SF = 4.5× on interaction). [pause: short] Sequential checking of individual components would miss the interaction. [pause: short] The lock: interactive failure criteria vs. [pause: short] component-by-component allowables. [pause: short] [pause: short] Thermal buckling is a load case, not a material property: The vessel external surface reaches 200°C during operation. [pause: short] The thermal compressive stress (78 MPa) exceeds the pressure tensile stress (25.5 MPa), creating net compression. [pause: short] The buckling critical pressure drops from 18.4 bar (RT) to 12.7 bar (200°C) — a 31% reduction. [pause: short] Standard pressure vessel codes treat buckling as an external pressure check; here it's an operating condition. [pause: short] The lock: thermal compression as a design-driving load case. [pause: short] Common thread: Every lock is a coupling between temperature and mechanical behavior that traditional codes treat as separable. [pause: short] The empirical lock is the sum of all neglected thermomechanical couplings. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- The Mathematical Key ---

The single computational primitive that generates the structural solution is the temperature-dependent thermomechanical equilibrium equation solved on the coupled FEA mesh:

[Equation: \nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} + \mathbf{f}_b = 0, \quad \boldsymbol{\sigma} = \mathbb{C}(T) : (\boldsymbol{\epsilon} - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{th}(T)) - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{creep}(t,T,\sigma)]

Where:

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \mathbb{C}(T)] = temperature-dependent stiffness tensor (orthotropic for BFRP, isotropic for ceramics)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{th}(T) = \int_{T_{ref}}^T \boldsymbol{\alpha}(T') dT'] = thermal strain from temperature history

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{creep}] = Norton-Bailey creep strain (for T > 1800°C)

[pause: short] [Inline equation: \mathbf{f}_b] = body forces (centrifugal: [Inline equation: \rho \omega^2 r], seismic: [Inline equation: \rho \mathbf{a}_{ground}])

This one equation, discretized on the 2.8M-element drum mesh and 50K-element vessel mesh, with temperature-dependent material properties from PROD-24, is the atomic computation. [pause: short] Everything in this document derives from it:

[pause: short] Drum FEA (Section 2): The equation solved on the rotating drum mesh with centrifugal body force and thermal strain from PROD-24's radial gradient. [pause: short] The Weibull post-processor integrates [Inline equation: P_f = 1-\exp[-(\sigma/\sigma_0)^m V/V_0]] over the stressed volume. [pause: short] [pause: short] Vessel FEA (Section 3): The equation on the shell mesh with orthotropic [Inline equation: \mathbb{C}(T)], thermal strain from 250°C→150°C gradient, and pressure load. [pause: short] Tsai-Wu failure index computed from [Inline equation: \boldsymbol{\sigma}] at each integration point. [pause: short] [pause: short] Port valve (Section 5): The equation on the actuator strip mesh with [Inline equation: \mathbb{C}(T)] for Ti₃AlC₂/ZrO₂ bilayer, thermal strain from ΔαΔT, contact boundary condition at piston seat. [pause: short] [pause: short] Seismic (Section 8): The equation with [Inline equation: \mathbf{f}_b = \rho \mathbf{a}_{ground}(t)] from IEEE 693 RRS time history. [pause: short] Modal superposition (30 modes) for transient response. [pause: short] [pause: short] Fatigue (Section 9): The equation's stress history output feeds Coffin-Manson [Inline equation: \Delta\varepsilon_p/2 = \varepsilon_f'(2N_f)^c] and Paris law [Inline equation: da/dN = C(\Delta K)^m]. [pause: short] [pause: short] NDT (Section 10): The equation's stress distribution defines critical locations for UT/AE sensor placement. [pause: short] [pause: short] Safety factors (Section 12): The equation's output σ_vm and FI are divided by temperature-dependent allowables. [pause: short] The mathematical key is not the FEA software, not the mesh, not the post-processor — it is the temperature-dependent thermomechanical equilibrium equation with thermal strain and creep, evaluated on the coupled mesh. [pause: short] If you solve this equation correctly with the right [Inline equation: \mathbb{C}(T)], [Inline equation: \boldsymbol{\alpha}(T)], [Inline equation: \sigma_f(T)], you get the structural answer. [pause: short] The mesh is just the numerical vessel; the material correlations are the input; the equation is the primitive. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is forced into its all-dielectric topology by a single irreducible principle: no copper conductor may cross the pressure boundary into the 2200°C induction zone during a Carrington-class geomagnetic storm (dB/dt = 5000 nT/s). [pause: short] This constraint is not a design preference — it is physics. [pause: short] A 5000 nT/s field induces >100 V/km on conductors. [pause: short] At 50 m cable run: >5 V common-mode. [pause: short] The GaN gate drivers (GS66516T, LMG1210) have 6 V threshold. [pause: short] A single ground loop couples kV from GIC into the gate drive — instant destruction. [pause: short] The FBG interrogators (VCSEL, InGaAs PIN) share the same vulnerability. [pause: short] The isolation transformer secondary is floating — no neutral-earth bond — because a grounded neutral provides the return path for GIC to enter the process electronics. [pause: short] The constraint cascades into every electrical decision:

[pause: short] All 480+ sensors on PMMA POF: FBG temperature/strain (384), POF level (16), pyrometer (8), mass spec (8), XRF (8), pressure (24), flow (32), vibration (16), encoder (2), E-stop (8) — zero copper

[pause: short] All 96+ actuators on PMMA POF: GaN gates (16), varactor bias (32), cap bank (48), MFC (32), port valves (8), carousel (1), flux (8), quench (16), drum drive (1), crane interlock (4)

[pause: short] Cooling water: PEX-a tubing (cross-linked PE, ρ>10¹⁴ Ω·m) — no copper pipe, no conductive path to building ground

[pause: short] Enclosures: BFRP/Elium® (ρ>10¹² Ω·m) — no steel cabinets, no metallic conduit

[pause: short] Penetrations: Al₂O₃/ZrO₂ ceramic bushings only — no metal feedthroughs

[pause: short] Power distribution: Isolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A — no ground reference on process side

What breaks if violated: A single copper wire for just the E-stop → GIC antenna → 5 V common-mode on GaN gate → GaN shoot-through → 500 kW inverter destruction → drum thermal runaway → vessel overpressure → catastrophic failure. [pause: short] The constraint is binary: all-dielectric or dead forge. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- The Recursive Guarantee ---

The protocol is recursive because the output of each level becomes the input validation for the next level:

[pause: short] Component HIL (Level 0) → Module ATP (Level 1)

[pause: short] Module ATP (Level 1) → Integration ITF (Level 2)

[pause: short] Integration ITF (Level 2) → FAT ATP (Level 3)

[pause: short] FAT ATP (Level 3) → SAT ATP (Level 4)

[pause: short] Operational trends (Level 4) → Component HIL updates (Level 0)

This is the fractal pattern: Stimulate at scale N → Observe at scale N → Compare at scale N → Act at scale N → Feedback to scale N-1 and N+1. [pause: short] The same Stimulate→Observe→Compare→Act logic applies whether N = gate, switch, zone, stage, forge, or fleet. [pause: short] The protocol guarantees fidelity because it never assumes — it always stimulates and observes against the mathematical key (thermal-admittance model) and validates against the empirical lock (test data). [pause: short] If the model predicts the test, and the test corrects the model, the recursion converges. [pause: short] If it diverges, the protocol catches it at the next level. [pause: short] No scale is exempt. [pause: short] The gate is stimulated like the forge. [pause: short] The forge is validated like the gate. [pause: short] The operator participates at every authorization boundary. [pause: short] The machine mirrors itself at every electrical metrology tier. [pause: short] This is the recursive sequence that guarantees the Aegis-Forge I electrical system does not just meet code — it survives the storm. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- 1. [pause: short] Electrical Safety Architecture ---

--- 1.1 Design Philosophy ---

The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is governed by a single irreducible principle: no conductive path shall exist between the process zone (2200°C, 500 kW induction, Carrington-class GIC environment) and earth ground. [pause: short] This constraint forces the entire field layer — 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, 8 GaN inverter modules — to communicate and be powered through all-dielectric media: PMMA plastic optical fiber (POF) for signals, PEX-a tubing for coolant, BFRP housings for enclosures, ceramic bushings for penetrations. [pause: short] Three non-negotiable constraints define the architecture:

[Table row: ,  Constraint ,  Implementation ,  Verification , ]

[Table row: , ------------, ----------------, --------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Zero conductive penetration ,  PMMA POF only fieldbus (980 μm core), PEX-a coolant, BFRP enclosures, ZrO₂/Al₂O₃ bushings ,  Megger >10 GΩ at 500 VDC between process and earth , ]

[Table row: ,  Floating power distribution ,  Isolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A, no neutral-earth bond ,  Ground fault current <5 A under any single fault , ]

[Table row: ,  Carrington GIC immunity ,  5000 nT/s → <1 V induced on POF; ride-through mode (5 ms cap → 10 ms island → LiFePO₄) ,  Helmholtz coil test 100 A/m, no spurious trips , ]

Consequences of violation: A single copper wire crossing the pressure boundary becomes a GIC antenna. [pause: short] 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. [pause: short] At 50 m cable length: >5 V common-mode on a GaN gate driver (6 V threshold) = destruction. [pause: short] At 100 V common-mode on FBG interrogator = permanent damage. [pause: short] The all-dielectric architecture is not a preference — it is the only topology that survives. [pause: short] --- 1.2 Hierarchy Summary — Electrical Perspective ---

Utility Substation (Single Point)

       ├──► Cable Trays (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Enclosures (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)

       └──► Structure (BFRP frame, no steel)

--- Combined Heuristic Introduction — PROD-26 Electrical Safety & GIC Immunity ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is forced into its all-dielectric topology by a single irreducible principle: no copper conductor may cross the pressure boundary into the 2200°C induction zone during a Carrington-class geomagnetic storm (dB/dt = 5000 nT/s). [pause: short] This constraint is not a design preference — it is physics. [pause: short] A 5000 nT/s field induces >100 V/km on conductors. [pause: short] At 50 m cable run: >5 V common-mode. [pause: short] The GaN gate drivers (GS66516T, LMG1210) have 6 V threshold. [pause: short] A single ground loop couples kV from GIC into the gate drive — instant destruction. [pause: short] The FBG interrogators (VCSEL, InGaAs PIN) share the same vulnerability. [pause: short] The isolation transformer secondary is floating — no neutral-earth bond — because a grounded neutral provides the return path for GIC to enter the process electronics. [pause: short] The constraint cascades into every electrical decision:

[pause: short] All 480+ sensors on PMMA POF: FBG temperature/strain (384), POF level (16), pyrometer (8), mass spec (8), XRF (8), pressure (24), flow (32), vibration (16), encoder (2), E-stop (8) — zero copper

[pause: short] All 96+ actuators on PMMA POF: GaN gates (16), varactor bias (32), cap bank (48), MFC (32), port valves (8), carousel (1), flux (8), quench (16), drum drive (1), crane interlock (4)

[pause: short] Cooling water: PEX-a tubing (cross-linked PE, ρ>10¹⁴ Ω·m) — no copper pipe, no conductive path to building ground

[pause: short] Enclosures: BFRP/Elium® (ρ>10¹² Ω·m) — no steel cabinets, no metallic conduit

[pause: short] Penetrations: Al₂O₃/ZrO₂ ceramic bushings only — no metal feedthroughs

[pause: short] Power distribution: Isolation transformer (Δ-Y, floating secondary), NGR 5A — no ground reference on process side

What breaks if violated: A single copper wire for just the E-stop → GIC antenna → 5 V common-mode on GaN gate → GaN shoot-through → 500 kW inverter destruction → drum thermal runaway → vessel overpressure → catastrophic failure. [pause: short] The constraint is binary: all-dielectric or dead forge. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap this document closes is the measured divergence between standard industrial electrical safety (grounded, copper-wired, EMC-compliant) and the verified behavior of the Aegis-Forge I under combined Carrington GIC + 500 kW induction + 2200°C thermomechanical loading. [pause: short] Three specific gaps demand this architecture:

[pause: short] Standard grounding creates the GIC antenna: IEEE 142 / NFPA 70 require equipment grounding conductors. [pause: short] But in a 5000 nT/s event, the ground conductor is the antenna. [pause: short] The measured GIC on Hydro-Québec 1989 was 100 A on neutral conductors. [pause: short] A grounded forge would see 100 A flowing through its safety ground into the GaN gate drivers. [pause: short] The gap: grounding for safety vs. [pause: short] grounding as GIC antenna. [pause: short] [pause: short] Standard EMC assumes copper shielding: CISPR 11 / IEC 61000-4 assume metallic enclosures and shielded cables. [pause: short] But in the forge, a steel cabinet at 2200°C ambient (radiative coupling) with 500 kW of 1–100 kHz magnetic fields becomes a Faraday cage that concentrates eddy currents. [pause: short] The measured field inside PROD-03 coil housing is 39.6 mT at Z8. [pause: short] A steel enclosure would see 50 kW of eddy current heating. [pause: short] The gap: metallic shielding vs. [pause: short] dielectric transparency. [pause: short] [pause: short] Standard SIL-3 assumes independent channels: IEC 61508 2oo3 voting assumes physical separation. [pause: short] But in the forge, all 3 FBG sensors per zone share: same interrogator, same POF cable tray, same 24 VDC supply, same RTU. [pause: short] A single interrogator failure = common cause = all 3 channels lost. [pause: short] The gap: independent channels vs. [pause: short] shared infrastructure in constrained volume. [pause: short] Measured data demanding this approach:

[pause: short] PROD-23 GIC ride-through test: 100 A/m Helmholtz field, 30 min — zero spurious trips, zero data loss

[pause: short] PROD-10 EMC test: CISPR 11 Class A passed with 20 dB margin — no metal shielding

[pause: short] PROD-23 SIS proof test (CT-04): 24 SIL-3 SIFs, PFD<sub>avg</sub> = 2.3×10⁻³ — meets <10⁻²

[pause: short] PROD-25 megger test: All 50+ penetrations >1 GΩ at 500 VDC — no conductive leakage

[pause: short] PROD-10 arc flash calc: 0.3 cal/cm² at 18 (process) vs 4.2 cal/cm² (grid) — Cat 0 PPE

--- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I electrical safety is the divergence between IEC 61508 / NFPA 70E compliant design and the measured behavior of an all-dielectric control system inside a 500 kW induction furnace at 2200°C during a Carrington storm. [pause: short] Three specific locks prevent traditional electrical safety engineering from closing this gap:

[pause: short] Grounding is the vulnerability, not the protection: Every industrial standard (IEEE 142, NFPA 70, IEC 60364) mandates equipment grounding conductors for fault current return and shock protection. [pause: short] But in the forge, the ground conductor becomes the GIC antenna. [pause: short] 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. [pause: short] A 50 m ground wire = 5 V common-mode. [pause: short] The GaN gate driver threshold is 6 V. [pause: short] The safety ground destroys the safety system. [pause: short] The lock: safety ground as GIC antenna. [pause: short] [pause: short] EMC shielding requires conductivity — the forge forbids it: CISPR 11 / IEC 61000-4 assume metallic enclosures (steel, aluminum) for radiated emission containment and immunity. [pause: short] But at 2200°C with 500 kW of 1–100 kHz magnetic fields, a steel cabinet becomes an induction heater. [pause: short] The measured B-field at Z8 is 39.6 mT. [pause: short] Eddy current heating in 2 mm steel: P = π²B²f²d²V/6ρ ≈ 50 kW. [pause: short] The cabinet would melt. [pause: short] The lock: metallic shielding as induction heater. [pause: short] [pause: short] SIL-3 independence assumes no shared infrastructure: IEC 61508 2oo3 voting requires physical separation of sensors, logic solvers, and final elements. [pause: short] But the forge has: 3 FBG sensors sharing 1 interrogator, 3 RTUs sharing 1 TSN ring, 3 SIS FPGAs sharing 1 TSN VLAN, all powered from 1 DC bus. [pause: short] A single interrogator failure = common cause = all 3 channels lost. [pause: short] The lock: shared infrastructure as common cause failure. [pause: short] Common thread: Every lock is a standard safety practice that becomes a hazard in the forge's unique electromagnetic-thermal environment. [pause: short] The empirical lock is the sum of all safety practices that invert under Carrington + induction + temperature. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- The Mathematical Key ---

The single computational primitive that generates the electrical safety solution is the discrete-time thermal-admittance model executed at 1 kHz on the Zone RTU, which doubles as the GIC/SIF prediction engine:

[Equation: T_{inner}[k+1] = T_{inner}[k] + \frac{\Delta t}{\rho c V} \left( P_{ind}[k] - h A (T_{inner}[k] - T_{flange}[k]) - \epsilon \sigma A (T_{inner}^4[k] - T_{surr}^4) \right)]

Where:

[pause: short] ]T_{inner}[Inline equation:  = Drum inner surface temperature (virtual sensor, reconstructed from 48 FBG/zone)

[pause: short] ]P_{ind}[Inline equation:  = Induction power command (from thermal PID + feedforward)

[pause: short] ]h A[Inline equation:  = Convective conductance to flange (identified online)

[pause: short] ]\epsilon \sigma A[Inline equation:  = Radiative conductance (dominant >800°C, T⁴ nonlinearity)

--- 1. [pause: short] Electrical Safety Architecture ---

--- 1.1 Design Philosophy ---

The Aegis-Forge I electrical safety architecture is governed by a single irreducible principle: no conductive path shall exist between the process zone (2200°C, 500 kW induction, Carrington-class GIC environment) and earth ground. [pause: short] This constraint forces the entire field layer — 480+ sensors, 96+ actuators, 8 GaN inverter modules — to communicate and be powered through all-dielectric media: PMMA plastic optical fiber (POF) for signals, PEX-a tubing for coolant, BFRP housings for enclosures, ceramic bushings for penetrations. [pause: short] Three non-negotiable constraints define the architecture:

[Table row: ,  Constraint ,  Implementation ,  Verification , ]

Consequences of violation: A single copper wire crossing the pressure boundary becomes a GIC antenna. [pause: short] 5000 nT/s induces >100 V/km. [pause: short] At 50 m cable length: >5 V common-mode on a GaN gate driver (6 V threshold) = destruction. [pause: short] At 100 V common-mode on FBG interrogator = permanent damage. [pause: short] The all-dielectric architecture is not a preference — it is the only topology that survives. [pause: short] --- 1.2 Hierarchy Summary — Electrical Perspective ---

Every vessel/drum penetration uses ceramic-to-ceramic or ceramic-to-composite joints with no metal:

VESSEL FLANGE (PEEK CF40):
  ├─ 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts (ceramic paste, 160 N·m)
  ├─ ZrO₂ flat gasket (3 mm, graphite-loaded)
  ├─ 8× FBG feedthrough (Al₂O₃ bushing, ZrO₂ ferrule)
  ├─ 4× POF bulkhead (BFRP ferrule, ZrO₂ sleeve)
  ├─ 2× POF Level sensor (Al₂O₃ bushing)
  └─ 1× Pressure transducer (ZrO₂ bushing, welded)

DRUM BEARING HOUSING (BFRP):
  ├─ Si₃N₄ ceramic races (inner/outer)
  ├─ ZrO₂ ceramic balls (Ø12 mm, 16 per bearing)
  ├─ PEEK CF40 cage (carbon fiber reinforced)
  ├─ N₂ film lubrication (no oil, no metal)
  ├─ FBG strain feedthrough (Al₂O₃ bushing)
  └─ POF encoder (BFRP ferrule)

PORT VALVE PENETRATION (Drum wall):
  ├─ ZrB₂-SiC sleeve (press-fit 0.03 mm)
  ├─ ZrO₂ piston (3Y-TZP, hone 0.05 mm)
  ├─ Ti₃AlC₂ actuator (brazed Ag-CuO-TiO₂)
  ├─ PEEK CF40 wave spring (3 waves, 50 N)
  └─ 5 mm ZrO₂ felt insulation (actuator pocket)
[End code block]

GIC EVENT DETECTION (L3 SCADA + L2 PLC):
  Grid Monitor (dedicated) → dV/dt > 5 V/ms OR NGR current > 2 A
       │
       ▼
  RIDE-THROUGH INITIATION (<5 ms):
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. [pause: short] DC link capacitors sustain inverter power (100 ms hold)  │
  │ 2. [pause: short] Vacuum contactor opens (10 ms) → island from grid        │
  │ 3. [pause: short] LiFePO₄ backup (100 Wh/module) powers controls           │
  │ 4. [pause: short] All zones ramp to 20% power (thermal hold)               │
  │ 5. [pause: short] SIS remains active (dedicated FPGA + POF)                │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
  GIC EVENT DURATION (1–10 min):
  • Drum rotation maintained (piezo drive, battery)
  • Gas atmospheres maintained (MFC battery backup)
  • FBG/PTP/TSN fully operational (all-dielectric)
  • No data loss — historian buffers locally
       │
       ▼
  GRID RECOVERY (30 min stable):

[pause: short] Verify drum thermal state (no shock >100°C/s)

[pause: short] Verify SIF health (all 24 SIL-3 OK)

[End code block]

Common Cause Failure (β-factor) Analysis:

[pause: short] Sensor separation: 3 FBG/zone at 120° intervals → β < 0.01

[pause: short] Power: Dedicated isolated DC-DC per RTU → β < 0.005

[pause: short] Network: Dedicated TSN VLAN + time slice → β < 0.005

[pause: short] Software: Diversity (FPGA vs. [pause: short] ARM vs. [pause: short] PLC) → β < 0.01

[pause: short] Total β < 0.03 (well below 0.1 limit for SIL-3)

--- 9. [pause: short] Grounding & Bonding — IEEE Std 142 / IEEE Std 1100 ---

--- 9.1 Grounding Philosophy ---

Single-Point Ground at Substation Only. [pause: short] No ground reference anywhere in the process zone. [pause: short] All grounding inside the forge is equipotential bonding via 1 MΩ bleed resistors for static dissipation only. [pause: short] [Code block]
GROUNDING TOPOLOGY:
Utility Substation (Single Point)
       │
       ▼
Isolation Transformer (Δ-Y, Floating Secondary)
       │
       ▼
Neutral Grounding Resistor (5 A, 400 V) → Earth
       │
       ├──► Transformer Tank (BFRP, no metal)
       ├──► Cable Trays (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Enclosures (BFRP, 1 MΩ bleed)
       ├──► Cooling Water (PEX-a, DI water 18 MΩ·cm)
       └──► Structure (BFRP frame, no steel)
[End code block]

[pause: short] Charge Generation: Drum rotation (500 RPM), particle flow, gas flow

[pause: short] Maximum Potential: <100 V (verified by ESD test IEC 61000-4-2)

[pause: short] Spark Prevention: All ports have ZrO₂ piston with 0.05 mm clearance — no spark gap

FPGA/RTU/PLC BOOT SEQUENCE:

[pause: short] Stage 2 → Verify Application (Git tag hash, SHA256)

[pause: short] All stages → Measure into TPM 2.0 (PCR 0-7)

[pause: short] Remote Attestation → SCADA verifies PCR values at startup

  Single point at substation ONLY

  ML anomaly: FOLLOW-29 autoencoder on digital twin

KEY EQUATIONS:

  Ride-through: E_cap = ½CV² = 100 Wh/module
  Skin depth: δ = √(2ρ/ωμ)
  Arc flash: IE = k·E·t/D² (NFPA 70E)
  SIL: PFD = λ·TI/2 (per channel), 2oo3 = 3λ²TI²/2

--- PROD-27 Manufacturing Process Plan — Combined Heuristic Introduction ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The manufacturing plan is forced by a single irreducible constraint: the Aegis-Forge I contains zero structural metals in its hot zone — every component exposed to the 2200°C induction environment must be ceramic, composite, or dielectric. [pause: short] This is not a material preference; it is the physics of Carrington immunity. [pause: short] A single steel bolt in the drum assembly becomes a GIC antenna at 5000 nT/s, inducing >5 V common-mode on GaN gate drivers (6 V threshold) → shoot-through → 500 kW destruction → drum thermal runaway → catastrophic failure. [pause: short] This constraint cascades into every manufacturing decision:

[pause: short] Flash sintering is mandatory — no hot pressing achieves 600×800×35 mm monolithic ceramic; no pressureless sintering achieves 99.8% density with sub-micron grains

[pause: short] Filament winding is mandatory — no metal vessel, no autoclave (metal mandrel), no metallic tooling contact

[pause: short] Brazing is mandatory — no welding (metal), no mechanical fasteners in hot zone (CTE mismatch, stress concentration)

[pause: short] In-house synthesis is mandatory — commercial basalt fiber at [Inline equation: 14/kg vs. [pause: short] in-house at ]2/kg; commercial Elium® at [Inline equation: 18/kg vs. [pause: short] in-house at ]5/kg; the Forge must make its own materials to close the Phoenix Protocol loop

The constraint writes the entire 18-month critical path: three zero-float parallel streams (Drum, Vessel, Electronics) that cannot be accelerated because each step is the unique solution to a physics lock. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap this document closes is the fabrication fidelity gap between laboratory-scale ceramic/composite processes and production-scale manufacturing of a 226 L, 2200°C, Carrington-immune industrial machine. [pause: short] Three specific gaps demand this manufacturing architecture:

[pause: short] Scale gap: Lab flash sintering achieves 99.8% density at 50 mm scale. [pause: short] The Forge requires 600 mm diameter × 800 mm length × 35 mm wall — a 1000× volume increase. [pause: short] The key is vertical sintering with sacrificial support ring — gravity-assisted densification prevents barreling at scale. [pause: short] The graphite die (672 mm ID) with ZrO₂ fiber board support is the unique tooling that enables this. [pause: short] [pause: short] Integration gap: Eight independent subsystems (drum, vessel, 8 coil zones, 8 inverter modules, 8 port valves, carousel, frame, TSN network) must converge in Week 21 with zero float. [pause: short] The key is synchronization gates (SG-1 through SG-4) — each stream delivers a verified, tested assembly; integration never waits. [pause: short] The bolt ceremony (dual-verify 160 N·m on 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts) is the physical instantiation of this gate. [pause: short] [pause: short] Traceability gap: Phoenix Protocol requires every element tracked from mine to return. [pause: short] The key is QR-coded material certificates linked to Hyperledger Fabric — each drum, vessel, coil, module carries its birth record. [pause: short] The FAT data package (CT-01 through CT-10) is the genesis block for each Forge's digital twin. [pause: short] [pause: long]

This document makes the following non-negotiable commitments that constrain all downstream documents:

[pause: short] 18-month critical path is immutable — three zero-float paths (Drum 13 wk, Vessel 11 wk, Electronics 14 wk) converge at Integration Week 21. [pause: short] No schedule compression without physics violation. [pause: short] [pause: short] Flash sintering is the sole drum manufacturing route — PROD-28 QA validates the V/I flash signature; PROD-29 deployment installs the sinter furnace; PROD-30 maintenance includes graphite die replacement every 20 drums. [pause: short] [pause: short] Filament winding ±18°/90° layup is frozen — PROD-28 acceptance criteria lock fiber angle ±1°; PROD-30 spare vessel program uses same mandrel. --- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I manufacturing is the divergence between aerospace-grade ceramic/composite processes (low rate, high touch) and the production reality of an 18-month, 14-assembly, zero-metal industrial machine. [pause: short] Three specific locks prevent traditional manufacturing engineering from closing this gap:

[pause: short] Ceramic scale lock: Conventional ceramic manufacturing (hot pressing, HIP, pressureless sintering) maxes at ~200 mm. [pause: short] The Forge drum is 600 mm diameter. [pause: short] The lock: no existing ceramic process achieves production-scale monolithic UHTC components. [pause: short] [pause: short] Composite integration lock: Filament winding is mature for pressure vessels. [pause: short] But the Forge vessel requires: BFRP/Elium® (thermoplastic, no autoclave), 50 mm aerogel infusion gap, YInMn Blue glaze, PEEK CF40 flanges — all integrated on a 900 mm ID mandrel with 18 mm wall. [pause: short] The lock: no existing composite process integrates thermoplastic winding, aerogel infusion, ceramic glaze, and composite flanges in a single production flow. [pause: short] [pause: short] Dielectric assembly lock: Eight inverter modules, eight coil zones, 384 FBG sensors, dual-ring TSN, PTP grandmaster — all assembled with zero conductive fasteners, zero metallic conduit, zero ground references. [pause: short] The lock: no existing electronics assembly process operates under all-dielectric constraints at 500 kW. [pause: short] Common thread: Every lock is a standard manufacturing practice that inverts under the Forge's zero-metal, Carrington-immune, 2200°C constraints. [pause: short] The empirical lock is the sum of all manufacturing practices that become hazards or impossibilities in the Forge's unique electromagnetic-thermal environment. FOR each critical operation (flash sinter, winding, braze, module assembly, FBG splice):
    Prepare: Inputs certified (material certs, tool cal, operator qual)
    Execute: Run per work instruction, real-time sensor capture
    Verify: In-process data vs. [pause: short] physics model (V/I flash, laser angle, TIM bond, ZVS)
    Authorize: Operator logs event witnessed (flash, ZVS, braze flow)
    Feedback: Update tool life, material lot history, operator qual
[End code block]

Level 1 — Assembly Completion (Per Assembly):

[Code block]
FOR each assembly A_i in stream:
    Prepare: All operations complete, data collected
    Execute: Compile data package (CMM, UT, CT, functional, logs)
    Verify: Package vs. [pause: short] acceptance criteria (all predicates)
    Authorize: Mfg Eng + QA Eng dual-sign
    Feedback: NCRs → CAPA → work instruction update
[End code block]

Level 2 — Synchronization Gate (Per Stream):

[Code block]
FOR each gate SG_k (k=1..4):
    Prepare: All stream assemblies signed, integration fixture ready
    Execute: Gate review meeting (30 min max), walk physical hardware
    Verify: All SG_k predicates TRUE (complete ∧ verified ∧ data_package_signed)
    Authorize: Stream Lead + QA Lead sign gate release
    Feedback: Gate timing vs. [pause: short] baseline, float consumption, risk update
[End code block]

Level 3 — System Integration & FAT (Per Forge):

[Code block]
FOR integration + FAT:
    Prepare: All 3 streams at SG-4, integration checklist IC-1..IC-10
    Execute: 4-week integration per sequence, then 3-week FAT CT-01..CT-10
    Verify: All IC pass, all CT pass, data packages complete
    Authorize: Plant Mgr + Lead EE + Lead ME + Safety Eng sign FAT release
    Feedback: FAT duration, first-time yield, NCR trend → next Forge baseline
[End code block]

Level 4 — Fleet Production (Across Forges):

[Code block]
FOR each Forge n in production sequence:
    Prepare: Fleet baseline from Forges 1..n-1
    Execute: Run Levels 0-3 with baseline parameters
    Verify: Gate timing, FAT yield, NCR rate vs. [pause: short] fleet baseline
    Authorize: Continuous — twin auto-adjusts parameters within guard bands
    Feedback: Fleet baseline updated, parameter guards tightened, best practices deployed
[End code block]

--- The Recursive Guarantee ---

The protocol is recursive because the output of each level becomes the input validation for the next level:

[pause: short] Process verification (Level 0) → Assembly data package (Level 1)

[pause: short] Assembly package (Level 1) → Gate release (Level 2)

[pause: short] Gate release (Level 2) → Integration readiness (Level 3)

[pause: short] FAT release (Level 3) → Fleet baseline (Level 4)

[pause: short] Fleet baseline (Level 4) → Process parameters (Level 0)

This is the fractal pattern: Prepare→Execute→Verify→Authorize at scale N → Feedback to scale N-1 and N+1. [pause: short] The same logic applies whether N = flash event, assembly, gate, FAT, or fleet. [pause: short] The protocol guarantees fidelity because it never assumes — it always executes and verifies against the mathematical key (synchronization function) and authorizes through human participation. [pause: short] If the physics model predicts the verification, and the verification corrects the model, the recursion converges. [pause: short] If it diverges, the protocol catches it at the next gate. [pause: short] No scale is exempt. [pause: short] The flash event is verified like the fleet. [pause: short] The fleet is optimized like the flash event. [pause: short] The operator participates at every authorization boundary. [pause: short] The factory mirrors itself at every metrology tier. [pause: short] This is the recursive sequence that guarantees the Aegis-Forge I is not just manufactured — it is witnessed into existence. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- 2.5 Liner Zone Installation (A-02, A-03) ---

Zone A — Si₃N₄ (4 tiles, 200 mm arc × 250 mm):

[pause: short] Tiles sintered 1800°C/2h/N₂, diamond ground, pin holes drilled

[pause: short] 12 × ZrO₂ pins (Ø6×20 mm) inserted through tile/drum

[pause: short] Pins peened, heads laser-welded (ZrO₂ fiber laser)

Zone B — ZrB₂-SiC (6 tiles, 100 mm arc × 300 mm):

[pause: short] Tiles flash-sintered same as drum body (matched CTE)

[pause: short] 18 × ZrO₂ pins (Ø6×20 mm) through overlap joint with Zone C

[pause: short] Tiles matched to drum curvature ±0.1 mm

Zone C — 3Y-TZP (4 tiles, 200 mm arc × 250 mm):

[pause: short] Isostatic press 200 MPa, sinter 1500°C/4h, HIP 150 MPa/1400°C/2h

[pause: short] 12 × ZrO₂ pins (Ø8×25 mm) through overlap with Zone B

[pause: short] Larger pins for higher thermal loads

Installation sequence (vertical, feed-end up):

[pause: short] Zone C installed first (bottom): pins inserted, seated, peened

[pause: short] Zone B installed: overlap with Zone C aligned, pins through both

[pause: short] Zone A installed last (top): overlap with Zone B aligned, pins inserted

[pause: short] All pin heads laser-welded for positive retention

[pause: short] Final ID scan: roundness <25 μm, taper <10 μm over 800 mm

--- 3.2 Aerogel Infusion (A-07) ---

Aerogel specification: Polyimide-silica hybrid (PISi), λ = 0.010 W/m·K, ρ = 0.12 g/cm³, 50 mm radial gap. [pause: short] Infusion process:

[pause: short] Vessel placed on rotation fixture (2 RPM)

[pause: short] Aerogel slurry (PISi + IPA, 15% solids) pumped into annulus

[pause: short] Centrifugal casting at 10 RPM for 30 min — uniform radial distribution

[pause: short] IPA evaporation: 80°C/4h vacuum oven

[pause: short] Supercritical CO₂ drying: 120°C/100 bar/2h (prevents capillary stress)

[pause: short] Final density verification: gamma densitometer, 0.12 ±0.01 g/cm³

Mechanical standoffs (ZrO₂, 12× circumferentially):

[pause: short] 50 mm tall × 25 mm dia, spaced 300 mm axial

[pause: short] Prevent aerogel compression under thermal expansion

[pause: short] ZrO₂ chosen for CTE match to drum (10.5×10⁻⁶/K)

[pause: short] Plasma spray CoAl₂O₄: 100 μm, over YInMn

[pause: short] Seal coat: SiO₂ sol-gel, 25 μm, hydrophobic

[pause: short] Cure: 120°C/1h

Performance:

--- 5.2 Winding Process ---

[pause: short] BFRP housing layup: Filament wind on collapsible mandrel, [±30°/90°]₃, Elium®, 120°C cure

[pause: short] Conductor preparation: Cu tube annealed (400°C/1h), Al₂O₃ tape spiral wrapped (50% overlap)

[pause: short] Coolant tube: PEX-a coiled inside conductor, brazed connections (Ag-Cu)

[pause: short] Winding: CNC 4-axis winder, tension 30 N, layer insulation (Nomex 0.2 mm)

[pause: short] Vacuum impregnation: Elium® resin, -0.9 bar/30 min, 120°C/4h cure

[pause: short] FBG embed: 48 sensors/zone (384 total) in grooves between layers

[pause: short] Microchannel cold plate bond: In foil TIM (50 μm), 150°C/1 MPa/10 min

[Code block]
MODULE HOUSING (BFRP, 400×300×150 mm)
├─ GS66516T GaN HEMT ×2 (half-bridge)

├─ Varactor Array (32×, 0.5–30 pF, 30 V)

├─ TSN Switch Port (PMMA POF, 1 Gbps)
├─ FBG Interrogator Interface (POF)
├─ SIL-3 FPGA (Artix-7, dedicated)
└─ Microchannel Cold Plate (AlSiC, In foil TIM)

--- 8. [pause: short] System Integration & Loop Closure (A-13) ---

--- 8.1 Integration Sequence (4 Weeks) ---

Week 1 — Foundation & Frame:

[pause: short] Install elastomeric isolators on foundation (tiltmeter 0.1 μrad level)

[pause: short] Mount BFRP frame, torque PEEK CF40 bolts (dual-verify)

[pause: short] Install carousel rotor, bearing preload verification

[pause: short] Route PEX-a coolant mains, POF cable trays (BFRP)

Week 2 — Vessel & Drum Insertion:

[pause: short] Lower vessel onto frame (crane 10t, spreader bar, load cells)

[pause: short] Install aerogel gap standoffs (12× ZrO₂, verified gap 50 mm ±2 mm)

[pause: short] Insert drum into vessel (vertical, guided by alignment pins)

[pause: short] Verify drum-to-vessel concentricity: <0.5 mm radial runout

Week 3 — Flange Closure & Port Valves:

[pause: short] Install drum-end PEEK CF40 flanges (12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts, 160 N·m dual-verify)

[pause: short] Install port valve assemblies (×8) into drum sleeves

[pause: short] Connect actuator FBG leads to POF bulkheads

[pause: short] Install ZrO₂ gaskets, torque sequence (star pattern)

Week 4 — Coil Bank, Electronics, Loop Closure:

[pause: short] Install 8-zone coil bank around vessel (alignment pins, BFRP brackets)

[pause: short] Connect PEX-a coolant: zone → cold plate → manifold → chiller

[pause: short] Mount 8 power electronics modules on frame

[pause: short] Route POF: TSN ring (dual), PTP grandmaster, FBG interrogators

[pause: short] TSN ring closure: verify <100 μs latency, PTP <1 μs sync

[pause: short] FBG splices: all 384 channels verified (IL <0.5 dB)

[pause: short] SIL-3 SIS FPGA config load + self-test

--- Appendix D: FAT/SAT Test Procedures (CT-01 through CT-10) ---

--- D.1 CT-01 Drum Rotordynamics ---

Objective: Verify drum dynamic behavior matches FEA predictions (PROD-25). [pause: short] Setup: Drum mounted on integration fixture, drive motor + encoder, accelerometers (8×), proximity probes (4×), laser vibrometer. [pause: short] Procedure:

[pause: short] Install drum, verify runout <25 μm at 50 RPM

[pause: short] Accelerate 10 RPM/s to 500 RPM, record at each 50 RPM increment

[pause: short] Coast down, record critical speed crossings

[pause: short] Balance correction: add/remove mass at correction planes

[pause: short] Re-run to 500 RPM, verify G0.4 (ISO 21940-11)

[pause: short] Overspeed test: 600 RPM for 5 min (1.2× operating)

Pass Criteria:

[pause: short] 1st bending critical speed >1890 RPM (FEA: 2100 RPM)

[pause: short] Balance grade G0.4 at 500 RPM

[pause: short] Synchronous vibration <25 μm pk-pk

[pause: short] No subsynchronous instability

--- D.2 CT-02 Vessel Hydrotest ---

Objective: Verify pressure boundary integrity per ASME BPVC Sec X. [pause: short] Setup: Vessel on frame, N₂ supply 15 bar, pressure transducers (3×), He leak detector. [pause: short] Procedure:

[pause: short] Visual inspection: welds, bonds, flange faces

[pause: short] Pressurize to 5 bar, hold 10 min, inspect

[pause: short] Pressurize to 10 bar, hold 10 min, inspect

[pause: short] Pressurize to 15 bar (1.5× design), hold 30 min

[pause: short] Depressurize to 5 bar, He leak test all joints

[pause: short] Full depressurization, final visual

Pass Criteria:

[pause: short] Zero pressure drop at 15 bar/30 min (temp compensated)

[pause: short] Zero leaks at all joints (He <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s)

[pause: short] No permanent deformation (CMM pre/post)

--- D.3 CT-03 Flange Leak Test ---

Objective: Verify all 24 bolted joints (12 per flange) seal at design pressure. [pause: short] Procedure:

[pause: short] Pressurize vessel to 10 bar N₂

[pause: short] He sniffer probe at each bolt hole, gasket OD, flange face

[pause: short] Record leak rate per joint

[pause: short] Any leak >10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s → re-torque → re-test

Pass Criteria: All 24 joints <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s

--- D.4 CT-04 SIS Proof Test ---

Procedure per SIF: (See Section 9.2)

--- D.5 CT-05 Coil Resonance ---

Objective: Verify all 8 zones achieve ZVS at target frequency and power. [pause: short] Setup: Each zone connected to test inverter, water load, V/I probes, thermal camera. [pause: short] Procedure per zone:

[pause: short] Frequency sweep 50–100 kHz (Z1–Z2), 1–50 kHz (Z3–Z8)

[pause: short] Identify resonant peak, set operating point

[pause: short] Ramp power 0→100% in 10% steps, 5 min dwell

[pause: short] Record V/I phase, switch voltage, current, temperature

[pause: short] Verify ZVS: v_DS zero crossing before gate turn-on

Pass Criteria: ZVS phase <5° at 100% load all zones

--- D.6 CT-06 FBG Calibration ---

Objective: Calibrate all 384 FBG sensors against reference temperatures. [pause: short] Setup: Drum in furnace, 5 reference thermocouples (Type C) at known positions, FBG interrogator. [pause: short] Temperature points: 25°C, 500°C, 1000°C, 1500°C, 2000°C

Procedure:

[pause: short] Ramp furnace to each point, hold 30 min stabilization

[pause: short] Record all 384 FBG wavelengths + 5 reference TCs

[pause: short] Compute calibration coefficients per sensor

[pause: short] Verify linearity R² >0.999, drift <0.5%/1000 hrs

Pass Criteria: All 384 sensors calibrated, drift <0.5%/1000 hrs

--- D.7 CT-07 GIC Ride-Through ---

Setup: Helmholtz coil (100 A/m, 5000 nT/s), full system operational. [pause: short] Procedure:

[pause: short] Start 6-batch sequence (CT-10)

[pause: short] At Batch 3 midpoint, energize Helmholtz to 100 A/m

[pause: short] Maintain 30 min, monitor all systems

[pause: short] De-energize, verify 30 min stable grid

[pause: short] Operator authorizes continued operation

Pass Criteria: Zero spurious SIF trips, zero data loss, all comms intact

--- D.8 CT-08 Thermal Cycle ---

Objective: Full thermal cascade (Stages 0-8) without feedstock. [pause: short] Procedure:

[pause: short] Execute Stage 0: AMLS 20 min, verify LI >0.8

[pause: short] Execute Stage 1: IR drying to 150°C, verify moisture <0.1%

[pause: short] Execute Stages 2-8 per thermal profile (PROD-02)

[pause: short] Hold each stage 30 min, record all FBG, power, gas

[pause: short] Cool down per controlled ramp (50°C/min max)

Pass Criteria: All stages ±5°C of setpoint, no SIF trips, no anomalies

--- D.9 CT-09 Seismic Shake ---

Setup: Shake table, IEEE 693 High RRS, 3 axes. [pause: short] Procedure:

[pause: short] Mount integrated system on shake table (isolators installed)

[pause: short] 5 OBE events (0.4g ZPA), inspect between

[pause: short] 1 SSE event (1.0g ZPA), inspect

[pause: short] Post-shake: CT-01, CT-02, CT-03, CT-04 re-run

Pass Criteria: HCLPF >1.6g, no structural damage, all re-tests pass

--- D.10 CT-10 Integrated Hot Run ---

See Section 9.3 for 6-batch protocol. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- PROD-27 Manufacturing Process Plan — Combined Heuristic Introduction ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The manufacturing plan is forced by a single irreducible constraint: the Aegis-Forge I contains zero structural metals in its hot zone — every component exposed to the 2200°C induction environment must be ceramic, composite, or dielectric. [pause: short] This is not a material preference; it is the physics of Carrington immunity. [pause: short] A single steel bolt in the drum assembly becomes a GIC antenna at 5000 nT/s, inducing >5 V common-mode on GaN gate drivers (6 V threshold) → shoot-through → 500 kW destruction → drum thermal runaway → catastrophic failure. [pause: short] This constraint cascades into every manufacturing decision:

[pause: short] Flash sintering is mandatory — no hot pressing achieves 600×800×35 mm monolithic ceramic; no pressureless sintering achieves 99.8% density with sub-micron grains

[pause: short] Filament winding is mandatory — no metal vessel, no autoclave (metal mandrel), no metallic tooling contact

[pause: short] Brazing is mandatory — no welding (metal), no mechanical fasteners in hot zone (CTE mismatch, stress concentration)

[pause: short] In-house synthesis is mandatory — commercial basalt fiber at [Inline equation: 14/kg vs. [pause: short] in-house at ]2/kg; commercial Elium® at [Inline equation: 18/kg vs. [pause: short] in-house at ]5/kg; the Forge must make its own materials to close the Phoenix Protocol loop

The constraint writes the entire 18-month critical path: three zero-float parallel streams (Drum, Vessel, Electronics) that cannot be accelerated because each step is the unique solution to a physics lock. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap this document closes is the fabrication fidelity gap between laboratory-scale ceramic/composite processes and production-scale manufacturing of a 226 L, 2200°C, Carrington-immune industrial machine. [pause: short] Three specific gaps demand this manufacturing architecture:

[pause: short] Scale gap: Lab flash sintering achieves 99.8% density at 50 mm scale. [pause: short] The Forge requires 600 mm diameter × 800 mm length × 35 mm wall — a 1000× volume increase. [pause: short] The key is vertical sintering with sacrificial support ring — gravity-assisted densification prevents barreling at scale. [pause: short] The graphite die (672 mm ID) with ZrO₂ fiber board support is the unique tooling that enables this. [pause: short] [pause: short] Integration gap: Eight independent subsystems (drum, vessel, 8 coil zones, 8 inverter modules, 8 port valves, carousel, frame, TSN network) must converge in Week 21 with zero float. [pause: short] The key is synchronization gates (SG-1 through SG-4) — each stream delivers a verified, tested assembly; integration never waits. [pause: short] The bolt ceremony (dual-verify 160 N·m on 12× M24 ZrO₂ bolts) is the physical instantiation of this gate. [pause: short] [pause: short] Traceability gap: Phoenix Protocol requires every element tracked from mine to return. [pause: short] The key is QR-coded material certificates linked to Hyperledger Fabric — each drum, vessel, coil, module carries its birth record. [pause: short] The FAT data package (CT-01 through CT-10) is the genesis block for each Forge's digital twin. [pause: short] [pause: long]

This document makes the following non-negotiable commitments that constrain all downstream documents:

[pause: short] 18-month critical path is immutable — three zero-float paths (Drum 13 wk, Vessel 11 wk, Electronics 14 wk) converge at Integration Week 21. --- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap in Aegis-Forge I manufacturing is the divergence between aerospace-grade ceramic/composite processes (low rate, high touch) and the production reality of an 18-month, 14-assembly, zero-metal industrial machine. [pause: short] Three specific locks prevent traditional manufacturing engineering from closing this gap:

[pause: short] Ceramic scale lock: Conventional ceramic manufacturing (hot pressing, HIP, pressureless sintering) maxes at ~200 mm. [pause: short] The Forge drum is 600 mm diameter. [pause: short] The lock: no existing ceramic process achieves production-scale monolithic UHTC components. [pause: short] [pause: short] Composite integration lock: Filament winding is mature for pressure vessels. [pause: short] But the Forge vessel requires: BFRP/Elium® (thermoplastic, no autoclave), 50 mm aerogel infusion gap, YInMn Blue glaze, PEEK CF40 flanges — all integrated on a 900 mm ID mandrel with 18 mm wall. [pause: short] The lock: no existing composite process integrates thermoplastic winding, aerogel infusion, ceramic glaze, and composite flanges in a single production flow. [pause: short] [pause: short] Dielectric assembly lock: Eight inverter modules, eight coil zones, 384 FBG sensors, dual-ring TSN, PTP grandmaster — all assembled with zero conductive fasteners, zero metallic conduit, zero ground references. [pause: short] The lock: no existing electronics assembly process operates under all-dielectric constraints at 500 kW. [pause: short] Common thread: Every lock is a standard manufacturing practice that inverts under the Forge's zero-metal, Carrington-immune, 2200°C constraints. [pause: short] The empirical lock is the sum of all manufacturing practices that become hazards or impossibilities in the Forge's unique electromagnetic-thermal environment. [pause: short] [pause: long]

 November 2026# Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-28 Quality Assurance & Testing

--- Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The irreducible principle forcing this QA architecture is zero-metal construction under SIL-3 Carrington immunity — a conjunction that eliminates every conventional quality method relying on conductive paths, magnetic particle inspection, eddy current on ferromagnetic substrates, or electrical continuity testing. [pause: short] The Forge operates at 2200°C in a 100 A/m GIC field with 384 FBG channels embedded in ZrB₂-SiC and BFRP; any QA method introducing metal (MQ probes, UT couplant residues, conductive epoxy, grounding straps) creates a GIC antenna that violates PROD-26 dielectric requirements. [pause: short] The Lock: quality assurance must itself be dielectric, non-magnetic, and thermally survivable to 2200°C. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap is the absence of any precedent for qualifying a zero-metal pressure vessel at 2200°C with embedded photonics. [pause: short] ASME BPVC Sec VIII/X covers composites to 300°C; ASTM E2700 UT assumes metallic wave speeds; IEC 61508 SIL-3 proof testing assumes electrical trip paths. [pause: short] Our validation data (PROD-24 V&V, PROD-25 FEA, PROD-27 FA) shows: UT phased array on ZrB₂-SiC requires 5 MHz 64-element PA at 45°/60°/70° wedges (longitudinal wave speed 11,200 m/s vs steel 5,900); CT at 200μm voxel resolves FBG position ±100μm but adds 8 hr/drum; AE continuous monitoring on BFRP detects delamination at Felicity ratio <1.0 but requires 8-channel R15α at 100 kHz–1 MHz. [pause: short] The Key: a multi-method NDT program where each method's physics is re-derived for zero-metal substrates, calibrated against flash-sinter and filament-wind process signatures, not material certificates. [pause: short] --- Commitment (The Turn) ---

This document commits the Forge to three non-negotiable verification chains:

[pause: short] FBG-as-primary-metrology: All 384 channels survive flash sinter (PROD-04 PQR-FS-001), filament winding (PROD-06 PQR-FW-001), and 500 thermal cycles (CT-06) with drift <0.5%/1000 hrs. [pause: short] No backup thermocouples — they are metal. [pause: short] FBG interrogation at 125 Hz continuous is the only in-process temperature/strain verification. [pause: short] [pause: short] SIL-3 SIF proof test per CT-04 is the gate: All 24 SIFs (3 per module × 8 zones) must trip <50 ms on TSN VLAN 10 with 2oo3 agreement. [pause: short] PFD_avg <1×10⁻³. [pause: short] This test runs before hot commissioning (CT-08) and after any design change (ECO). [pause: short] No SIL-3 SIF = no Forge shipment. [pause: short] [pause: short] QR + Hyperledger traceability is the quality record: Every drum, vessel, port valve, coil, module carries a QR code linking to immutable blockchain record (material lot, process params, NDT results, FAT data). [pause: short] Paper travelers are supplementary. [pause: short] The digital twin (PROD-37) ingests this chain at 10 Hz; any gap triggers automatic NCR. [pause: short] These commitments cascade: PROD-29 commissioning inherits CT-04/CT-06/CT-08 pass data; PROD-30 PM schedules inherit NDT intervals; PROD-31 economics inherits scrap/rework rates from NCR log; PROD-32 permitting inherits audit evidence. [pause: short] The Turn: quality is not a phase — it is the continuous witnessing of the Forge's own fabrication fidelity, recorded in light through glass fiber, verified by proof test, anchored in blockchain. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap is dimensional stability of ZrB₂-SiC at 2200°C with embedded FBGs through 500 thermal cycles — a regime where no NDT standard exists. [pause: short] Flash sintering (PROD-04) produces drums at 99.8% density but with residual stress gradients: ID compressive 120 MPa, OD tensile 80 MPa (FEA PROD-25). [pause: short] During thermal ramp (50°C/min to 2200°C), CTE mismatch (ZrB₂ 7.5, SiC 4.5, FBG silica 0.55 ×10⁻⁶/K) generates shear at FBG/matrix interface. [pause: short] Accelerated testing (PROD-27 FA) shows: 3% FBG channels fail by cycle 200 (debond); UT phased array detects debond as 15% amplitude drop at 5 MHz but cannot size <0.2 mm; CT at 200 μm voxel sees debond >0.5 mm but misses sub-voxel. [pause: short] The Lock: no single NDT method closes the gap between theoretical FBG survival (100%) and empirical (97% at 500 cycles) — the gap is the debond nucleation zone below UT resolution and CT voxel. --- El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence ---

--- Mirror (Self-Reflection) ---

The fabricator observes their own fabrication through three recursive sensor loops that close at the speed of the process:

[pause: short] Flash Sinter V/I Mirror (100 kHz DAQ): During the 5-minute dwell at 1720°C, the flash sinter power supply records voltage/current at 100 kHz. [pause: short] The resistivity drop (1000×) is the primary witness of sinter completion — not the thermocouple (metal, forbidden). [pause: short] The V/I signature shape (dV/dt inflection, I plateau) maps to density via PROD-04 calibrated curve: ρ_final = f(∫I dt, V_min, t_dwell). [pause: short] This mirror runs inside the furnace; the operator sees the curve on HMI but the decision (dwell complete / extend / abort) is automated by PROD-23 SIS logic comparing live V/I to PQR-FS-001 envelope. [pause: short] The fabricator watches the process witness itself. [pause: short] [pause: short] Filament Winding Dielectric Cure Mirror (10 kHz): The Elium® resin cure is monitored by in-mold dielectric sensors (interdigitated capacitive electrodes on mandrel, non-conductive). [pause: short] Permittivity ε' and loss ε'' track degree of cure α(t) via PROD-06 kinetic model: dα/dt = A exp(-Ea/RT) α^m (1-α)^n. [pause: short] The mirror outputs α(t) in real time; winding pauses if α deviates >2% from trajectory. [pause: short] No post-cure DSC needed — the cure witnesses its own completion through the resin's own electrical response. [pause: short] [pause: short] FBG Interrogation Mirror (125 Hz continuous): All 384 FBG channels (128 drum, 48×8 coils, 16 port valves, 16 vessel, 16 frame) stream wavelength at 125 Hz to PROD-37 digital twin. --- 8.2 CAPA Process (8D) ---

[Table row: ,  Step ,  Action ,  Owner ,  Timing , ]

[Table row: , ---, ---, ---, ---, ]

[Table row: ,  D1: Team ,  Form cross-functional team (Mfg, QA, Design, Supplier) ,  Quality Eng ,  24 hr , ]

[Table row: ,  D2: Describe ,  5W2H: What, Where, When, Who, Why, How, How many ,  Team ,  48 hr , ]

[Table row: ,  D3: Contain ,  Interim containment (quarantine, sort, retrofit) ,  Mfg Eng ,  Immediate , ]

[Table row: ,  D4: Root Cause ,  5 Whys → Fishbone → Fault tree; verify with data ,  Team ,  5 days , ]

[Table row: ,  D5: Corrective ,  Permanent fix (design, process, material, training) ,  Design/Mfg Eng ,  15 days , ]

[Table row: ,  D6: Verify ,  Pilot run / test / inspection proving fix works ,  Quality Eng ,  20 days , ]

[Table row: ,  D7: Prevent ,  Update work instructions, PFMEA, control plan, training ,  Quality Eng ,  30 days , ]

[Table row: ,  D8: Close ,  Team recognition; lessons learned to fleet twin ,  Plant Manager ,  30 days , ]

--- Appendix B: NDT Procedure Index ---

--- B.1 UT Phased Array — Drum/Vessel (PROD-28-UT-001) ---

Scope: 100% volumetric inspection of drum wall, vessel wall, flange weld/bond zones. [pause: short] Equipment: Olympus OmniScan MX2, 5MHz 64-element probe, wedge 45°/60°/70°. [pause: short] Calibration: IIW block (ref), DAC curve 80% FSH, TCG normalization. [pause: short] Scan Pattern: Raster 2mm × 2mm; encoder-coupled; 100% coverage. [pause: short] Acceptance: No indications >0.5mm flat / 2mm Ø; signal-to-noise >6dB. [pause: short] Reporting: C-scan image + A-scan at each indication; depth/sizing per ASME Sec V. [pause: short] --- B.2 CT High-Resolution — Drum (PROD-28-CT-001) ---

Scope: Drum body (FBG channels, porosity, grain structure). [pause: short] Equipment: Nikon XTH 225/320, 225kV/320kV, 200μm voxel. [pause: short] Calibration: NIST-traceable density standards; geometric phantom. [pause: short] Reconstruction: Feldkamp algorithm; beam hardening correction. [pause: short] Analysis: Porosity distribution (volume %, size, sphericity); FBG channel position ±100μm. [pause: short] Acceptance: Open porosity <0.05%; closed <0.2%; FBG position per design. [pause: short] --- B.3 ET — Port Valve Sleeves (PROD-28-ET-001) ---

Scope: ZrB₂-SiC port sleeves (surface + near-surface). [pause: short] Equipment: Rohmann Elotest M6, 100kHz-2MHz, differential probe. [pause: short] Calibration: ASME Sec V notch standards (EDM notches 0.1/0.2/0.5mm). [pause: short] Scan: Rotating probe, 360° coverage, 0.5mm axial step. [pause: short] Acceptance: No signals >20% DAC at 0.2mm notch equivalent. [pause: short] --- B.4 AE — Vessel Continuous (PROD-28-AE-001) ---

Scope: BFRP vessel continuous monitoring (pressure + thermal cycles). [pause: short] Equipment: Physical Acoustics PCI-2, 8 channels, 40dB preamp, 100kHz-1MHz. [pause: short] Sensors: 8× R15α (broadband) at 45° increments, 2 axial positions. [pause: short] Threshold: 40dB AE; hit definition: peak > threshold, duration >50μs. [pause: short] Analysis: Source location (ΔT triangulation ±50mm); b-value; RA-value; Felicity ratio. [pause: short] Alert: Hit rate >2× baseline (30-day rolling); Felicity <1.0; cluster >10 hits/hr. [pause: short] Reporting: Daily summary + anomaly alerts; monthly trend report. [pause: short] --- B.5 IR Thermography — System (PROD-28-IR-001) ---

Scope: Frame, vessel exterior, coil bank, power electronics, coolant manifolds. [pause: short] Equipment: FLIR T1040, 1024×768, <20mK NETD, 24° lens. [pause: short] Calibration: Blackbody 35°C/200°C; emissivity per material table (BFRP 0.95, ZrB₂ 0.85). [pause: short] Frequency: Monthly + post-CT-08 + post-seismic. [pause: short] Analysis: ΔT vs. [pause: short] baseline; hotspot detection; thermal gradient mapping. [pause: short] Alert: Any point >5°C above baseline; new hotspot; gradient >50°C/100mm. --- Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-28 Quality Assurance & Testing ---

--- Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The irreducible principle forcing this QA architecture is zero-metal construction under SIL-3 Carrington immunity — a conjunction that eliminates every conventional quality method relying on conductive paths, magnetic particle inspection, eddy current on ferromagnetic substrates, or electrical continuity testing. [pause: short] The Forge operates at 2200°C in a 100 A/m GIC field with 384 FBG channels embedded in ZrB₂-SiC and BFRP; any QA method introducing metal (MQ probes, UT couplant residues, conductive epoxy, grounding straps) creates a GIC antenna that violates PROD-26 dielectric requirements. [pause: short] The Lock: quality assurance must itself be dielectric, non-magnetic, and thermally survivable to 2200°C. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap is the absence of any precedent for qualifying a zero-metal pressure vessel at 2200°C with embedded photonics. [pause: short] ASME BPVC Sec VIII/X covers composites to 300°C; ASTM E2700 UT assumes metallic wave speeds; IEC 61508 SIL-3 proof testing assumes electrical trip paths. [pause: short] Our validation data (PROD-24 V&V, PROD-25 FEA, PROD-27 FA) shows: UT phased array on ZrB₂-SiC requires 5 MHz 64-element PA at 45°/60°/70° wedges (longitudinal wave speed 11,200 m/s vs steel 5,900); CT at 200μm voxel resolves FBG position ±100μm but adds 8 hr/drum; AE continuous monitoring on BFRP detects delamination at Felicity ratio <1.0 but requires 8-channel R15α at 100 kHz–1 MHz. [pause: short] The Key: a multi-method NDT program where each method's physics is re-derived for zero-metal substrates, calibrated against flash-sinter and filament-wind process signatures, not material certificates. [pause: short] --- Commitment (The Turn) ---

This document commits the Forge to three non-negotiable verification chains:

[pause: short] FBG-as-primary-metrology: All 384 channels survive flash sinter (PROD-04 PQR-FS-001), filament winding (PROD-06 PQR-FW-001), and 500 thermal cycles (CT-06) with drift <0.5%/1000 hrs. [pause: short] No backup thermocouples — they are metal. [pause: short] FBG interrogation at 125 Hz continuous is the only in-process temperature/strain verification. [pause: short] [pause: short] SIL-3 SIF proof test per CT-04 is the gate: All 24 SIFs (3 per module × 8 zones) must trip <50 ms on TSN VLAN 10 with 2oo3 agreement. [pause: short] PFD_avg <1×10⁻³. [pause: short] This test runs before hot commissioning (CT-08) and after any design change (ECO). [pause: short] No SIL-3 SIF = no Forge shipment. [pause: short] [pause: short] QR + Hyperledger traceability is the quality record: Every drum, vessel, port valve, coil, module carries a QR code linking to immutable blockchain record (material lot, process params, NDT results, FAT data). [pause: short] Paper travelers are supplementary. [pause: short] The digital twin (PROD-37) ingests this chain at 10 Hz; any gap triggers automatic NCR. [pause: short] These commitments cascade: PROD-29 commissioning inherits CT-04/CT-06/CT-08 pass data; PROD-30 PM schedules inherit NDT intervals; PROD-31 economics inherits scrap/rework rates from NCR log; PROD-32 permitting inherits audit evidence. [pause: short] The Turn: quality is not a phase — it is the continuous witnessing of the Forge's own fabrication fidelity, recorded in light through glass fiber, verified by proof test, anchored in blockchain. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap is dimensional stability of ZrB₂-SiC at 2200°C with embedded FBGs through 500 thermal cycles — a regime where no NDT standard exists. [pause: short] Flash sintering (PROD-04) produces drums at 99.8% density but with residual stress gradients: ID compressive 120 MPa, OD tensile 80 MPa (FEA PROD-25). [pause: short] During thermal ramp (50°C/min to 2200°C), CTE mismatch (ZrB₂ 7.5, SiC 4.5, FBG silica 0.55 ×10⁻⁶/K) generates shear at FBG/matrix interface. [pause: short] Accelerated testing (PROD-27 FA) shows: 3% FBG channels fail by cycle 200 (debond); UT phased array detects debond as 15% amplitude drop at 5 MHz but cannot size <0.2 mm; CT at 200 μm voxel sees debond >0.5 mm but misses sub-voxel. [pause: short] The Lock: no single NDT method closes the gap between theoretical FBG survival (100%) and empirical (97% at 500 cycles) — the gap is the debond nucleation zone below UT resolution and CT voxel. The single computational primitive is the recursive Bayesian update of component health state using multi-source likelihood fusion:

--- El Segundo Heuristic — Operational Excellence ---

--- Mirror (Self-Reflection) ---

The fabricator observes their own fabrication through three recursive sensor loops that close at the speed of the process:

[pause: short] Flash Sinter V/I Mirror (100 kHz DAQ): During the 5-minute dwell at 1720°C, the flash sinter power supply records voltage/current at 100 kHz. [pause: short] The resistivity drop (1000×) is the primary witness of sinter completion — not the thermocouple (metal, forbidden). [pause: short] The V/I signature shape (dV/dt inflection, I plateau) maps to density via PROD-04 calibrated curve: ρ_final = f(∫I dt, V_min, t_dwell). [pause: short] This mirror runs inside the furnace; the operator sees the curve on HMI but the decision (dwell complete / extend / abort) is automated by PROD-23 SIS logic comparing live V/I to PQR-FS-001 envelope. [pause: short] The fabricator watches the process witness itself. [pause: short] [pause: short] Filament Winding Dielectric Cure Mirror (10 kHz): The Elium® resin cure is monitored by in-mold dielectric sensors (interdigitated capacitive electrodes on mandrel, non-conductive). [pause: short] Permittivity ε' and loss ε'' track degree of cure α(t) via PROD-06 kinetic model: dα/dt = A exp(-Ea/RT) α^m (1-α)^n. [pause: short] The mirror outputs α(t) in real time; winding pauses if α deviates >2% from trajectory. [pause: short] No post-cure DSC needed — the cure witnesses its own completion through the resin's own electrical response. [pause: short] [pause: short] FBG Interrogation Mirror (125 Hz continuous): All 384 FBG channels (128 drum, 48×8 coils, 16 port valves, 16 vessel, 16 frame) stream wavelength at 125 Hz to PROD-37 digital twin. [pause: short] The twin runs the Bayesian health update (Keymaker Key) on the same data the process generates. [pause: short] The mirror is not a separate inspection — it is the process's own nervous system reporting to itself. [pause: short] Anomaly (Λ > 10) triggers automatic NCR before the operator acknowledges it. [pause: short] The Mirror: quality assurance is not applied to the product — it is the product's own sensorium, reflected back to the process in real time. [pause: short] --- Participation (Witness) ---

The inside operator witnesses the phenomenon at four non-automatable gates where human judgment closes the loop that sensors cannot:

[pause: short] Gate SG-2 (Flange Torque Ceremony): 24 bolts, 160 N·m ±5 N·m, dual-verify (two operators, independent torque wrenches, acoustic emission monitoring). --- 6.2 SOP-002: Batch Execution (Core Procedure) ---

[Code block]
PHASE 1: FEED PREPARATION (0-15 min)
├── 1.1 Scan feedstock QR → verify Category A-D (PROD-13)
├── 1.2 Load shredder → verify <150 mm, ferrous removed (PROD-11)
├── 1.3 Confirm drum empty (Carousel position 1, FBG + encoder)
└── 1.4 Operator confirms recipe match → BATCH <ID> RECIPE CONFIRMED

PHASE 2: CASCADE EXECUTION (15-105 min)
├── 2.1 Stage 0-1: Acoustic + Drying (auto, FBG/PID controlled)
├── 2.2 Stage 2: Polymer melt + centrifuge (auto, CFDO-CB operator)
├── 2.3 Stage 3: Pyrolysis + char (auto, CDO-SG operator)
├── 2.4 Stage 4: Indium-First (auto, Port 4A/B/C thermal actuation)
├── 2.5 Stage 5: Aluminum window (auto, Port 5 at 680°C)
├── 2.6 Stage 6: Copper + PM (auto, anode carousel, XRF verify)
├── 2.7 Stage 7: Ferrous + REE (auto, dual-port Port 7A/7)
├── 2.8 Stage 8: Mineral/Zr (auto, ZrSiO₄ dissociation, 3Y-TZP flash)

PHASE 3: SLUG POUR & DATA CAPTURE (105-115 min)
├── 3.1 Carousel positions molds → N₂ quench → mass spec spot check
├── 3.2 Each slug: LIBS scan → QR stamp → weight → mass spec → vault
├── 3.3 Batch mass balance calculated → digital twin sync
├── 3.4 Operator reviews batch record → BATCH <ID> COMPLETE
└── 3.5 Data package auto-signed → Hyperledger commit

PHASE 4: INTER-BATCH RESET (115-120 min)
├── 4.1 Drum rotation to Position 1 (empty)
├── 4.2 Gas purge (N₂ 200 Nm³/hr × 5 min)
├── 4.3 SIF status verify → READY FOR NEXT BATCH
└── 4.4 Shift handover log entry (if shift change)
[End code block]
