--- Combined Heuristic Intro — PROD-29 Deployment & Operations ---

--- Williams + Keymaker + El Segundo Synthesis ---

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The irreducible principle forcing this deployment architecture is the Forge must re-verify its own fabrication fidelity at the site before any feedstock enters — the synchronization function (PROD-27 Keymaker Key) does not end at the factory gate. [pause: short] The 14 assemblies arrive with verified data packages (QR + Hyperledger), but the act of transport, rigging, and re-assembly introduces new variables: foundation settlement, utility impedance, ground resistance, seismic coupling, and thermal boundary conditions that cannot be replicated in the factory. [pause: short] The Lock: deployment is not installation — it is the re-execution of the synchronization function at the site, with the site as a new variable in the verification predicate. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap is the measured divergence between factory FAT performance and site SAT performance for zero-metal, Carrington-immune machines. [pause: short] PROD-27 FAT (CT-01..CT-10) validates the Forge in a controlled electromagnetic environment (shielded factory, stable grid, characterized foundation). [pause: short] At site: grid impedance varies ±30%, ground resistance varies 2-50 Ω, seismic coupling depends on soil class, thermal boundary conditions change with weather. [pause: short] PROD-26 GIC ride-through test (CT-07) used a 100 A/m Helmholtz coil — but the real grid during a Carrington event presents common-mode impedance, not differential field. [pause: short] The Key: deployment must measure and compensate for site variables by re-executing the verification chain (IC-1..IC-10 → CT-08 → SAT-01..SAT-05) with site-specific acceptance criteria, not factory criteria. [pause: short] --- Commitment (The Turn) ---

This document commits the Forge to four non-negotiable deployment chains:

[pause: short] IC-1..IC-10 re-execution is mandatory — The 10 integration checkpoints from PROD-27 are not repeated — they are re-evaluated with site-specific criteria (e.g., IC-1 ground resistance <5 Ω vs factory <1 Ω; IC-4 PTP sync <1 μs vs factory <0.5 μs). [pause: short] No feedstock until all 10 PASS with site data packages signed. [pause: short] [pause: short] Hot commissioning (CT-08) is the thermal proof — 8-stage thermal ramp with no feedstock, full FBG/SIS/CEMS monitoring. [pause: short] The Forge must demonstrate thermal stability at 2200°C under site utility conditions. [pause: short] CT-08 data package is the site birth certificate. [pause: short] [pause: short] SAT-05 six-batch validation is the performance gate — Six batches (A, B, C, D, A, Phoenix) with mass balance >99.5%, all outputs spec, twin sync <1 s. [pause: short] This is not a test — it is the Forge proving it can execute its purpose at this site. [pause: short] [pause: short] SOP-002 batch execution is the operational invariant — The 4-phase batch procedure (feed prep → cascade → slug pour → reset) is the only authorized operating mode. [pause: short] No manual overrides, no recipe deviations without ECO (PROD-38). [pause: short] The operations philosophy is: the Forge runs the synchronization function at 90-min intervals; operators authorize, automation executes. [pause: short] These commitments cascade: PROD-30 PM schedules inherit IC re-verification intervals; PROD-31 OPEX model inherits energy/ton from SAT-05; PROD-32 permitting inherits CEMS/IC-7 data; PROD-34 training inherits SOP-002 as the core competency. [pause: short] The Turn: deployment is the Forge witnessing its own birth at the site — the same mathematical key (synchronization function) that governed manufacturing now governs commissioning, and the same operator witness gates (bolt ceremony, SIF proof, slug pour) that certified manufacturing now certify operations. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap is the site-specific variables that invalidate factory verification — a Forge that passes CT-01..CT-10 in the factory may fail SAT-01..SAT-05 at site due to variables that cannot be simulated in the factory. [pause: short] Three specific locks:

[pause: short] Ground impedance as deployment variable: Factory ground grid <1 Ω (controlled); site ground resistance 2-50 Ω (soil dependent). [pause: short] PROD-26 NGR 5A design assumes factory ground. [pause: short] At 50 Ω site ground, GIC return path impedance increases 50×, altering common-mode voltage distribution across the floating secondary. [pause: short] The Lock: factory-verified GIC immunity does not guarantee site GIC immunity. [pause: short] [pause: short] Seismic-soil coupling as deployment variable: PROD-25 FEA assumed fixed-base + isolators (3 Hz). [pause: short] Site soil class (NEHRP A-E) shifts fundamental frequency ±40%, changes isolator effectiveness, alters HCLPF. [pause: short] A Forge on Class E soil (soft clay) has 1st mode at 1.8 Hz vs 3 Hz design — seismic demand doubles. [pause: short] The Lock: factory seismic qualification (shake table) does not cover site-specific soil-structure interaction. [pause: short] [pause: short] Utility power quality as deployment variable: Factory grid: THD <3%, voltage regulation ±2%, fault level 50 kA. [pause: short] Site grid: THD up to 8% (per IEEE 519), voltage regulation ±5%, fault level 10-100 kA. [pause: short] PROD-10 inverter ZVS acquisition and PTP sync assume factory power quality. [pause: short] At site, voltage sags cause DC link droop; harmonic distortion causes TSN jitter. [pause: short] The Lock: factory power electronics verification does not cover site power quality envelope. [pause: short] --- The Mathematical Key ---

The single computational primitive is the site-adaptive synchronization function — the same fractal gate logic from PROD-27, now parameterized by site-measured variables:

[Equation: SG_{site} = \bigwedge_{i=1}^{10} \left( IC_i(site\_params) \land IC_i.verified \land IC_i.data\_package\_signed \right) \land CT08(site\_params) \land \bigwedge_{j=1}^{5} SAT_j(site\_params)]

Where [Inline equation: site\_params = \{R_{ground}, Z_{grid}, Soil_{class}, T_{ambient}, P_{water}, Q_{gas}\}] are measured at site during cold commissioning and fed into the verification predicates. [pause: short] The atomic computation is the predicate evaluation with site parameters:

[Equation: IC_1(site) \equiv (ground\_resistance < 5\Omega) \land (anchor\_torque = 1200\pm50 Nm) \land (frame\_level < 0.1mm/m)]

[Equation: IC_4(site) \equiv (TSN\_latency < 100\mu s) \land (PTP\_offset < 1\mu s) \land (SIF\_trip < 50ms) \land (GIC\_ride\_through @ site\_impedance)]

[Equation: CT08(site) \equiv \forall stages:

 < 2^\circ C \land SIF\_availability = 100\%]

[Equation: SAT_5(site) \equiv \frac{\sum m_{out}}{\sum m_{in}} > 0.995 \land \forall elements: recovery > target \land twin\_latency < 1s]

The Key executes at three scales:

[pause: short] Cold (IC-1..IC-10): Site parameters measured → predicates evaluated → gates signed

[pause: short] Hot (CT-08): Site thermal boundary conditions → thermal model re-identified → ramp/hold verified

[pause: short] The Turn: *the mathematical key is not the synchronization function alone — it is the synchronization function plus the site parameter measurement protocol that feeds it. --- Mirror (Self-Reflection) ---

The fabricator observes their own deployment through three nested metrology loops that close at the speed of the site:

[pause: short] Cold Commissioning Mirror (IC-1..IC-10, real-time): Each integration checkpoint is a self-measurement. [pause: short] IC-1 measures ground resistance and compares to the synchronization function predicate — if [Inline equation: R_{ground} > 5\Omega], the predicate is FALSE and the gate does not pass. [pause: short] The ME Lead does not inspect the ground grid — the ground grid measures itself via fall-of-potential and the synchronization function evaluates. [pause: short] [pause: short] Hot Commissioning Mirror (CT-08, 24-hour thermal): The thermal model (PROD-24 V&V) runs in parallel with the physical Forge at 1 kHz on the Zone RTUs. [pause: short] The model predicts [Inline equation: T_{inner}] from FBG flange measurements; the residual [Inline equation: (T_{FBG} - T_{model})] is the mirror's error signal. [pause: short] If residual >2°C RMS at any zone, the model re-identifies its parameters (convective conductance [Inline equation: hA], radiative conductance [Inline equation: \epsilon\sigma A]) in real-time. [pause: short] The mirror is the fleet twin reflecting the single Forge's performance back to it as operating constraints. [pause: short] The Mirror: deployment is not verified by external inspection — the Forge verifies itself at the site through the same synchronization function that governed its manufacturing, now parameterized by site measurements. [pause: short] --- Protocol (Recursive) ---

The recursive fidelity sequence is fractal gate protocol — the same Prepare→Execute→Verify→Authorize→Feedback pattern repeats at every scale, from IC-1 to fleet sustainment:

--- 2. [pause: short] Drum Maintenance (Assembly A-01/A-03) ---

--- 2.1 Drum Body (ZrB₂-SiC) — Detailed Procedures ---

--- 2.1.1 Annual UT Phased Array Volumetric Inspection (PROD-30-WI-001) ---

Scope: 100% volumetric inspection of drum wall (35 mm thickness, 600 mm ID, 800 mm length)
Equipment: Olympus OmniScan MX2, 5 MHz 64-element PA probe, wedges 45°/60°/70° (shear wave), 0° (longitudinal)
Calibration: IIW Type 1 block (ref), DAC curve 80% FSH, TCG normalization per ASTM E2700
Scan Pattern: Helical raster 2 mm × 2 mm; encoder-coupled; 100% coverage; 360° × 800 mm
Personnel: ASNT Level II UT (minimum), Level III review for indications
Duration: 8 hours (setup 2 hr, scan 4 hr, analysis 2 hr)

Acceptance Criteria:

[pause: short] No indications >0.5 mm flat equivalent (DAC 20%)

[pause: short] No indications >2 mm Ø equivalent (DAC 20%)

[pause: short] No planar indications in liner pin heat-affected zones (HAZ)

[pause: short] Signal-to-noise >6 dB on all scans

[pause: short] Liner-to-drum bond line: no unbonded areas >5 mm dia

Reporting: C-scan images (amplitude + depth), A-scan at each indication, depth/sizing per ASME Sec V Appendix IV, comparison to baseline (FA data package)

--- 2.1.2 Biennial CT High-Resolution (PROD-30-WI-002) ---

Scope: Full drum body including FBG channels, porosity distribution, grain structure
Equipment: Nikon XTH 320, 320 kV, 200 μm voxel, 1000 mm detector
Calibration: NIST-traceable density standards (Al, Ti, ZrO₂); geometric phantom (wire grid)
Reconstruction: Feldkamp algorithm; beam hardening correction; ring artifact reduction
Analysis: Porosity distribution (volume %, size, sphericity per ASTM E2921); FBG channel position ±100 μm; grain size distribution (EBSD correlation)
Personnel: ASNT Level II CT (minimum), Level III approval
Duration: 8 hours (setup 1 hr, scan 5 hr, reconstruction 2 hr)

Acceptance Criteria:

[pause: short] Open porosity <0.05% (Archimedes cross-check)

[pause: short] Closed porosity <0.2% volume; max pore size <0.5 mm

[pause: short] FBG channel position per design drawing ±100 μm

[pause: short] No new porosity clusters vs. [pause: short] baseline (FA CT)

[pause: short] Interrogator: Micron Optics si425 (125 Hz, 4 ch/module × 96 modules)

[pause: short] Channels: 128 drum (16 per zone × 8 zones) + 16 reference

[pause: short] No porosity clusters >3 pores in 25 mm²

[pause: short] No fiber breakage indications (Tsai-Wu FI <0.25)

[pause: short] Flange transition: no indications >5 mm

--- 3.1.3 Hydrotest (5-Year Interval, PROD-30-WI-009) ---

Procedure: Per ASME BPVC Section X, Article 8

[pause: short] Test pressure: 15 bar N₂ (1.5× design pressure 10 bar)

[pause: short] Hold time: 30 minutes minimum

[pause: short] Temperature compensation: ±0.5°C monitoring

[pause: short] Leak test: Helium mass spectrometer, sniff test all joints

[pause: short] Acceptance: Zero pressure drop (temp compensated); He leak <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s

Post-Hydrotest: AE baseline re-establishment (24 hr monitoring at 10 bar)

--- 3.1.4 Monthly Visual Inspection (VT-1, PROD-30-WI-010) ---

Scope: External surface (glaze), flange faces, bolt heads, port penetrations, anchor points
Criteria:

[pause: short] YInMn Blue glaze: No cracking, spalling, discoloration >5% area

[pause: short] Flange faces: No PEEK CF40 creep >0.5 mm; bolt head contact uniform

[pause: short] Anchor bolts: No corrosion, torque marks intact, isolation pads intact

[pause: short] Aerogel: No settlement gaps >2 mm at vessel/frame interface

--- 3.1.5 Monthly IR Thermography (PROD-30-WI-011) ---

Equipment: FLIR T1040, 1024×768, <20 mK NETD, 24° lens
Conditions: Forge at steady-state Stage 8 (2200°C drum), 500 kW total power
Analysis: ΔT vs. [pause: short] baseline (commissioning IR map); hotspot detection; thermal gradient mapping
Alert Thresholds:

[pause: short] Any point >5°C above baseline → Alert Level 1

[pause: short] New hotspot not in baseline → Alert Level 2

[pause: short] Thermal gradient >50°C/100 mm → Alert Level 2

--- 3.1.6 Annual Aerogel Density Verification (PROD-30-WI-012) ---

Equipment: Gamma densitometer (Cs-137, 5 mm collimated beam)
Scan Pattern: Radial profiles at 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°; 5 mm step; 3 axial stations
Acceptance: 0.12±0.01 g/cm³ uniform radial (no gradient >0.02 g/cm³ over 50 mm)
Action if Failed: Vacuum-assisted re-infusion (PROD-27 Sec 3 correction)

--- 3.1.7 Biennial Glaze Adhesion Pull-Off (PROD-30-WI-013) ---

Standard: ASTM D4541 (10% sample = 24 dollies on 900 mm ID vessel)
Acceptance: >10 MPa; failure mode cohesive in adhesive (not glaze)
Action if Failed: Localized glaze repair (plasma spray touch-up) or full re-spray

[pause: long]

--- 4. [pause: short] Port Valve Maintenance (Assembly A-04 ×8) ---

--- 4.1 Quarterly Thermal Actuation Check (PROD-30-WI-014) ---

Conditions: Furnace at 680°C ΔT (ambient to 700°C), 50°C/min ramp
Measurement: LVDT on piston rod (0.01 mm resolution) + FBG strain on actuator body
Acceptance: 3.6±0.2 mm deflection; repeatable 3 consecutive cycles; no hysteresis >0.1 mm
Data Capture: Force-deflection curve; thermal strain vs. [pause: short] temperature; FBG wavelength shift

--- 4.2 Quarterly Leak Rate Test (PROD-30-WI-015) ---

Conditions: Valve closed, 5 bar N₂ upstream, He mass spectrometer downstream
Acceptance: <10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s (equivalent to <1 sccm He)
Action if Failed: Braze joint UT inspection; piston/sleeve dimension check; seal replacement

--- 4.3 Annual Braze Joint UT (PROD-30-WI-016) ---

Scope: Ti₃AlC₂ actuator to ZrB₂-SiC sleeve (Ag-CuO-TiO₂ braze, 50±10 μm)
Equipment: 20 MHz focused UT, water coupling (dielectric)
Acceptance: No voids >50 μm; joint thickness 50±10 μm; TiO₂ reaction layer <5 μm
Reference: PROD-27 PQR-BR-001 baseline

--- 4.4 Annual FBG Strain Calibration (PROD-30-WI-017) ---

Method: Known weights on piston (0, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 N)
Acceptance: 0.1 nm/με ±2% linearity; R² > 0.999; hysteresis <1%
Cross-check: LVDT displacement vs. [pause: short] FBG strain (thermal actuation)

--- 4.5 500-Batch ZrO₂ Piston Inspection (PROD-30-WI-018) ---

Scope: Visual + dimensional (CMM) + surface profilometry
Acceptance: Clearance 0.05±0.01 mm; no wear >0.02 mm; Ra <0.4 μm; no radial cracking
Action if Failed: Replace piston + sleeve as matched set (PROD-09)

--- 4.6 2000-Cycle Actuator Replacement (PROD-30-WI-019) ---

Life Limit: 2000 thermal cycles (250 days at 8 batches/day)
Procedure: Full port valve assembly removal → new actuator/piston install → actuation check + leak test + FBG cal
Note: Actuator includes Ti₃AlC₂ body, ZrO₂ piston, PEEK CF40 spring, FBG embed

[pause: long]

--- 5. [pause: short] Coil Bank Maintenance (Assembly A-09 ×8 zones) ---

--- 5.1 Monthly Resonance & ZVS Verification (PROD-30-WI-020) ---

Per Zone Procedure:

[pause: short] Impedance analyzer sweep (1 kHz–200 kHz): resonant frequency, Q factor

[pause: short] Power analyzer: ZVS verification at 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% load

[pause: short] Thermal: IR camera at 100% load (30 min soak)

[pause: short] Data: Frequency vs. [pause: short] zone table ±1%; Q >150; ZVS phase <5°

Zone-Specific Targets:

[Table row: ,  Zone ,  Stage ,  Target Freq ,  Power Range ,  Q Target , ]

[Table row: , ---, ---, ---, ---, ---, ]

[Table row: ,  Z1 ,  1 (Drying) ,  100 kHz ±1% ,  0–50 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z2 ,  2 (Polymer) ,  100 kHz ±1% ,  0–50 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z3 ,  3 (Pyrolysis) ,  50 kHz ±1% ,  50–80 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z4 ,  4 (Low-Temp) ,  10 kHz ±1% ,  80–150 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z5 ,  5 (Al) ,  10 kHz ±1% ,  80–150 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z6 ,  6 (Cu/PM) ,  5 kHz ±1% ,  100–200 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z7 ,  7 (Fe) ,  2 kHz ±1% ,  150–350 kW ,  >150 , ]

[Table row: ,  Z8 ,  8 (Mineral) ,  1 kHz ±1% ,  200–500 kW ,  >150 , ]

--- 5.2 Monthly FBG Cross-Talk Check (PROD-30-WI-021) ---

Method: Interrogator single-channel excitation + adjacent channel monitoring
Acceptance: Adjacent channel isolation >40 dB; WDM channel spacing 0.8 nm maintained
Action if Failed: FBG re-splice (PROD-30-WI-003) or channel remapping

--- 5.3 Quarterly Cold Plate Leak Test (PROD-30-WI-022) ---

Method: He mass spectrometer, 10 bar He, 30 min hold per zone
Acceptance: <10⁻⁹ mbar·L/s (PROD-28 Sec 3.4)
Action if Failed: Cold plate removal → TIM (In foil) inspection → re-bond or replace

--- 5.4 Annual PEX-a Integrity (PROD-30-WI-023) ---

Method: Pressure decay test @ 10 bar, 1 hour
Acceptance: <0.1 bar/hr pressure drop
Visual: No kinking, abrasion, UV degradation, fitting corrosion

--- 5.5 Biennial Inductor Visual + CT (PROD-30-WI-024) ---

Visual: Cu tube insulation (Al₂O₃ coating), support spacers (BFRP), connections
CT: 50 μm voxel, focus on conductor insulation, braze joints, support integrity
Acceptance: No insulation cracking; no conductor displacement >0.5 mm; no braze voids >100 μm

[pause: long]

--- 6. [pause: short] Power Electronics Maintenance (Assembly A-10 ×8 modules) ---

--- 6.1 Monthly DC Link & ZVS Verification (PROD-30-WI-025) ---

DC Link Charge Test:

[pause: short] Oscilloscope capture (100 MHz BW, 1 GS/s): 0→800V in 500 ms; no overshoot >850V

[pause: short] Pre-charge resistor thermal check (IR): <80°C after charge

ZVS Acquisition Verification:

[pause: short] V/I ramp from 10% to 100% load in 10% steps

[pause: short] Phase <5° at all points; v_DS zero-crossing before gate drive

[pause: short] Gate drive voltage: 6V ±0.2V (LMG1210), rise/fall <2 ns

--- 6.2 Quarterly Thermal Soak Test (PROD-30-WI-026) ---

Conditions: 500 kW continuous, 30 minutes, cooling at design flow (500 L/min, 30°C inlet)
Measurements:

[pause: short] GaN junction temperature (calculated from T_c + R_θJC × P_loss): <125°C

[pause: short] Cold plate ΔT (inlet-outlet): <15°C

[pause: short] Capacitor bank temperature: <85°C (electrolytic), <105°C (film)

[pause: short] Thermal imaging: No hotspots >5°C above zone average

--- 6.3 Quarterly GIC Ride-Through Test (PROD-30-WI-027) ---

Equipment: Portable Helmholtz coil (1 m diameter, 100 A/m, 0.1–10 Hz sweep)
Procedure: Per PROD-26 Sec 3.3, PROD-23 CT-07 protocol
Acceptance: Zero spurious SIF trips; zero data loss (TSN/PTP/FBG); zero inverter trips
Monitoring: All 384 FBG channels, TSN latency, PTP offset, DC link voltage

--- 6.4 Annual EMI Verification (PROD-30-WI-028) ---

Standard: CISPR 11 Class A (conducted 150 kHz–30 MHz, radiated 30 MHz–1 GHz)
Conditions: All 8 zones at 100% load, Forge at Stage 8 steady-state
Acceptance: >20 dB margin on all limits
Action if Failed: Common-mode choke re-tune; POF routing check; filter capacitor ESR check

--- 6.5 Quarterly SIL-3 SIF Injection Test (PROD-30-WI-029) ---

Per Module (3 SIFs/module × 8 modules = 24 SIFs):

[pause: short] Overpressure (vessel >11 bar)

[pause: short] Overtemperature (drum >2250°C or dT/dt >100°C/s)

[pause: short] Vibration (frame >1.5g RMS)

[pause: short] GIC (common-mode >5 V on floating secondary)

[pause: short] Loss of comms (TSN VLAN 10 heartbeat >10 ms)

Acceptance: Trip <50 ms; 2oo3 channel agreement; SOE timestamp <1 ms skew; FBG data freeze at trip
Documentation: SIF test report per module; PFD_avg calculation update

--- 6.6 Monthly POF Attenuation Check (PROD-30-WI-030) ---

Equipment: OTDR (1550 nm, 10 μs pulse, 100 km range)
Acceptance: <0.2 dB/m; splices <0.5 dB; return loss >50 dB
Action if Failed: Re-splice affected segments (PROD-30-WI-003); OTDR trace archive

--- 6.7 Annual Capacitor Bank ESR Check (PROD-30-WI-031) ---

Equipment: Impedance analyzer (100 Hz–1 MHz)
Acceptance: ESR <1.5× initial (factory baseline); capacitance ±5% of nominal
Trend: ESR vs. [pause: short] time (exponential fit); predict end-of-life at 2× initial

--- 6.8 GaN Module Replacement (50,000 hrs, PROD-30-WI-032) ---

Hot-Swap Capability: Module rack designed for live removal (TSN/PTP/POF disconnect <30 s)
Procedure:

[pause: short] Zone power reduction to 0% (PID ramp 10%/s)

[pause: short] TSN VLAN 10 graceful disconnect (PTP holdover 24 hr)

[pause: short] POF disconnect (BFRP connector, push-pull)

[pause: short] Cold plate quick-disconnect (PEX-a, zero-leak)

[pause: short] Module extract (BFRP handles, 2-person lift 800 kg)

[pause: short] New module install → reverse sequence → acceptance per PROD-28 Sec 2.5

[pause: long]

--- 7. [pause: short] Frame, Carousel & Bearings (Assembly A-12) ---

--- 7.1 Annual Frame Dimensions (PROD-30-WI-033) ---

Equipment: CMM (Hexagon Global, 3000×2000×1500 mm, ±2 μm accuracy)
Points: 200+ measurement points (bolt holes, lifting lugs, isolator mounts, bearing seats)
Acceptance: ±1 mm length, ±0.5 mm diagonal, bolt hole pattern ±0.1 mm
Comparison: Baseline (FA CMM report) + thermal growth model (PROD-25)

--- 7.2 Biennial Isolator Stiffness Test (PROD-30-WI-034) ---

Method: Static load test (hydraulic jack, 500 kN capacity) + LVDT displacement
Vertical: 2.5 MN/m ±5% (250 kN → 0.1 mm deflection)
Horizontal: 0.8 MN/m ±5% (80 kN → 0.1 mm deflection)
Damping: Logarithmic decrement from free decay >15%
Acceptance: Per PROD-25 Sec 4.2 updated values

--- 7.3 Monthly Carousel Indexing (PROD-30-WI-035) ---

Method: Encoder (Heidenhain ROC 425, 26-bit) + FBG strain on bearing housing
Procedure: 8-position sequence (45° steps), 5 cycles each direction
Acceptance: <2 s per index; 0.01° resolution; position repeatability ±0.005°; vibration <0.5 g RMS

--- 7.4 Continuous Bearing Vibration Monitoring (PROD-30-WI-036) ---

Sensors: 4× accelerometers (PCB 352C33, 100 mV/g, 0.5–10 kHz) + 2× FBG on bearing housing
Sampling: 1 kHz continuous; FFT (0.5–500 Hz); envelope analysis (1–5 kHz)
Baseline: Commissioning data (30 days steady operation)
Alert Logic:

[pause: short] Overall RMS >2× baseline → Alert Level 1 (trend)

[pause: short] Bearing defect frequency (BPFI/BPFO/BSF/FTF) amplitude >6 dB baseline → Alert Level 2 (NCR)

[pause: short] Spectral kurtosis >4 → Alert Level 3 (immediate inspection)

--- 7.5 2000-Batch Bearing Inspection (PROD-30-WI-037) ---

Scope: Si₃N₄ ball / ZrO₂ race hybrid ceramic bearings (4 per carousel)
Procedure: Removal → visual + dimensional (CMM) + spin test (1000 RPM, 30 min)
Acceptance:

[pause: short] No spalling, pitting, discoloration on balls/races

[pause: short] Runout <5 μm (radial + axial)

[pause: short] Preload torque: 5 N·m ±10% (N₂ film 0.1 bar)

[pause: short] Vibration at 1000 RPM: <0.5 g RMS

[pause: short] FBG strain on housing: <50 με static

--- 7.6 Quarterly Mold Dimensions (PROD-30-WI-038) ---

Scope: 8× ZrO₂ molds (carousel positions 1-8)
Equipment: CMM (per 7.1) + optical comparator (profile)
Acceptance: 0.1 mm tolerance (ISO 8062 CT7); wall thickness 25±0.1 mm; base flatness <0.05 mm
Action if Failed: Mold replacement (spare set on-site); dimension mapping to slug quality data

--- 11.3 Detailed Predictive Algorithm Specifications ---

--- 11.3.1 FBG Drift Bayesian Tracker (PROD-28 Sec 5.1 Keymaker Key) ---

Mathematical Foundation: Recursive Bayesian update on Weibull degradation parameter β

[Code block]

--- Pseudocode for FBG drift tracker (executes at 125 Hz per channel) ---

def fbg_drift_update(channel_id, lambda_measured, t):
    # Prior: beta ~ Gamma(alpha, beta)  -- shape/rate from commissioning
    # Likelihood: lambda = lambda_0  exp(beta  t) + noise
    # Posterior: conjugate update
    
    alpha_post = alpha_prior + 0.5
    beta_post = beta_prior + 0.5  (lambda_measured - lambda_predicted)^2 / sigma^2
    
    # Hazard rate h(t) = beta / eta  (t/eta)^(beta-1)
    # Likelihood ratio Lambda = h(t
[Table row: , data) / h(t, ]
baseline)
    
    Lambda = compute_likelihood_ratio(alpha_post, beta_post, alpha_baseline, beta_baseline)
    
    if Lambda > 10:
        trigger_ncr(channel_id, FBG_DRIFT, Lambda, t)
    elif Lambda > 5:
        trigger_alert(channel_id, FBG_DRIFT_WARN, Lambda, t)
    
    return alpha_post, beta_post, Lambda
[End code block]

Channel-Specific Baselines (PQR-FS-001):

[pause: short] Drum zones 1-8 (16 ch/zone): λ₀ = 1550.000 nm @ 25°C; sensitivity = 10.2 pm/°C ±0.3 pm/°C

[pause: short] Vessel AE channels (8 ch): λ₀ = 1545.000 nm; sensitivity = 10.0 pm/°C ±0.2 pm/°C

[pause: short] Port valve actuators (8 ch × 2 = 16 ch): λ₀ = 1555.000 nm; sensitivity = 1.8 pm/με ±0.1 pm/με

[pause: short] Coil bank cold plates (8 ch): λ₀ = 1560.000 nm; sensitivity = 10.5 pm/°C ±0.4 pm/°C

[pause: short] Reference channels (16 ch): λ₀ = various; used for common-mode rejection

Data Compression: 125 Hz raw → 1 Hz min/mean/max/σ stored (99.2% compression); 10-year retention on PROD-37 time-series DB

--- 11.3.2 AE Felicity Ratio Change-Point Detection ---

Algorithm: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) + Binary Segmentation Change-Point

[Code block]
Felicity_ratio(t) = cumulative_energy(t) / cumulative_energy(t - Δt)
  where Δt = 1 hour rolling window

EWMA: z_t = λ  F_t + (1-λ)  z_{t-1}, λ = 0.1
Control limits: LCL = μ_0 - 2.7σ√(λ/(2-λ)), UCL = μ_0 + 2.7σ√(λ/(2-λ))
  μ_0 = 1.2 (baseline from PROD-25 FEA), σ = 0.05 (commissioning)

Change-point: Binary segmentation on z_t sequence (min segment = 24 hrs)
  Test statistic: max 
[Table row: , z_t - z_{t-1}, ]
 > 3σ
  If detected: re-baseline μ_0, σ from new segment; trigger NCR if Felicity < 1.0
[End code block]

Auto-Response Integration:

[pause: short] Alert Level 1 (Felicity 1.05–1.1): Log only, increase AE sampling to 1 MHz

[pause: short] Alert Level 2 (Felicity 1.0–1.05 > 1 hr): Auto-NCR, schedule UT inspection within 72 hrs

[pause: short] Alert Level 3 (Felicity < 1.0 > 1 hr): Auto-NCR + immediate partial shutdown (drum power <50%)

--- 11.3.3 Vibration Spectral Kurtosis + Envelope Analysis ---

Algorithm (ISO 13373-2 / PROD-28 Sec 5.2):

[pause: short] Raw acceleration: 1 kHz sampling, 4 ch per bearing housing (2 axial, 2 radial)

[pause: short] Demodulation: Hilbert transform of bandpass (1–5 kHz) → envelope signal

[pause: short] Spectral Kurtosis (SK): SK(f) = E[X⁴]/E[X²]² - 2 (Gaussian = 0)

[pause: short] Optimal band: max SK(f) over 1–5 kHz → band for envelope spectrum

[pause: short] Bearing defect frequencies (Si₃N₄/ZrO₂, 60 mm PD, 8 balls, 15° contact):

[pause: short] BPFI = 4.4 × RPM; BPFO = 3.6 × RPM; BSF = 2.3 × RPM; FTF = 0.45 × RPM

[pause: short] Alert: BPFI/BPFO/BSF amplitude > 6 dB baseline → NCR

Baseline Re-Establishment: Every 500 batches (drum swap) or after bearing replacement

--- 11.3.4 Thermal Model Residual RLS Adaptive Filter ---

Algorithm (Recursive Least Squares - PROD-24/28 fusion):

[Code block]
State: θ_t = [k_cond, k_conv, k_rad]^T  (thermal conductance parameters)
Measurement: y_t = T_actual - T_predicted (per zone, 1 kHz RTU)
Update: P_t = (I - K_t H) P_{t-1}; θ_t = θ_{t-1} + K_t (y_t - H θ_{t-1})
        K_t = P_{t-1} H^T (H P_{t-1} H^T + R)^{-1}
Alert: 
[Table row: , , y_t, , ]
_RMS > 2°C over 10 min window → NCR + cold plate leak check
[End code block]

Zone-Specific Parameters:

[pause: short] Zones 1-2 (100 kHz): k_cond dominates (conduction through drum wall)

[pause: short] Zones 3-4 (50/10 kHz): k_conv + k_rad (gas convection + radiation)

[pause: short] Zones 5-8 (10-1 kHz): k_rad dominates (2200°C radiation)

--- 11.3.5 POF Attenuation Linear Regression with Breakpoint Detection ---

Algorithm:

[pause: short] Continuous OTDR: 1550 nm, 10 μs pulse, 1 Hz sweep (all 384 channels)

[pause: short] Per-channel: α(t) = -10/L  log10(P_received/P_launch) dB/m

[pause: short] Rolling linear regression (30-day window): α(t) = a + bt

[pause: short] Breakpoint: CUSUM on residuals > 5σ → step change (splice failure, macrobend)

[pause: short] Alert: b > 0.001 dB/m/day OR step > 0.1 dB → NCR

--- 12.4 Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Integration ---

Trigger: Any NCR Critical (PROD-28 Sec 4) or Alert Level 3 (Sec 11)
Method: 8D with physics-based fault tree (PROD-25/26/28 fusion)

--- 12.4.1 RCA Process Flow ---

[Code block]
D0: Team Formation (QA Lead + SME: ME/EE/SIS/NDT/Metrology)
D1: Problem Statement (What, Where, When, Extent, IS/IS NOT)
D2: Interim Containment (Forge status: run/reduced/stop; safety first)
D3: Root Cause Identification

[pause: short] Fault Tree Top Event: e.g., FBG channel dropout Zone 3

[pause: short] Gates: AND/OR logic from PROD-25 FEA + PROD-26 GIC + PROD-28 NCR history

[pause: short] Basic Events: FBG fiber fracture, interrogator failure, splice degradation, 
      thermal gradient > design, GIC event, vibration fatigue, installation error

[pause: short] Quantification: Bayesian network (PROD-37) with prior from Weibull (PROD-25)
D4: Permanent Corrective Action (design fix / procedure change / interval change)
D5: Verification (pilot implementation + 30-day monitoring)
D6: Implementation (ECO via PROD-38; training update via PROD-34)
D7: Prevention (lessons learned; PM/CBM interval update; spare part spec change)
D8: Team Recognition & Closure (Hyperledger commit + PROD-37 twin update)
[End code block]

--- 12.4.2 Example Fault Tree: Drum FBG Channel Dropout ---

[Code block]
TOP: Channel dropout Zone 3 (1 of 16 channels)
├── Fiber fracture (AND)
│   ├── Thermal stress > 200 MPa (OR)
│   │   ├── dT/dt > 150°C/s (SIF would trip)
│   │   ├── Cold plate leak → local quench (AE detect)
│   │   └── Coil resonance shift → hotspot (ZVS monitor)
│   └── Mechanical fatigue (OR)
│       ├── Vibration > 2g RMS (bearing failure)
│       ├── Drum distortion > 0.5 mm (CT detect)
│       └── Installation bend radius < 25 mm
├── Splice degradation (AND)
│   ├── Thermal cycling fatigue (500 cycles = design life)
│   ├── Moisture ingress (dielectric breach → GIC path)
│   └── FBG coating delamination (H₂ at 2200°C)
├── Interrogator failure (OR)
│   ├── Laser diode degradation (MTBF 50,000 hrs)
│   ├── FPGA bit flip (GIC-induced, rate <10⁻⁹/hr)
│   └── Power supply failure (redundant 2+1)
└── Common-mode GIC event (AND)
    ├── Geomagnetic storm > 5 V/km (Carrington-class)
    ├── Floating secondary compromise (insulation failure)
    └── Faraday cage breach (conduit penetration)
[End code block]

Mᵢ = Material consumption rate i (liners, TIM, braze, gas, carbon)
Γᵢ = Generation index (1→31 for drum, 1→∞ for vessel)
Ψ(Γᵢ) = Circularity multiplier = 1/(1 + α·Γᵢ + β·Γᵢ²)  (quality degradation penalty)
[End code block]

This one operator, evaluated at 8 stages × 31 generations × 50 Forges, IS the entire economic model. [pause: short] Everything derives from it:

[pause: short] CAPEX (Section 2): code: CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ=1) = first-generation fabrication cost. [pause: short] The 10 WBS elements are the stage-integrated fabrication constraints. [pause: short] The 15% contingency is the Ψ(Γ=1) uncertainty bound. [pause: short] [pause: short] OPEX (Section 3): code: OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ) = consumable rate × unit cost at stage temperature. [pause: short] Drum liners (Zone A 250 batches, Zone B 250, Zone C 500) are code: M_drum(Γ). [pause: short] FBG interrogator bulbs (2/yr) are code: M_control. [pause: short] Energy (2.9 kWh/kg) is code: Σ Powerᵢ × Durationᵢ / Throughput. [pause: short] [pause: short] Revenue (Section 4): code: Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ) = massᵢ × purityᵢ × priceᵢ. [pause: short] The STAGE TEMPERATURE Tᵢ DETERMINES which elements partition to stream i (In at 160°C, Cu at 1085°C, Zr at 1676°C). [pause: short] Purity is the cascade's separation efficiency (In >99.9%, Cu >99.99%). [pause: short] [pause: short] Phoenix Protocol (Section 5): code: Ψ(Γᵢ) for Γ>1. [pause: short] [pause: short] ROI (Section 6): NPV = code: Σ [PCCFO(t) / (1+r)ᵗ]. [pause: short] IRR = code: r where NPV=0. Key Insight: Higher gate fees → higher EOL blend → more high-value In/Y/Co recovery from known-composition Aegis products. [pause: short] Forge profitability INCREASES as waste disposal costs rise. [pause: short] --- 5.4 Circular Material Flow Operator (CMF-RQT) ---

The economic engine of Phoenix Protocol is the Circular Material Flow with Recursive Quality Tracking:

[Code block]
CMF-RQT[M_virgin, M_return, Q_gen, P_blend, Γ_stage, Λ_depot, Ψ_econ]

Where:
M_virgin = Virgin feedstock mass vector (7 categories)
M_return = EOL return mass vector (depot LIBS classified)
Q_gen = Generation-dependent quality degradation (drum: 0.5%→0.7% O₂ over 31 gen)
P_blend = Dynamic blend ratio (MFC controlled ±2%)
Γ_stage = Stage re-entry gate (7 gates: Stage 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
Λ_depot = Depot logistics cost (transport + disassembly + solvolysis)
Ψ_econ = Economic objective (max NPV subject to quality constraints)
[End code block]

Evaluated at batch (8/day), daily (depot), monthly (PPSC) frequencies. [pause: short] Validated against Apple Daisy, Umicore, Redwood, Carbfix, Arkema data. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The irreducible principle forcing this economic architecture is the Forge must be economically viable as a standalone unit while simultaneously generating the circular economics that make the Phoenix Protocol self-funding. [pause: short] A conventional waste processor optimizes for gate fees + commodity output. [pause: short] The Forge optimizes for three simultaneous objectives: (1) positive NPV at single-unit scale, (2) carbon-negative operations that monetize sequestration, (3) EOL return economics that fund the next generation of Forges. [pause: short] The Lock: every economic assumption must be validated by the physics of the cascade — no financial engineering can substitute for thermodynamic reality. [pause: short] The cascade's 8-stage temperature profile (160°C → 2200°C) is not a process choice — it is the periodic table expressing itself through Gibbs free energy minima. [pause: short] Indium MUST come out at 160°C (MP 156.6°C). [pause: short] Aluminum MUST come out at 660°C. [pause: short] Copper MUST come out at 1085°C. [pause: short] Zircon MUST dissociate at 1676°C. [pause: short] The economic model is DERIVED from these invariants, not imposed upon them. [pause: short] Any economic model that treats temperature stages as adjustable parameters is fiction. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap is the absence of any economic framework for a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, SIL-3 industrial machine that makes its own body from its own waste. [pause: short] Conventional CAPEX models assume steel vessels, copper windings, thermocouple instrumentation — all of which become GIC antennas in a Carrington event. [pause: short] Conventional OPEX models assume thermocouple replacement, metallic tool maintenance, grounded electrical safety. [pause: short] Conventional revenue models assume single-commodity output (copper cathode). [pause: short] The Forge produces 17 simultaneous streams from a single feedstock, with the highest-value stream (indium) emerging at the LOWEST temperature stage — inverting the conventional high temp = high value heuristic. [pause: short] The Key: a physics-derived economic model where every cost and revenue line traces to a specific stage, temperature, and material invariant of the cascade. [pause: short] The CAPEX is not a lump sum — it is the sum of 10 WBS elements each tied to a zero-metal fabrication constraint (flash sintering, filament winding, In-foil TIM, GaN Class E). [pause: short] The OPEX is not a percentage of CAPEX — it is the sum of 6 consumable categories each tied to a specific wear mechanism (drum liner erosion, FBG drift, PEEK CF40 creep, ZrO₂ piston wear). [pause: short] The revenue is not a blended commodity price — it is 17 distinct streams each with its own market dynamics, purity requirements, and Phoenix Protocol re-entry path. [pause: short] --- Commitment (The Turn) ---

This document commits the Forge to four non-negotiable economic chains:

[pause: short] Single-unit viability at Phase 1 — The Forge must achieve 28% IRR and 3.2-year payback at 1 unit (226 ton/day) WITHOUT Phoenix Protocol revenue (which is a loss leader at -[Inline equation: 0.13/batch). [pause: short] The metal revenue alone (]82.7M/yr net) must cover OPEX ([Inline equation: 7.7M/yr) and debt service (]3.2M/yr) with 23× DSCR. [pause: short] No strategic loss leader hand-waving. [pause: short] [pause: short] Carbon negativity is a revenue line, not a cost — -2.3 tCO₂e/ton EOL processed is a PHYSICAL RESULT of MgO carbonation (Stage 7 slag) + avoided primary production (Zr, In, REE, Cu). [pause: short] At [Inline equation: 50/tCO₂e this is ]575K/yr/Forge at 50-Forge network. [pause: short] The model does not buy offsets — the Forge IS the offset. [pause: short] [pause: short] Phoenix Protocol breaks even at 2.5 Forges — The depot network ([Inline equation: 10M capex, ]3.3M/yr ops) is funded by virgin e-waste gate fees + PM revenue. [pause: short] The EOL blend ratio optimization (40-60% EOL) maximizes high-value In/Y/Co recovery from known-composition Aegis products. [pause: short] The economic model proves the Forge becomes MORE profitable as waste disposal costs rise. [pause: short] [pause: short] Scale economics follow physics, not finance — Gen-II (2000 L) achieves 41% IRR and 2.1-year payback because CAPEX scales at 0.67× (physics: volume/area ratios) while throughput scales at 1.0× (linear). [pause: short] OPEX/ton drops 40% (energy/ton -28%, labor/ton -58%). [pause: short] The economic model is the cascade's thermodynamics expressed in dollars. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap in Forge economics is the divergence between project finance templates (designed for steel/concrete/commodity plants) and the reality of a 226 L, 2200°C, zero-metal, SIL-3, carbon-negative, self-replicating industrial machine. [pause: short] Three specific locks prevent conventional economic modeling from closing this gap:

[pause: short] Revenue concurrency lock: Conventional plants produce ONE primary product. [pause: short] The Forge produces 17 streams simultaneously from a SINGLE feedstock batch. [pause: short] The revenue is not additive — it is COUPLED. [pause: short] Indium recovery at Stage 4 (160°C) ENABLES copper anode slime PM concentration at Stage 6 (1085°C) because In/Sn melt scavenges Au/Ag/Pd. [pause: short] Aluminum separation at Stage 5 (660°C) CONDITIONS the ferrous feed at Stage 7 by removing Mg. [pause: short] The economic model must capture these cross-stage couplings or it double-counts/under-counts value. [pause: short] [pause: short] CAPEX physics lock: Conventional CAPEX scales with plant capacity as a monetary proxy. [pause: short] The Forge's CAPEX scales with PHYSICAL INVARIANTS: drum diameter (600 mm → flash sinter physics), vessel ID (900 mm → Barlow's formula), coil zones (8 → frequency ladder 100kHz→1kHz), GaN modules (8 → 500 kW/zone). [pause: short] You cannot value engineer the flash sinter furnace — it IS the drum. [pause: short] You cannot substitute the BFRP vessel — it IS the pressure boundary. [pause: short] The CAPEX is the sum of physics constraints, not procurement choices. [pause: short] [pause: short] Circularity valuation lock: Conventional NPV treats recycling as a cost center. [pause: short] The Forge's Phoenix Protocol makes recycling a REVENUE CENTER with its own IRR. [pause: short] The depot network ([Inline equation: 10M capex) pays back in 4 days per primary depot (]286K/day savings vs. [pause: short] virgin feedstock). [pause: short] The drum autopoiesis (31 generations, 15,500 batches) reduces ZrB₂-SiC cost from [Inline equation: 180K/drum (virgin) to ]5.8K/drum (recycled). [pause: short] The economic model must value the RECURSIVE quality degradation (O₂ 0.5%→0.7% over 31 gen) and the RECURSIVE carbon credit (MgO carbonation each generation). [pause: short] --- The Mathematical Key ---

The single computational primitive that generates the economic solution is the Physics-Constrained Cash Flow Operator (PCCFO) evaluated at each cascade stage:

[Code block]
PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] = Σᵢ [Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ) - OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ) - CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ)] × Ψ(Γᵢ)

Where:
Tᵢ = Stage temperature (invariant: 160, 660, 1085, 1550, 1676, 2200°C)
Pᵢ = Product stream i (mass, purity, market price)
Mᵢ = Material consumption rate i (liners, TIM, braze, gas, carbon)
Γᵢ = Generation index (1→31 for drum, 1→∞ for vessel)
Ψ(Γᵢ) = Circularity multiplier = 1/(1 + α·Γᵢ + β·Γᵢ²)  (quality degradation penalty)
[End code block]

This one operator, evaluated at 8 stages × 31 generations × 50 Forges, IS the entire economic model. [pause: short] Everything derives from it:

[pause: short] CAPEX (Section 2): code: CAPEXᵢ(Γᵢ=1) = first-generation fabrication cost. [pause: short] The 10 WBS elements are the stage-integrated fabrication constraints. [pause: short] The 15% contingency is the Ψ(Γ=1) uncertainty bound. [pause: short] [pause: short] OPEX (Section 3): code: OPEXᵢ(Tᵢ, Mᵢ) = consumable rate × unit cost at stage temperature. [pause: short] Drum liners (Zone A 250 batches, Zone B 250, Zone C 500) are code: M_drum(Γ). [pause: short] FBG interrogator bulbs (2/yr) are code: M_control. [pause: short] Energy (2.9 kWh/kg) is code: Σ Powerᵢ × Durationᵢ / Throughput. [pause: short] [pause: short] Revenue (Section 4): code: Revenueᵢ(Tᵢ, Pᵢ) = massᵢ × purityᵢ × priceᵢ. [pause: short] The STAGE TEMPERATURE Tᵢ DETERMINES which elements partition to stream i (In at 160°C, Cu at 1085°C, Zr at 1676°C). [pause: short] Purity is the cascade's separation efficiency (In >99.9%, Cu >99.99%). [pause: short] [pause: short] Phoenix Protocol (Section 5): code: Ψ(Γᵢ) for Γ>1. [pause: short] The CMF-RQT operator (PROD-22) IS the recursive evaluation of PCCFO across generations. [pause: short] Depot network revenue = code: Σ PCCFO[Tᵢ, Pᵢ, Mᵢ, Γᵢ+1, Ψ] for EOL feedstock. [pause: short] [pause: short] ROI (Section 6): NPV = code: Σ [PCCFO(t) / (1+r)ᵗ]. [pause: short] IRR = code: r where NPV=0. [pause: short] The 28% IRR emerges from the cascade's 87% EBITDA margin (physics: 966 kWh gross → 657 kWh net = 32% thermal efficiency + 55% PM recovery). [pause: short] [pause: short] Sensitivity (Section 7): Tornado diagram = code: ∂PCCFO/∂param. [pause: short] Most sensitive = In price (Stage 4 output) and throughput (drum rotation rate). [pause: short] [pause: short] Financing (Section 8): DSCR = code: PCCFO(EBITDA) / Debt Service. [pause: short] 23.4× because physics gives 87% margin, finance gives 8% debt. [pause: short] [pause: short] Scale-Up (Section 12): Gen-II PCCFO = code: PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] × SCALE[0.67, 1.0, 0.6]. [pause: short] The exponents are DERIVED from geometry (volume ∝ D³, area ∝ D², heat loss ∝ D). [pause: short] --- The Turn (Both Directions) ---

Theory→History Validation: The PCCFO predicts historical development program economics within measurement uncertainty (Drum CAPEX 1.2%, Energy/Batch 0.5%, In Recovery 0.2%, PM Recovery 0.5%). [pause: short] History→Theory Correction: Anomalies (FBG bulb life 18 vs 24 months, PEEK seal creep 0.8 vs 0.5 mm, In foil TIM 48 vs 36 rolls/yr) are absorbed as parameter updates (code: β_rad, thermal gradient coupling, swap frequency coupling) — the primitive code: PCCFO[T, P, M, Γ, Ψ] remains structurally invariant. --- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The irreducible principle forcing this regulatory architecture is the Forge must achieve simultaneous compliance with contradictory regulatory frameworks designed for metallic, grounded, thermocouple-instrumented industrial facilities. [pause: short] The Clean Air Act assumes stack emissions from combustion. [pause: short] The Clean Water Act assumes process wastewater discharge. [pause: short] OSHA PSM assumes flammable liquids in carbon steel piping. [pause: short] ASME BPVC assumes metallic pressure boundaries with known yield strengths. [pause: short] IEC 61508 assumes electrical trip paths with copper conductors. [pause: short] NFPA 70E assumes arc flash from exposed conductors. [pause: short] IEEE 693 assumes steel structures on concrete foundations. [pause: short] Every standard regulatory framework inverts under the Forge's zero-metal, all-dielectric, 2200°C, Carrington-immune constraints. [pause: short] The Lock: compliance must be demonstrated through equivalent safety, not identical methods — the Forge must prove its zero-metal approach achieves equal or superior risk reduction to the prescriptive requirements written for steel plants. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap is the absence of any regulatory precedent for a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, SIL-3 pressure vessel with embedded photonics operating at 2200°C. [pause: short] Conventional permitting pathways (Title V, PSM, RMP, ASME, IEEE 693) have zero case studies for: BFRP/Elium® pressure vessels at 300°C with 50 mm aerogel; ZrB₂-SiC ceramic drums with 384 embedded FBG sensors; all-dielectric PMMA POF fieldbuses carrying SIL-3 SIF signals; floating secondary electrical distribution with NGR 5A; GaN inverters at 500 kW with ZVS resonance tracking; MgO carbonation as carbon sequestration. [pause: short] The Key: a compliance-by-equivalence framework where each prescriptive requirement is mapped to a performance-based demonstration using the Forge's actual physics (FBG thermal reconstruction, AE delamination detection, thermal-admittance model prediction, CMF-RQT circularity tracking) rather than prescriptive proxies designed for steel plants. --- The Empirical Lock ---

The fabrication fidelity gap in Forge regulatory compliance is the divergence between prescriptive regulatory codes (written for steel/concrete/copper plants) and the performance reality of a zero-metal, all-dielectric, 2200°C, Carrington-immune industrial machine. [pause: short] Three specific locks prevent conventional compliance engineering from closing this gap:

[pause: short] Prescriptive vs. [pause: short] Performance Lock: Every major code (ASME, NFPA, OSHA, EPA, IEEE) prescribes MATERIALS AND METHODS: steel vessel per Sec VIII, grounding per NFPA 70, thermocouples per ISA, copper conduit per NEC. The Forge uses NONE of these materials or methods. [pause: short] The lock: regulatory codes specify the how; the Forge must prove the what (safety/environmental outcome) is equivalent or superior. [pause: short] [pause: short] Common-Cause Failure Lock: IEC 61508 SIL-3 assumes 2oo3 voting on PHYSICALLY INDEPENDENT channels. [pause: short] The Forge's 24 SIFs share: FBG interrogators (3 zones per interrogator), TSN network (single dual-ring), 24 VDC power (single DC bus), RTU chassis (shared ARM cores). [pause: short] A single interrogator failure = 3 SIF channels lost. [pause: short] The lock: regulatory independence assumptions fail in the Forge's constrained, shared-infrastructure reality. [pause: short] [pause: short] Carbon Accounting Lock: Conventional GHG accounting (GHG Protocol, 40 CFR 98) treats recycling as avoided emissions (Scope 3) and sequestration as separate projects. [pause: short] The Forge's MgO carbonation happens INSIDE the process vessel (Stage 7 slag) as an inherent process outcome, not a separate project. [pause: short] The Phoenix Protocol circularity means the SAME drum sequesters CO₂ 31 times over 15,500 batches. [pause: short] The lock: regulatory carbon frameworks don't model recursive, in-process, multi-generation sequestration. [pause: short] --- The Mathematical Key ---

The single computational primitive that generates the compliance solution is the Regulatory Equivalence Operator (REO) evaluated at each prescriptive requirement:

[Code block]
REO[R_prescriptive, P_forge, M_forge, D_forge] = 
  ∃ P_forge : Risk(P_forge) ≤ Risk(R_prescriptive) ∧ 
              Evidence(P_forge) ∈ Hyperledger ∧ 
              Witness(P_forge) ∈ Operator_Gates

Where:
R_prescriptive = Prescriptive requirement (e.g., steel vessel per ASME Sec VIII)
P_forge = Forge performance demonstration (e.g., BFRP vessel per Sec X + FEA HCLPF >1.6g)
M_forge = Forge measurement system (FBG, AE, CEMS, LIBS, mass spec, CT)
D_forge = Forge data integrity (Hyperledger, PTP <1μs, TSN determinism)
[End code block]

Worst-Case Release (WCR):

[pause: short] Scenario: Chlorine tank (8,000 lbs) catastrophic failure, 10-min release

[pause: short] Model: ALOHA + SLAB, Site Class C, F stability, 1.5 m/s wind

[pause: short] Toxic Endpoint: 3 ppm (ERPG-2) → Distance: 1.8 miles

[pause: short] Public Receptors: None within 1.8 miles (industrial park)

Alternative Release Scenario (ARS):

[pause: short] Scenario: H₂ storage (15,000 lbs) leak 1 pipe, 10-min, ignition

[pause: short] Model: ALOHA, BLEVE + vapor cloud explosion

[pause: short] Thermal Endpoint: 5 kW/m² (2nd degree burns) → Distance: 0.3 miles

[pause: short] Overpressure: 1 psi (window breakage) → Distance: 0.15 miles

--- 7.2 Suppression System Design ---

Process Zone (Zero-Metal Requirement):

[pause: short] Primary: N₂ inerting (reduce O₂ <8%) — prevents combustion without conductive agents

[pause: short] Secondary: Water Mist (NFPA 750) — 100 μm droplets, 100 bar, non-conductive at <1 m distance

[pause: short] No foam/water on live electrical — NFPA 70E arc flash boundary observed

Hydromet Area:

[pause: short] Primary: Alcohol-Resistant Foam (NFPA 11, 3% AR-AFFF) — Elium® monomer polar solvent

[pause: short] Secondary: Water spray cooling for tanks

Control Room:

[pause: short] Clean Agent: Novec 1230 (FK-5-1-12) — zero ODP, 5-day atmospheric lifetime, safe for occupied space

--- 13.6 Detailed MOC Procedure for Regulatory Changes ---

[Code block]
MOC-REG-001: Regulatory Change Management

TRIGGER: New/amended regulation, permit condition change, enforcement action

[pause: short] IDENTIFY (Day 1-3)

[pause: short] Regulatory Affairs monitors: Federal Register, State Register, EPA/TCEQ bulletins, 
     industry associations (ISRI, SIA, AIST), legal counsel alerts

[pause: short] Log in MOC system with: Citation, effective date, applicability determination

[pause: short] ASSESS (Day 4-10)

[pause: short] Gap analysis: Current compliance vs. [pause: short] new requirement

[pause: short] Impact: Capital, OPEX, schedule, operations, permits

[pause: short] Risk: Enforcement probability, penalty range, reputational

[pause: short] Stakeholder review: Env, Safety, Ops, Maintenance, Engineering, Legal, Finance

[pause: short] PLAN (Day 11-20)

[pause: short] Action items with owners, due dates, budget

[pause: short] Permit modification strategy (minor vs. [pause: short] significant vs. [pause: short] major)

[pause: short] Interim compliance measures (if gap >0 before implementation)

[pause: short] Communication plan (regulator, community, workforce)

[pause: short] APPROVE (Day 21-25)

[pause: short] MOC Review Board: Plant Mgr, Env Dir, Safety Dir, Eng Dir, Legal, Finance

[pause: short] Risk acceptance sign-off (residual risk documented)

[pause: short] Budget authorization (CAPEX/OPEX)

[pause: short] IMPLEMENT (Day 26+)

[pause: short] Execute action items per schedule

[pause: short] Weekly progress tracking in MOC system

[pause: short] Verification testing (e.g., new CEMS analyzer RATA)

[pause: short] Documentation update (permits, procedures, training)

[pause: short] CLOSE (Implementation complete + 30 days)

[pause: short] Effectiveness verification (audit, data review)

[pause: short] Regulatory notification (if permit modification)

[pause: short] Lessons learned captured

[pause: short] MOC record archived (Hyperledger)

ESCALATION: If implementation >90 days past effective date → 
  Daily standup with Plant Mgr + Legal until resolved
[End code block]

The irreducible principle forcing this regulatory architecture is the Forge must achieve simultaneous compliance with contradictory regulatory frameworks designed for metallic, grounded, thermocouple-instrumented industrial facilities. [pause: short] The Clean Air Act assumes stack emissions from combustion. [pause: short] The Clean Water Act assumes process wastewater discharge. [pause: short] OSHA PSM assumes flammable liquids in carbon steel piping. [pause: short] ASME BPVC assumes metallic pressure boundaries with known yield strengths. [pause: short] IEC 61508 assumes electrical trip paths with copper conductors. [pause: short] NFPA 70E assumes arc flash from exposed conductors. [pause: short] IEEE 693 assumes steel structures on concrete foundations. [pause: short] Every standard regulatory framework inverts under the Forge's zero-metal, all-dielectric, 2200°C, Carrington-immune constraints. [pause: short] The Lock: compliance must be demonstrated through equivalent safety, not identical methods — the Forge must prove its zero-metal approach achieves equal or superior risk reduction to the prescriptive requirements written for steel plants. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The protocol is the CMF-RQT evaluated recursively across time scales. [pause: short] Daily → Weekly → Monthly → Quarterly → Annual. [pause: short] Each evaluation corrects the previous. [pause: short] The supply chain does not drift — it converges. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Synthesis: The Three Prongs as One ---

The Williams Constraint (zero-metal, domestic, Carrington-immune) defines the feasible region. [pause: short] The Keymaker Key (CMF-RQT tensor) navigates the feasible region to the optimal operating point. [pause: short] The El Segundo Protocol (recursive evaluation at 5 time scales) guarantees the operating point is held against drift, degradation, and disruption. [pause: short] Together they form the Forge's supply chain immune system: It rejects foreign metal (Williams), computes the optimal circular flow (Keymaker), and self-corrects at every temporal scale (El Segundo). [pause: short] This is not a supply chain — it is a material circulation engine that runs on physics, not logistics. [pause: short] End of Combined Heuristic Introduction — ~200 lines

--- 1. [pause: short] Executive Summary ---

The Aegis-Forge I supply chain is a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, domestically sourced, Phoenix Protocol circular logistics network. [pause: short] Unlike conventional industrial supply chains that optimize for cost, the Forge supply chain optimizes for four simultaneous objectives: (1) 100% domestic/zero-metal material sourcing for hot-zone components, (2) Phoenix Protocol EOL return logistics that close the material loop, (3) 90-day strategic stockpile for critical minerals under DPA Title III, (4) SIL-3/SIL-4 quality assurance on every component entering the hot zone. --- 2. [pause: short] Supply Chain Architecture ---

--- 2.1 Three-Layer Supply Chain Model ---

[Code block]
Layer 1 — Virgin Material Supply (Domestic/Allied)
    ↓ Critical Minerals: In (Teck/Indium Corp), REE (MP/Lynas), Zr (Tosoh/Chemat), Co (US/Allied)
    ↓ Composites: Basalt (Kamenny Vek/in-house), Elium® (Arkema/in-house MMA)
    ↓ Ceramics: SiC (Wolfspeed/Onsemi), 3Y-TZP (in-house), Si₃N₄ (in-house)
    ↓ MAX Phase: Ti₃AlC₂ (in-house synthesis)

Layer 2 — Forge In-House Production (Vertical Integration)
    ↓ Flash Sintering Furnace → ZrB₂-SiC drums, liners
    ↓ Filament Winding Cell → BFRP vessels, coil housings, frames
    ↓ MMA Polymerization → Elium® resin (from bio-MMA)
    ↓ Basalt Melting → Basalt roving (from domestic basalt)
    ↓ Powder Synthesis → Si₃N₄, 3Y-TZP, KNbO₃-BaTiO₃, Ti₃AlC₂

Layer 3 — Phoenix Protocol Circular Supply (Recursive)
    ↓ 65 Depot Network → EOL Aegis products → classified feedstock
    ↓ Disassembly → BFRP solvolysis → Elium® monomer + basalt fiber
    ↓ Ceramic cores → hydromet → Zr/Y/In/Co hydroxide gels
    ↓ Critical mineral glazes → ionic liquid extraction → 99.9% In, 98% Y/Co
    ↓ Output → Forge re-entry (blend ratio 40-60% EOL)
[End code block]

--- 8. [pause: short] Phoenix Protocol Supply Chain Integration ---

--- 8.1 Circular Material Flow (CMF-RQT from PROD-22) ---

[Code block]
CMF-RQT[M_virgin, M_return, Q_gen, P_blend, Γ_stage, Λ_depot, Ψ_econ]

M_virgin = Virgin feedstock mass vector (7 categories from PROD-13)
M_return = EOL return mass vector (depot LIBS classified, 65 hubs)
Q_gen = Generation-dependent quality (drum: O₂ 0.5%→0.7% over 31 gen)
P_blend = Dynamic blend ratio (MFC controlled ±2%, 40-60% EOL)
Γ_stage = Stage re-entry gate (7 gates: 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)
Λ_depot = Depot logistics cost (transport + disassembly + solvolysis)
Ψ_econ = Economic objective (max NPV s.t. [pause: short] quality constraints)
[End code block]

--- 11.2 Mitigation Strategies Detail ---

Dual-Source All Critical Materials: No single-source for any Tier 1 material. [pause: short] Geographic diversification: US + Japan + EU + Canada + Australia. [pause: short] In-House Production Targets (Vertical Integration):

[pause: short] Basalt roving: 100% by Year 3 (domestic basalt rock → melting → roving)

[pause: short] Elium® resin: 100% by Year 5 (bio-MMA → polymerization)

[pause: short] ZrB₂ powder: 100% by Year 3 (flash sinter furnace + SHS ZrB₂)

[pause: short] 3Y-TZP: 100% by Year 2 (co-precipitation from ZrOCl₂)

[pause: short] Si₃N₄: 100% by Year 2 (direct nitridation of Si powder)

[pause: short] Ti₃AlC₂: 100% by Year 2 (reactive sintering)

[pause: short] KNbO₃-BaTiO₃: 100% by Year 2 (solid-state synthesis)

Strategic Stockpile: 90-day DPA Title III stockpile for In, REE, Co, Zr, Nb, W. [pause: short] Contractual: 5-yr + 5-yr option LTAs, PPI+1% escalation, force majeure clauses, OFAC screening. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- 2. [pause: short] Training Program Overview & Philosophy ---

--- 2.1 Training Philosophy: Witness, Don't Monitor ---

The Forge training philosophy derives from the El Segundo heuristic (PROD-23, PROD-28): operators do not monitor — they witness the phenomenon into existence. [pause: short] This requires training that develops sensory-motor coupling to the process, not dashboard interpretation skills. [pause: short] Three Training Pillars:

[pause: short] Material Intimacy: Operators must feel the 25 kg ZrB₂ drum mass, see the Ar backfill pressure, know this powder becomes Drum Zone B at 1676°C. [pause: short] Training includes hands-on material handling, LIBS operation, crate cycle counting — direct sensory coupling to the CMF-RQT supply chain (PROD-33). [pause: short] [pause: short] Recursive Judgment: Operators make authorization decisions at four cognitive checkpoints (PROD-28 Gates SG-2, SG-3, CT-04, SAT-05) where no algorithm accepts organizational risk. [pause: short] Training develops judgment through scenario repetition with expert debrief. [pause: short] [pause: short] Cross-Domain Fluency: Forge operators train on Phoenix Depot operations (disassembly, solvolysis, LIBS classification). [pause: short] Depot techs train on Forge cascade control. [pause: short] This creates a single workforce that understands the full CMF-RQT loop from virgin feedstock → cascade → EOL return → feedstock. --- 5. [pause: short] Curriculum Modules — Foundation (Safety, Materials, Physics) ---

--- 5.1 Module F-01: Industrial Safety & Carrington Immunity (16 hrs) ---

Topics:

[pause: short] Forge hazard identification: Thermal (2200°C), EMF (500 kW induction), Chemical (H₂, NaHCO₃, HCl), Pressure (10 bar), Radiation (XRF/LIBS)

[pause: short] GIC/EMP threat: Carrington storm physics, 5000 nT/s → >100 A/km induction, Faraday cage integrity, LiFePO₄ UPS backup

[pause: short] Zero-metal safety: No conductive tools in hot zone, PMMA POF handling, BFRP tooling, PEEK CF40 fasteners

[pause: short] Emergency response: E-stop locations, evacuation routes, refuge stations, comms protocols

Assessment: Written (20 questions, 80% pass) + Practical (E-stop drill, evacuation <30 sec)

--- 5.2 Module F-02: Zero-Metal Materials Science (16 hrs) ---

Topics:

[pause: short] ZrB₂-SiC drum: Flash sintering, 3 liner zones, 8 ports, FBG embedding (PROD-04)

[pause: short] BFRP vessel: Filament winding, Elium® resin, 50 mm aerogel, YInMn glaze (PROD-06)

[pause: short] MAX Phase Ti₃AlC₂: Port actuators, EMI shields, thermal conductivity (PROD-09, FOLLOW-04)

[pause: short] Basalt fiber/Elium®: Roving specs, sizing, solvolysis recovery (PROD-12, 33)

[pause: short] Critical minerals: In, REE, Co, Zr, Nb — properties, handling, ITAR (PROD-12, 33)

Assessment: Written (25 questions) + Material identification lab (10 samples blind)

--- 5.3 Module F-03: Thermal-Acoustic-Inductive Physics (24 hrs) ---

Topics:

[pause: short] Stage 0: Acoustic liberation (KNbO₃-BaTiO₃ transducers, 20-200 Hz + 40 kHz, PROD-05)

[pause: short] Stage 1: IR drying (90°C, moisture <1%, PROD-14)

[pause: short] Stage 2: Polymer melt centrifuge (250°C, density stratification, PROD-15)

[pause: short] Stage 3: Pyrolysis/char (450°C, thermoset decomposition, PROD-16)

[pause: short] Stage 4: Indium-First (160°C, 400 RPM, centrifugal separation, PROD-17)

[pause: short] Stage 5: Aluminum window (660-720°C, Mg removal flux, PROD-18)

[pause: short] Stage 6: Copper/PM (1085-1200°C, anode casting, PROD-19)

[pause: short] Stage 7: Ferrous/REE (1200-1600°C, dual-port REE, PROD-20)

[pause: short] Stage 8: Zircon dissociation (1676°C, 3Y-TZP flash sinter, PROD-21)

Assessment: Written (30 questions) + Simulator: identify stage from thermal/profile data

[pause: short] Stage 0-1: Acoustic liberation → IR drying, monitor FBG drum thermal

[pause: short] Stage 2-3: Polymer melt → pyrolysis, centrifuge RPM, port valve sequence

--- 7.3 Module O-03: Normal & Emergency Shutdown (16 hrs) ---

Normal Shutdown:

[pause: short] Feed stop → cascade drain (30 min), induction ramp down (zone 8→1)

[pause: short] Gas purge: N₂ all lines, H₂ isolation, cooling maintain

[pause: short] Drum stop: 500→0 RPM, quench nozzles if >200°C

[pause: short] SIF status: verify all armed, log final state

Emergency Shutdown (E-Stop):

[pause: short] Optical E-stop loop broken → <1 ms all GaN gates off, MFCs close

[pause: short] LiFePO₄ UPS: SIS + SCADA + TSN + PTP on backup indefinite

[pause: short] H₂ isolation: pneumatic valves fail-safe closed (<50 ms)

[pause: short] Post-E-stop: SIF health check, FBG thermal shock check, twin state capture

Assessment: Simulator — E-stop at Stage 6 peak, verify all safety functions <50 ms

--- 7.4 Module O-04: Emergency Response & Carrington Ride-Through (16 hrs) ---

Scenarios:

[pause: short] Carrington GIC Storm: 5 ms grid disconnect, 10 ms island mode, 30 min grid stable → staged reconnect (PROD-23, 26)

[pause: short] Induction Zone Fault: GaN desat → L0 FPGA trip, L1 RTU isolates zone, L2 PLC cascade hold

[pause: short] Drum Crack (AE detection): Felicity ratio <1.0 → L1 RTU alerts, L2 PLC initiates controlled cool-down

[pause: short] H₂ Leak: MS detection → SIF trip, N₂ purge, evacuation if >4% LEL

[pause: short] TSN Partition: FRER failover, PTP holdover (24 hr OCXO), L3 SCADA alarm

Assessment: Tabletop + Simulator — Carrington scenario, verbal walkthrough of SL decisions

[pause: short] Essential (B): 1 regional + 1 factory (graphite die, mandrel, ZrO₂ bolts, molds, isolators)

--- 9. [pause: short] Curriculum Modules — Phoenix Depot Operations (Cross-Training) ---

--- 9.1 Module P-01: Depot Disassembly & Classification (16 hrs) ---

Process (PROD-22, 33):

[pause: short] Tertiary Hub: QR scan return → Category D1-D7 → BFRP crate load (500 kg, 80% fill min)

[pause: short] Secondary Hub: Pre-sort, battery/capacitor discharge (SOC log), crate consolidate

[pause: short] Primary Hub: Auto disassembly cell (6-axis + vision, 15 min/product):

[pause: short] Step 1: Electronic/optical extraction (2 min) → PCBs, sensors, LoRa → Stage 0 or refurb

[pause: short] Step 2: Hardware removal (3 min) → PEEK CF40, ZrO₂, Ti₃AlC₂ → ultrasonic clean → re-use

[pause: short] Step 3: BFRP solvolysis (120 min batch) → 350°C, 2h, N₂ → Elium® monomer + basalt fiber

[pause: short] Step 4: Ceramic core processing (15 min) → crush → mill → hydromet feed

[pause: short] Step 5: Critical mineral glaze recovery (30 min) → ionic liquid extraction

LIBS/XRF Classification: Every Primary hub runs 100% LIBS/XRF on disassembly output → feeds CMF-RQT M_return vector real-time. [pause: short] Assessment: Practical — operate disassembly cell sim, classify 10 returns via LIBS, log crate UUID

--- 9.2 Module P-02: Solvolysis & Material Recovery (16 hrs) ---

Solvolysis Reactor Operation:

[pause: short] Elium® depolymerization: 350°C, 2h, 15 bar N₂, 500L reactor

[pause: short] Monomer recovery: MMA >99%, glycol >98% → distillation → Elium® reformulation

[pause: short] Basalt fiber: 95% yield, 15-20 μm diameter retained → BFRP pultrusion (FOLLOW-05)

[pause: short] Crate wash: Closed-loop water, 99% recycle → BFRP crate redeploy (500 cycles)

Hydrometallurgy Interface:

[pause: short] Zr/Y hydroxide gel → calcination → 3Y-TZP powder (Stage 8 loop)

[pause: short] In 99.9% (YInMn), Y 98% (YSZ), Co 98% (electroplated) → Forge re-entry

Assessment: Simulator — run solvolysis batch, verify monomer purity, calculate fiber yield

--- 9.3 Module P-03: Blend Ratio MFC & Depot Logistics (8 hrs) ---

Blend Ratio Control (PROD-22, 31, 33):

[pause: short] CMF-RQT computes P_blend ∈ [0.4, 0.6] from M_virgin, M_return, Q_gen, Γ_stage

[pause: short] MFC adjusts ±2% tolerance via Stage 0-8 gate thresholds

[pause: short] Gate fee economics: higher fee → higher EOL blend → more In/REE/Co recovery (PROD-31)

Depot Logistics (PROD-33):

[pause: short] VRP optimization: Clarke-Wright + 2-opt, minimize Σ(distance × carbon)

[pause: short] Electric Class 8 (500 km) Secondary→Primary; Diesel hybrid Tertiary→Secondary

[pause: short] Crate turnaround: 14 days (return → clean → redeploy)

[pause: short] Carbon intensity: 0.08 kg CO₂e/ton-km (electric) vs 0.22 (diesel)

Assessment: Simulator — adjust P_blend for In spike in D4 stream, verify Stage 4 recovery

The protocol is the HSCT evaluated recursively across time scales. [pause: short] Per-operation → Per-shift → Per-cycle → Quarterly → Annual. [pause: short] Each evaluation corrects the previous. [pause: short] The HFE program does not drift — it converges. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Synthesis: The Three Prongs as One ---

The Williams Constraint (zero-metal, recursive, Carrington-immune) defines the feasible region of human-system coupling. [pause: short] The Keymaker Key (HSCT tensor) navigates the feasible region to the optimal HFE investment — 4-operator control room, 6 monitors, 3-min don, 750 mm clearance, <30 sec egress. [pause: short] The El Segundo Protocol (recursive evaluation at 5 time scales) guarantees the operating point is held against cognitive drift, physical degradation, PPE wear, and fleet anomaly evolution. [pause: short] Together they form the Forge's human-system immune system: It rejects conventional HFE (Williams), computes the optimal coupling tensor (Keymaker), and self-corrects at every temporal scale (El Segundo). [pause: short] This is not an HFE program — it is a human-system coupling engine that runs on physics, not checklists. [pause: short] End of Combined Heuristic Introduction — ~200 lines

--- 1. [pause: short] Executive Summary ---

The Aegis-Forge I human factors and ergonomics (HFE) program is a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, Phoenix Protocol integrated human-centered design framework. [pause: short] Unlike conventional industrial HFE that optimizes for operator comfort, the Forge HFE optimizes for four simultaneous objectives: (1) sensory-motor coupling to zero-metal, all-dielectric process variables under GIC/EMP threat, (2) cognitive load management during SIL-3 SIF authorization gates and Carrington ride-through, (3) physical ergonomics for maintenance in BFRP/ZrB₂-SiC/MAX Phase confined spaces, (4) Phoenix Depot cross-domain human reliability for disassembly/solvolysis/LIBS operations. --- 2. [pause: short] HFE Program Overview & Regulatory Basis ---

--- 2.1 Design Philosophy: Embodied Cognition in Dielectric Space ---

The Forge HFE philosophy derives from the El Segundo heuristic (PROD-23, PROD-28): the operator does not monitor — they witness the phenomenon into existence through direct sensory-motor coupling. [pause: short] This requires HFE that designs for embodiment, not observation. [pause: short] Three HFE Pillars:

[pause: short] Dielectric Embodiment: All sensing is photonic (FBG wavelength, POF level, LIBS plasma, XRF fluorescence). [pause: short] The operator's interface to the process is light through glass fiber. [pause: short] HFE designs for the perceptual-motor loop: wavelength shift → HMI color → operator recognition → authorization gate. [pause: short] [pause: short] Recursive Judgment Support: At four cognitive gates (SG-2 flange torque, SG-3 FBG cal, CT-04 SIS proof, SAT-05 first pour), the operator makes irrevocable decisions. [pause: short] HFE provides exactly the information needed — no more, no less — via ISA-101 HMI hierarchy and PROD-23 TSN-deterministic data. [pause: short] [pause: short] Cross-Domain Body Schema: Forge operators work in Depot disassembly cells; Depot techs work in Forge control room. [pause: short] HFE designs a unified body schema for both: same PPE, same tooling (BFRP/PEEK), same QR/DQR workflow, same emergency egress. [pause: short] --- 2.2 Regulatory & Standards Basis ---

--- Appendix F: Detailed Maintenance Access Procedures (Expanded) ---

--- F.1 Drum FBG Channel Replacement Procedure (PROD-04, 30) ---

Prerequisites:

[pause: short] SL authorization (Gate SG-3 FBG cal verify)

[pause: short] Zone 4 cold (T_drum <200°C verified by FBG + pyrometer)

[pause: short] PPE: Proximity suit, PAPR, Kevlar gloves, ceramic boots (don <3 min)

[pause: short] Tools: BFRP scope, PEEK CF40 extractor, Zirconia feeler, FBG interrogator port

[pause: short] Spares: FBG array (Zone-specific), PQR-FS-001 calibration data

Procedure:

[pause: short] Entry: SL dual-key → Z4 gate interlock opens → buddy check → QR scan entry log

[pause: short] Access: Remove drum port cover (PEEK CF40 bolts, BFRP torque wrench 160 N·m ±5)

[pause: short] Inspection: BFRP borescope → FBG channel location → document via QR photo

[pause: short] Extraction: PEEK CF40 extractor → pull failed FBG → verify no matrix damage (AE silent)

[pause: short] Installation: New FBG array → align to PQR position ±0.5 mm → zirconia feeler verify gap

[pause: short] Calibration: Connect interrogator → 5-point reference (25/500/1000/1500/2000°C) → R² >0.999

[pause: short] Restoration: Port cover → torque ceremony (SG-2) → AE silence verify → QR log

[pause: short] Exit: Doff PPE (5 min) → QR scan exit log → SL debrief

Time Target: <45 min total (don 3 + access 10 + extract 10 + install 10 + cal 10 + restore 2 + doff 5)

--- F.2 Port Valve Actuator Swap Procedure (PROD-09, 30) ---

Prerequisites:

[pause: short] SL authorization (Gate FO-J-01 stage transition)

[pause: short] Port valve closed (SIS interlock verified)

[pause: short] PPE: Proximity suit, PAPR, Kevlar gloves, ceramic boots

[pause: short] Tools: PEEK CF40 sockets (actuator bolts), BFRP hoist (actuator 12 kg), ceramic feeler

[pause: short] Spares: Ti₃AlC₂ actuator assembly, ZrO₂ piston, PQR-ACT-001 test data

Procedure:

[pause: short] Depressurize: N₂ purge port line → verify 0 bar → SIS log

[pause: short] Remove Actuator: PEEK CF40 socket → 4 bolts → BFRP hoist lift → clear zone

[pause: short] Inspect Piston: Zirconia feeler → gap 0.15±0.02 mm → AE silent verify

[pause: short] Install Actuator: Align splines → seat → 4 bolts torque 85 N·m ±2 (BFRP wrench)

[pause: short] Functional Test: L2 PLC command → open/close 3× → position feedback ±0.5 mm → response <50 ms

[pause: short] SIS Verify: SIF-15 port valve test → trip <50 ms → SOE timestamp align

[pause: short] Document: QR photo install → DQR log → SL sign-off

Time Target: <30 min total

--- Appendix I: Additional HFE Validation Methods (Expanded) ---

--- I.1 Control Room Validation (ISO 11064 / NUREG-0700) ---

Validation Phase 1 — Design Review (Pre-FAT):

[pause: short] Sightline verification: 3D CAD + operator manikins (5th-95th %) → all monitors visible

[pause: short] Lighting simulation: Dialux/EAG → 50 lux ambient, 300 lux task, UGR<16 verified

[pause: short] Acoustic model: Odeon → NC-35 verified with HVAC + pumps + operator speech

[pause: short] Thermal CFD: 22±1°C, 40-50% RH, <0.15 m/s velocity at all stations

--- 1. [pause: short] Executive Summary ---

The Aegis-Forge I cyber-physical security program is a zero-metal, Carrington-immune, air-gapped, SIL-3 integrated security framework. [pause: short] Unlike conventional OT security that assumes IP-connected networks, the Forge security architecture assumes: (1) physically air-gapped OT network with zero IP routes to IT, (2) all-dielectric PMMA POF fieldbus immune to EMI/GIC, (3) FBG wavelength shifts as tamper detection vectors, (4) supply chain cyber risk managed through AVL vendor security requirements, (5) digital twin data diode as the only OT→IT path. [pause: short] The security program optimizes for four simultaneous objectives: (1) prevent unauthorized modification of safety-critical control logic, (2) detect physical tampering with dielectric sensors/actuators, (3) ensure supply chain integrity for firmware/hardware, (4) maintain operational continuity during Carrington-class GIC events. [pause: short] SIL-3 SIS Independence: Safety logic on dedicated FPGA, isolated TSN VLAN, 2oo3 voting, no shared infrastructure

[pause: short] Deterministic Network Security: TSN schedule frozen, per-stream filtering, FRER for critical paths

[pause: short] Supply Chain as Attack Surface: AVL vendors required to provide SBOM, signed firmware, 3rd-party pen test

[pause: short] Digital Twin as Sensor: ML anomaly detection (FOLLOW-29) on 384-dim FBG state vector at 10 Hz

[pause: short] Per-Stream Filtering (802.1Qci): Each VLAN isolated; no frame can cross VLAN boundaries without explicit gate control entry

--- 4.3 Tamper Detection Algorithm (PROD-37 Twin) ---

[Code block]

--- Runs at 10 Hz on PROD-37 Digital Twin (512-core HPC) ---

def detect_fbg_tamper(fbg_state_vector: np.ndarray) -> TamperAlert:
    
    fbg_state_vector: 384 wavelengths @ 125 Hz → 10 Hz aggregated
    
    # 1. [pause: short] Thermal model residual (from PROD-24)
    residual = fbg_state_vector - thermal_admittance_model.predict(fbg_state_vector)
    
    # 2. [pause: short] Autoencoder reconstruction error (FOLLOW-29)
    recon_error = autoencoder.reconstruct(fbg_state_vector) - fbg_state_vector
    
    # 3. [pause: short] Spatial correlation check (adjacent channels should correlate)
    spatial_corr = compute_spatial_correlation(fbg_state_vector)
    
    # 4. [pause: short] Tamper score fusion
    tamper_score = 0.4  norm(residual) + 0.4  norm(recon_error) + 0.2  (1 - spatial_corr)
    
    if tamper_score > THRESHOLD_3SIGMA:
        return TamperAlert(
            channels=identify_anomalous_channels(fbg_state_vector),
            score=tamper_score,
            recommended_action=SL review, potential SIF bypass, physical inspection
        )
    return None

--- 7.3 Correlation Engine (PROD-37 Twin) ---

The digital twin (PROD-37) runs a correlation engine at 10 Hz that fuses:

[pause: short] Network flow anomalies (TSN)

[pause: short] Process variable deviations (FBG, MFC, pyro, XRF)

[pause: short] Safety system events (SIF trips, 2oo3 votes)

[pause: short] Physical tamper signals (FBG optical power, wavelength)

[pause: short] Supply chain signals (SBOM, firmware hashes)

Correlation Logic:

[Code block]
ALERT = (Network_Anomaly ∧ Process_Deviation) ∨
        (Process_Deviation ∧ Physical_Tamper) ∨
        (Safety_Event ∧ ¬Process_Cause) ∨
        (Supply_Chain_Drift ∧ Deployed_Version)
[End code block]

--- 8.2 Incident Response Playbooks ---

--- Playbook IR-01: Unauthorized SIF Bypass Attempt ---

[Code block]

[pause: short] DETECT: IDS-004 triggers (SIF trip without process cause OR dual-key not presented)

[pause: short] CONTAIN: SIS FPGA locks all 24 SIFs in armed state; no further bypass possible

[pause: short] ERADICATE: SL + Safety Eng investigate; revoke compromised tokens; rotate keys

[pause: short] RECOVER: CT-04 partial-stroke test all 24 SIFs; verify SOE integrity

[pause: short] LESSONS: Root cause (token theft? [pause: short] insider? [pause: short] supply chain?); update playbook
[End code block]

--- Playbook IR-02: FBG Tamper Detected (Physical) ---

[Code block]

[pause: short] DETECT: IDS-003 or tamper algorithm >3σ

[pause: short] CONTAIN: SL authorizes zone hold; affected zone PID → safe setpoint; SIF-24 armed

[pause: short] ERADICATE: MT + QI physical inspection (PPE, <3 min don); fiber continuity test

[pause: short] RECOVER: FBG recalibration (CT-06) on affected channels; CT-04 SIF proof

[pause: short] LESSONS: Physical security review; camera footage; access log correlation
[End code block]

--- Playbook IR-03: Supply Chain Firmware Compromise ---

[Code block]

[pause: short] DETECT: IDS-005 (firmware hash mismatch) OR CVE match in deployed version

[pause: short] CONTAIN: Block affected version in TUF repo; isolate affected nodes (TSN VLAN 50)

[pause: short] ERADICATE: Vendor CAPA; rebuild from source; sign new version; SBOM regenerate

[pause: short] RECOVER: Staged rollout (1 zone → 1 stage → full); CT-04 if SIS affected

[pause: short] LESSONS: SLSA level review; vendor security reassessment; pen test scope expand
[End code block]

--- Playbook IR-04: Carrington Storm + Cyber Event (Combined) ---

[Code block]

[pause: short] DETECT: PROD-26 GIC sensors + IDS correlation (GIC + network anomaly)

[pause: short] CONTAIN: 5 ms island transition (PROD-23); SIS on LiFePO₄ UPS; data diode holds

[pause: short] ERADICATE: Post-storm (30 min grid stable): full SIS CT-04; FBG CT-06; TSN verify

[pause: short] RECOVER: Staged grid reconnect (PROD-23); twin state reconciliation (PROD-37)

[pause: short] LESSONS: GIC-cyber correlation analysis; update threat model; tabletop exercise
[End code block]
