class FBGTamperClassifier:
    def __init__(self):
        self.thermal_model = ThermalAdmittanceModel()  # PROD-24
        self.autoencoder = Autoencoder(latent_dim=32)  # FOLLOW-29
        self.spatial_graph = SpatialCorrelationGraph()  # 384-channel topology
        
    def classify(self, fbg_wavelengths: np.ndarray) -> TamperClassification:
        
        fbg_wavelengths: shape (384,) - current wavelength readings (nm)
        Returns: TamperClassification enum + confidence + affected channels
        
        
        # Hypothesis H0: Nominal thermal operation
        thermal_pred = self.thermal_model.predict(fbg_wavelengths)
        residual = fbg_wavelengths - thermal_pred
        H0_score = np.linalg.norm(residual)
        
        # Hypothesis H1: Localized physical tamper (fiber tap, cut, strain)
        recon = self.autoencoder.reconstruct(fbg_wavelengths)
        recon_error = fbg_wavelengths - recon
        spatial_corr = self.spatial_graph.correlation(fbg_wavelengths)
        H1_score = 0.5  np.linalg.norm(recon_error) + 0.5  (1 - spatial_corr)
        
        # Hypothesis H2: Interrogator compromise (all channels shifted)
        common_mode = np.mean(fbg_wavelengths - thermal_pred)
        H2_score = np.abs(common_mode)
        
        # Hypothesis H3: Selective channel spoofing (adversarial injection)
        channel_stats = self.compute_channel_statistics(fbg_wavelengths)
        H3_score = self.detect_adversarial_pattern(channel_stats)
        
        # Bayesian model selection
        scores = np.array([H0_score, H1_score, H2_score, H3_score])
        priors = np.array([0.95, 0.03, 0.015, 0.005])  # From fleet history
        posteriors = scores  priors / np.sum(scores  priors)
        
        max_idx = np.argmax(posteriors)
        confidence = posteriors[max_idx]
        
        if max_idx == 0:
            return TamperClassification.NOMINAL, confidence, []
        elif max_idx == 1:
            affected = self.localize_tamper(recon_error, spatial_corr)
            return TamperClassification.LOCALIZED_TAMPER, confidence, affected
        elif max_idx == 2:
            return TamperClassification.INTERROGATOR_COMPROMISE, confidence, list(range(384))
        else:
            affected = self.identify_spoofed_channels(channel_stats)
            return TamperClassification.SELECTIVE_SPOOFING, confidence, affected

--- 2.2 Multi-Rate Fusion Algorithm ---

The sensor fusion operates as a multi-rate Kalman filter with physics-constrained prediction:

[Code block]
State vector x ∈ ℝⁿ: [T_drum(384), σ_drum(96), P_zone(8), ω, m_charge, X_composition, ...]

Prediction (1 kHz L1):
  x[k+1|k] = f(x[k], u[k]) + w[k]          // f = thermal-admittance operator (PROD-24)
  P[k+1|k] = F[k]P[k]Fᵀ[k] + Q[k]           // F = Jacobian of f

Correction (multi-rate):

Update: K[k] = P[k

k-1]Hᵀ + R)⁻¹

Key innovation: The measurement matrices H are time-varying — FBG channels drop out at >800°C (PMMA degradation), so the filter dynamically reconfigures H_FBG based on channel health from PROD-28 auto-NCR (Λ > 10 on >5 channels = channel dropout). [pause: short] --- 2.3 FBG Channel Health & Tamper Integration ---

Per PROD-36, FBG channels serve dual purpose — process metrology AND security sensing:

[Code block]
def fbg_health_check(channel_data, twin_autoencoder):
    # Process health
    snr = channel_data.optical_power / channel_data.noise_floor
    wavelength_drift = abs(channel_data.λ - channel_data.λ_nominal)
    
    # Tamper detection (PROD-36 CPAT)
    Λ_tamper = twin_autoencoder.anomaly_score(channel_data.window_10Hz)
    
    if snr < 10 or wavelength_drift > 0.5:  # nm
        return ChannelStatus.DEGRADED
    elif Λ_tamper > 10:
        return ChannelStatus.TAMPER_SUSPECT  # Auto-NCR triggered
    else:
        return ChannelStatus.NOMINAL
[End code block]

Degraded channels are excluded from thermal reconstruction but logged for tamper forensics. [pause: short] Tamper-suspect channels trigger immediate SIF-24 evaluation and CPAT update. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Williams Heuristic — Architectural Clarity ---

--- Constraint (The Lock) ---

The Forge's physics demands a data architecture that cannot exist in conventional IT/OT frameworks. [pause: short] A 2200°C induction furnace with 384 dielectric FBG sensors at 125 Hz, GaN inverters at 100 kHz, SIL-3 SIFs on TSN, and a physically air-gapped network generates a multi-rate sensor stream that no standard historian, SCADA, or digital twin platform can ingest, fuse, and act upon within the process time constants. [pause: short] Conventional data management assumes: (a) IP-connected networks with centralized historians, (b) uniform sampling rates (typically 1 Hz), (c) copper Ethernet with standard protocols (OPC-UA, MQTT), (d) cloud-based analytics with second-to-minute latency, (e) separate IT/OT security domains with firewalls. [pause: short] The Forge violates all five: the network is physically air-gapped (no IP routes OT↔IT), sampling spans 50 kHz (AE) to 1 Hz (gas) across four control hierarchy levels, the fieldbus is PMMA POF (immune to EMI/GIC), analytics must run at 10 Hz on a 512-core HPC to close the control loop, and the only OT→IT path is a hardware data diode with protocol break. [pause: short] The constraint is physics — thermal diffusion (ms), EM resonance (μs), material transformation (100 ms), and GIC immunity (ns) operate at time scales that cannot be bridged by conventional data architectures. [pause: short] The air-gap is not a policy — it is a dielectric requirement. [pause: short] --- Necessity (The Key) ---

The empirical gap is the absence of any data management framework that fuses multi-rate, all-dielectric sensor streams into a real-time digital twin that drives control, safety, maintenance, training, and fleet optimization simultaneously. [pause: short] No existing platform addresses: (a) 384-channel FBG thermal reconstruction at 1 kHz feeding a 10 Hz CFD-FEA-EM coupled twin, (b) autoencoder anomaly detection on 384-dim FBG state running in the twin at 10 Hz with <1 s detection latency, (c) Bayesian fleet parameter updates from twin posteriors propagating to supply chain (CMF-RQT), training (RCT), and HFE (HSCT) tensors, (d) hardware data diode as the only OT→IT path with merkle-verified integrity at 10 Hz, (e) blockchain-anchored data lineage for regulatory (EPA, NRC, ITAR) and liability traceability. [pause: short] The solution is inevitable because the Forge's physics demands it: the same FBG wavelength that measures drum temperature at 125 Hz also detects tamper (PROD-36); the same thermal-admittance operator that drives PID at 1 kHz (PROD-23) drives the twin at 10 Hz; the same POD-Galerkin ROM (12 modes, 118× speedup) that enables Monte Carlo UQ also generates training scenarios (PROD-34). [pause: short] Data management cannot be bolted on — it must be architected into the dielectric control fabric. [pause: short] --- Commitment (The Turn) ---

This document commits to three non-negotiables:

[pause: short] Four-level hierarchy fixed — L0 (100 kHz FPGA) → L1 (1 kHz RTU) → L2 (100 Hz PLC) → L3 (10 Hz SCADA/Twin). [pause: short] Time constants are physical (PROD-23 commitment #1). [pause: short] [pause: short] Physical air-gap absolute for data — No IP routes OT↔IT, no wireless, no powerline comms; hardware data diode enforces unidirectional OT→IT only at 10 Hz with merkle integrity; violation requires SCSC unanimous + full SIL-3 re-certification (CT-04). [pause: short] [pause: short] Twin is the single source of truth — The 512-core HPC digital twin (CFD+FEA+EM+ML at 10 Hz) is the authoritative state estimator for control, safety, maintenance, training, and fleet optimization. [pause: short] All downstream consumers (PROD-34, 35, 36, 38, 39, 40) read from twin, not from raw sensors. [pause: short] These commitments are irreversible. [pause: short] They define the Forge's data nervous system. [pause: short] Any deviation requires SCSC unanimous approval and re-validation of the SIL-3 SIF proof test (CT-04) which is the gate to hot commissioning. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- Keymaker Heuristic — Implementation Precision ---

--- The Empirical Lock ---

Fabrication fidelity gap: Conventional data management platforms — PI System, Ignition, InfluxDB Cloud, AWS IoT SiteWise, Azure Digital Twins — assume: (a) IP-routable networks with centralized collection, (b) uniform sampling (1-10 Hz) with interpolation, (c) cloud-based compute with 100 ms - 1 s latency, (d) separate historian + analytics + twin as distinct products, (e) standard protocols (OPC-UA, MQTT, Kafka) end-to-end. [pause: short] They cannot model: (a) physically air-gapped network with zero IP routes where the only OT→IT path is a hardware data diode with protocol break, (b) multi-rate sensor fusion spanning 50 kHz (AE) → 125 Hz (FBG) → 1 kHz (EM) → 10 Hz (twin) → 1 Hz (fleet) with physics-constrained Kalman filtering, (c) digital twin as the real-time control authority running CFD+FEA+EM coupled at 10 Hz on 512 cores, not a passive visualization, (c) FBG channels as dual-purpose (process metrology + tamper detection via CPAT), (d) autoencoder anomaly detection on 384-dim state running in the twin at 10 Hz feeding SEV levels to IDS, IR, and HMI, (e) Bayesian fleet learning loop where twin posteriors update PID gains, RPM profiles, and flux rates across all Forges via staged ECO. [Table row: , --------, ---------, ------------, --------------, ]

[Table row: ,  main ,  Production baseline — only tagged releases ,  Required PR, 2 approvals (CM + Safety), signed commits, status checks ,  Fast-forward only from release branches , ]

[Table row: ,  release/vX.Y.Z ,  Release candidate — FAT/SAT validation ,  Required PR, CCB approval, CT-01 through CT-10 passed ,  Merge to main via tag code: prod-vX.Y.Z , ]

[Table row: ,  feature/ ,  ECO implementation — one branch per ECO ,  Required PR, 1 approval (discipline lead), signed commits ,  Squash merge to release branch after CCB , ]

[Table row: ,  hotfix/ ,  Emergency ECO — production hotfix ,  CM + Safety approval, expedited review ,  Direct to main + release branch, tagged code: hotfix-vX.Y.Z , ]

[Table row: ,  develop ,  Continuous integration — nightly builds ,  Status checks only (no approvals required) ,  Auto-merge from feature/ after CI pass , ]

--- 2.3 Commit & Tag Conventions ---

Commit Message Format:

[Code block]
<type>(<scope>): <subject>  [ECO-XXXX]

<body>

Signed-off-by: Name <email>
GPG-Signature: <key-id>
[End code block]

Types: code: feat (new capability), code: fix (defect correction), code: docs (documentation), code: config (configuration), code: cm (CM process), code: security (cyber), code: safety (SIL-3), code: test (test updates), code: chore (maintenance)

Tag Format:

[pause: short] code: prod-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — Production baseline (e.g., code: prod-v3.2.1)

[pause: short] code: fat-v<major>.<minor> — FAT baseline (e.g., code: fat-v1.0)

[pause: short] code: sat-v<major>.<minor> — SAT baseline (e.g., code: sat-v1.0)

[pause: short] code: eco-<number> — ECO implementation (e.g., code: eco-1042)

[pause: short] code: fpga-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — L0 FPGA bitstream

[pause: short] code: rtu-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — L1 RTU firmware

[pause: short] code: plc-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — L2 PLC program

[pause: short] code: scada-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — L3 SCADA software

[pause: short] code: twin-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — Digital twin software

[pause: short] code: rom-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — ROM export (PROD-24)

[pause: short] code: ml-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — ML models (PROD-37)

[pause: short] code: sec-v<major>.<minor>.<patch> — Security baseline (PROD-36)

Git Tag Chain (Cryptographic Proof):

[Code block]
fpga-v1.3.7 → rtu-v2.1.4 → plc-v3.0.1 → scada-v1.2.0 → twin-v2.0.0
    ↓            ↓            ↓            ↓            ↓
prod-v3.2.1 ← fat-v1.0 ← sat-v1.0 ← eco-1042 ← eco-1038
[End code block]

--- 2.4 Signed Commits & Verification ---

[pause: short] All commits to main/release branches MUST be GPG-signed (developer YubiKey or HSM)

[pause: short] CI pipeline verifies signatures — rejects unsigned commits

[pause: short] GitHub Vigilant Mode enabled — flags unverified signatures

[pause: short] Commit signature chain provides cryptographic provenance from requirements → code → test → deployment

--- 3. [pause: short] Engineering Change Order (ECO) Process ---

--- 3.1 ECO Classification ---

[Table row: ,  Class ,  Criteria ,  Max Lead Time ,  Approval ,  Deployment , ]

[Table row: , -------, ----------, ---------------, ----------, ------------, ]

[Table row: ,  Critical ,  Safety (SIL-3), Security (SL-C), Regulatory, Data integrity ,  72 hours ,  CCB unanimous + Safety + Cyber ,  Staged: 1 zone → 1 stage → full (CT-04 re-test each) , ]

[Table row: ,  Major ,  Performance, reliability, new capability, interface change ,  30 days ,  CCB majority + discipline leads ,  Staged: 1 zone → 1 stage → full (CT-04 partial) , ]

[Table row: ,  Minor ,  Bug fix, documentation, parameter tuning, cosmetic ,  14 days ,  Discipline lead + CM ,  Direct to next release branch , ]

[Table row: ,  Documentation ,  Spec clarification, typo, format, non-technical ,  7 days ,  CM only ,  Direct to main , ]

[Table row: ,  Emergency ,  Production stoppage, imminent safety/security risk ,  4 hours ,  CM + Safety (verbal), CCB ratification within 24h ,  Direct to main + hotfix tag, CT-04 within 7 days , ]

--- 3.2 ECO Lifecycle ---

[Code block]
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│  INITIATE   │────►│  ANALYZE    │────►│   REVIEW    │────►│  APPROVE    │
│  (Any role) │     │  (Originator)│     │   (CCB)     │     │  (CCB/Lead) │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └──────┬──────┘
                                                                     │
                    ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌────────┴──────┐
                    │   CLOSE     │◄────│  VERIFY     │◄────│  IMPLEMENT    │
                    │  (Originator)│     │  (QA/Ops)   │     │  (Developers) │
                    └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └───────────────┘
[End code block]

Detailed Steps:

[pause: short] INITIATE — Any role submits ECO request via GitHub Issue template:

[pause: short] Title: code: ECO-XXXX: <class> - <one-line summary>

[pause: short] Description: Problem statement, proposed change, affected CIs, urgency

[pause: short] Auto-assigned ECO number (sequential)

[pause: short] ANALYZE — Originator (with discipline leads) performs:

[pause: short] Impact analysis: affected CIs, test cases, downstream documents, suppliers

[pause: short] Risk assessment: SIL-3 impact (PROD-23 Table 6.2), cyber impact (PROD-36 CPAT), schedule

[pause: short] Implementation plan: branch name, tasks, test requirements, rollback procedure

[pause: short] Cost/schedule estimate

[pause: short] REVIEW — CCB convenes (weekly for Major, ad-hoc for Critical/Emergency):

[pause: short] Safety Engineering: SIL-3 impact verdict (no impact / re-analysis / re-cert)

[pause: short] Cyber Security: SL-C impact, firmware signing, SBOM update, supply chain

[pause: short] QA: Test plan adequacy, NCR linkage, FA requirements

[pause: short] Operations: Production impact, recipe changes, operator retraining

[pause: short] Supply Chain: AVL impact, SCN issuance, requalification needs

[pause: short] Training: DQR impact, simulator updates, curriculum changes

[pause: short] APPROVE — CCB decision recorded in GitHub Issue:

[pause: short] Approved: Implementation branch created, ECO moves to IMPLEMENT

[pause: short] Conditional: Approved with mandatory conditions (additional test, phased deploy)

[pause: short] Deferred: Moved to backlog with rationale

[pause: short] Rejected: Closed with rationale

[pause: short] IMPLEMENT — Developers work on code: feature/eco-XXXX branch:

[pause: short] All changes in single branch (atomic ECO)

[pause: short] Signed commits, PR to release branch

[pause: short] CI passes: lint, typecheck, test, signature-verify, split-chunks-verify

[pause: short] Documentation updated (PROD docs, intros, cross-references)

[pause: short] VERIFY — QA validates implementation:

[pause: short] Unit/integration tests pass (mutation >90%)

[pause: short] CT tests executed per test plan (PROD-39)

[pause: short] Regression: prior FAT/SAT baselines re-run (automated in CI)

[pause: short] Digital twin validation: ROM/ML model cards updated (PROD-37)

[pause: short] CLOSE — Originator confirms:

[pause: short] All acceptance criteria met

[pause: short] As-Built/As-Maintained/As-Operated baselines updated

[pause: short] DQR blockchain updated (PROD-28, 34)

[pause: short] ECO Issue closed with code: Closed: ECO-XXXX verified in prod-vX.Y.Z

--- 4. [pause: short] Baseline Management ---

--- 4.1 Four Baseline Views ---

The Forge maintains four configuration baselines, each a signed Git tag with associated artifacts:

[Table row: ,  Baseline ,  Scope ,  Tag Format ,  Update Trigger ,  Consumers , ]

[Table row: , ----------, -------, ------------, ----------------, -----------, ]

[Table row: ,  As-Designed ,  Engineering intent — PROD docs, ICDs, schemas, models ,  code: design-vX.Y.Z ,  ECO approval (Major/Critical) ,  Engineering, CCB, QA , ]

[Table row: ,  As-Built ,  Manufacturing realization — FA data, CT results, serial numbers ,  code: build-vX.Y.Z ,  FAT completion (CT-01..10 passed) ,  QA, Deployment, Supply Chain , ]

[Table row: ,  As-Maintained ,  Maintenance state — PM records, modifications, spare levels ,  code: maintain-vX.Y.Z ,  PM completion, field modification ECO ,  Maintenance, Reliability , ]

[Table row: ,  As-Operated ,  Operational state — recipes, parameters, operator certs, twin state ,  code: operate-vX.Y.Z ,  Batch recipe auth, shift handover, twin sync ,  Operations, Training, Fleet , ]

Version Constraint Rules:

[pause: short] Downstream document version ≥ Upstream document version (major.minor)

[pause: short] Patch versions independent (bug fixes don't propagate)

[pause: short] Breaking changes (major increment) require CCB + all downstream ECOs

--- 7.3 Document Change Workflow ---

Document changes follow ECO process (Sec 3) with code: docs type commits:

[pause: short] ECO submitted — code: ECO-XXXX: docs - Update PROD-XX Section Y.Y

[pause: short] Impact analysis — Cross-reference matrix check, downstream consumers notified

--- 9.3 DR Activation Procedure ---

[Code block]
DR ACTIVATION (Shift Lead Authority):

[pause: short] DECLARE: Shift Lead declares DR event (site loss, cyber, GIC, seismic)

[pause: short] NOTIFY: CCB, CSMFAB HQ, Safety, Cyber, Regulatory (per PROD-32)

[pause: short] MOBILIZE: Deploy cold standby config to alternate site (pre-identified)

[pause: short] RESTORE:
   a. [pause: short] Clone Git mirror → verify signatures, tags, merkle chain
   b. [pause: short] Load golden images (L0 FPGA, L1 RTU, L2 PLC, L3 SCADA)
   c. [pause: short] Load ROM/ML models → verify checksums
   d. [pause: short] Restore historian from 1 Hz backup → verify merkle continuity
   e. [pause: short] Re-establish data diode → verify IT→OT integrity
   f. [pause: short] Re-establish PTP → verify <1 μs sync across all nodes
   g. [pause: short] Run CT-04 partial-stroke (6 SIFs) → verify safety envelope

[pause: short] VALIDATE: 30-min soak, zero spurious alarms, twin sync <3σ

[pause: short] AUTHORIZE: Shift Lead + Safety Engineer dual-key → resume production

[pause: short] DOCUMENT: NCR auto-generated, ECO if permanent, lessons learned
[End code block]

--- 11.2 Firmware Integrity Verification ---

Boot-time (Every Power Cycle):

[Code block]

[pause: short] FPGA: Bitstream SHA-256 vs. [pause: short] HSM-stored golden hash → mismatch = halt

[pause: short] RTU: Firmware SHA-256 vs. [pause: short] TUF target → mismatch = halt + alert

[pause: short] PLC: Program CRC vs. [pause: short] signed manifest → mismatch = halt + alert

[pause: short] SCADA: Container image digest vs. [pause: short] signed SBOM → mismatch = alert

[pause: short] Twin: ROM/ML model checksums vs. [pause: short] Git tags → mismatch = alert
[End code block]

Runtime (Continuous):

[pause: short] FBG tamper detection → CPAT update (PROD-36)

[pause: short] TSN frame anomaly → CPAT update (PROD-36)

[pause: short] PTP offset > 1 μs → CPAT update (PROD-36)

[pause: short] Weekly SBOM diff vs. [pause: short] TUF repo → drift = block deploy + vendor CAPA

--- 11.3 Secure Boot Chain ---

[Code block]
HSM Root CA (Offline, air-gapped)
    │
    ├── HSM-CM (Configuration Manager) → signs Git tags, ECO approvals
    ├── HSM-BUILDER (CI/CD Pipeline) → signs SFP packages, SBOMs
    ├── HSM-SAFETY (Safety Engineering) → signs SIL-3 artifacts, CT-04
    ├── HSM-CYBER (Cyber Security) → signs CPAT params, TUF root
    └── HSM-OPS (Operations) → signs batch recipes, operator certs

Each Forge node (FPGA, RTU, PLC, SCADA, Twin, Switch, Diode):

[pause: short] Stores HSM-CM + HSM-BUILDER + HSM-SAFETY public keys

[pause: short] Verifies signature chain: artifact → builder → CM → root

[pause: short] Rejects any artifact with broken chain
[End code block]

--- 1. [pause: short] T&E Program Overview ---

--- 1.1 Purpose & Scope ---

This document defines the Test & Evaluation (T&E) program for the Aegis-Forge I Thermal Cascade Inductive Material Separator, establishing the verification and validation requirements that demonstrate the system meets all safety, performance, reliability, cybersecurity, human factors, environmental, and regulatory requirements prior to shipment, commissioning, and throughout the operational lifecycle. [pause: short] The T&E program implements ASME V&V 40 (Verification and Validation in Computational Solid Mechanics), IEEE 1220 (System Requirements Verification), MIL-STD-810 (Environmental Engineering), IEC 61508 (Functional Safety), IEC 62443 (Industrial Cybersecurity), ISA-101 (Human-Machine Interfaces), and ISO 9001/AS9100 requirements in a unified framework tailored to the Forge's unique constraints: zero-metal hot zone, all-dielectric control network, physical air-gap, SIL-3 safety integrity, and Carrington-class GIC immunity. --- 2. [pause: short] Horizon 1: Gen-II Evolution (2026-2029) ---

--- 2.1 2000L Scale-Up — From 226L to 2000L Working Volume ---

The Gen-I drum (600 mm diameter × 800 mm length = 226 L) validates the physics. [pause: short] Gen-II targets 2000L (9× volume) for industrial throughput while maintaining thermal gradient fidelity. [pause: short] --- 2.1.1 Geometric Scaling Laws ---

[Code block]
Gen-I:  D = 600 mm, L = 800 mm, V = 226 L, A = 1.51 m²
Gen-II: D = 1200 mm, L = 1800 mm, V = 2035 L, A = 6.79 m²
[End code block]

Scaling ratios:

[pause: short] Volume ratio: (1200/600)² × (1800/800) = 9.0×

[pause: short] Surface area ratio: (1200/600) × (1800/800) = 4.5×

[pause: short] Aspect ratio L/D preserved: 800/600 = 1.33 → 1800/1200 = 1.50 (adjusted for thermal gradient length)

Critical constraint — Thermal gradient preservation:
The 8-stage temperature profile requires sufficient axial length for discrete zones. [pause: short] Gen-I has 8 zones × 100 mm = 800 mm active length. [pause: short] Gen-II requires ≥ 1600 mm for equivalent zone resolution at 2× diameter. [pause: short] 1800 mm provides margin for transition zones. [pause: short] --- 2.1.2 Structural Scaling — ZrB₂-SiC Drum ---

Wall thickness scaling (pressure vessel criterion):
Hoop stress σ_θ = P·r/t. [pause: short] For constant pressure (5 bar operating, 10 bar design):
t_gen2 = t_gen1 × (r_gen2/r_gen1) = 35 mm × (600/300) = 70 mm minimum

Reality check — Ceramic drum at 1200 mm diameter with 70 mm wall:

[pause: short] Mass: π × (0.65² - 0.58²) × 1.8 × 3200 kg/m³ = ~4.2 metric tons (vs Gen-I ~650 kg)

[pause: short] Flash sintering: Requires 2.5 m × 2.5 m sintering furnace (new capital)

[pause: short] Thermal shock: ΔT across 70 mm wall at 2400°C surface = 120°C gradient (FEA validated in PROD-24)

Alternative — Segmented drum architecture:
8 × 200 mm axial segments, each independently replaceable. [pause: short] Joint design: ZrB₂-SiC tongue-and-groove with PEEK CF40 compliant layer (PROD-09 valve seat heritage). [pause: short] Reduces single-piece sintering risk; enables staged replacement. [pause: short] --- 2.1.3 Induction Power Scaling ---

[Code block]
Gen-I: 500 kW total, 8 zones × 62.5 kW average
Gen-II: Target 4 MW total, 8 zones × 500 kW average
[End code block]

[pause: short] Stage 3: 50 kHz → 200 kW/zone

--- 2.3 Advanced Induction Control — Beyond GaN ---

--- 2.3.1 SiC MOSFET Transition (Gen-II) ---

Why SiC for 500 kW/zone:

[pause: short] 1.7 kV rating matches 480V 3-phase bus with margin

[pause: short] 200°C junction temperature enables higher power density

[pause: short] Two-phase cooling (dielectric immersion) handles 500 kW in 0.5U rack

[pause: short] Body diode reverse recovery <50 ns enables hard-switching at 2 kHz (Stage 7)

Zone architecture:

[Code block]
[3-Phase 480V] → [Active Front End] → [800V DC Bus] → [8 × Zone Inverter]
                                                                   │
                                                         [FBG Feedback 10 kHz]
                                                         [PID + MPC Control]
[End code block]

Model Predictive Control (MPC) replaces PID:
State vector x = [T_zone, T_wall, T_drum, ω_drum, P_induction]
Cost function: J = Σ(Q·(T_target - T)² + R·ΔP²) + P·(T_constraint_violation)
Horizon: 20 steps (2 sec at 10 Hz). [pause: short] Solves QP in <1 ms on ARM Cortex-R52 (PROD-37 edge compute). [pause: short] --- 2.3.2 Diamond Semiconductor Roadmap (Gen-III) ---

Diamond FET advantages:

[pause: short] Bandgap: 5.47 eV (vs SiC 3.26 eV, GaN 3.4 eV)

[pause: short] Thermal conductivity: 2200 W/m·K (vs SiC 370, GaN 130)

[pause: short] Breakdown field: 10 MV/cm (vs SiC 3 MV/cm)

[pause: short] Enables direct liquid metal cooling (GaInSn) at 400°C junction

Stage 0: Acoustic Liberation (skip — regolith already disaggregated)

Stage 2: Skip (no polymers)
Stage 3: Skip (no organics)
Stage 4: FeO Reduction Window (800-1000°C) → H₂ reduction: FeO + H₂ → Fe + H₂O
Stage 5: Ilmenite Reduction (1000-1100°C) → FeTiO₃ + H₂ → Fe + TiO₂ + H₂O
Stage 6: Aluminum Extraction (1600-1800°C) → Al₂O₃ electrolysis (molten salt) OR carbothermal
Stage 7: Silicate Glass Formation (1400-1600°C) → Basalt fiber, structural glass
Stage 8: Residual Oxides (CaO, MgO) → Slag for radiation shielding bricks
[End code block]

[Code block]
MARTIAN AEGIS-FORGE — CO₂ + REGOLITH CO-PROCESSING

Stage 1 (150°C): CO₂ compression/liquefaction + H₂O removal → LOX/LCH4 feedstock
Stage 2 (300°C): Perchlorate decomposition → Cl₂ capture (ZrO₂ scrubber) → O₂ release
Stage 3 (500°C): Sulfate decomposition → SO₂ capture → H₂SO₄ production

--- 3.3.2 Simplified Cascade (4-Stage) ---

[Code block]
ASTEROID AEGIS-FORGE — METALLIC SEPARATION ONLY

Stage 0: Acoustic (microgravity — capillary/acoustic hybrid)
Stage 1: Skip (no volatiles)

Stage 3: Skip (no organics)
Stage 4: Ni-Co-PGM separation (1455°C Ni, 1495°C Co) → Centrifugal density strat

Microgravity separation physics:
In microgravity, centrifugal force IS the effective gravity. [pause: short] Drum at 500 RPM, r=0.6m → 167 G. [pause: short] Density stratification occurs radially:

[pause: short] Inner radius: Fe (7.87 g/cm³)

[pause: short] Mid radius: Ni-Co (8.9 g/cm³)

[pause: short] Outer radius: PGM (12-22 g/cm³)

Port design: Radial ports at calculated density boundaries. [pause: short] No thermal actuators needed — ports opened by commanded drum position. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- 3.4 Microgravity Thermal Cascade — Capillary/Centrifugal Hybrid ---

Challenge: In microgravity, liquid metals don't pool at the bottom — they form spheres held by surface tension. [pause: short] Centrifugal force must overcome surface tension. [pause: short] Bond number criterion:
Bo = ρ·ω²·r·L²/σ > 10 for reliable separation

[pause: short] ρ = 7000 kg/m³ (Fe), σ = 1.8 N/m (Fe surface tension at 1600°C)

[pause: short] L = characteristic length (drum radius = 0.6 m)

[pause: short] Required ω: ω > √(10·σ/(ρ·r·L²)) = √(10×1.8/(7000×0.6×0.36)) = 0.11 rad/s = 1 RPM

At 100 RPM (104 rad/s): Bo = 10,000 >> 10. [pause: short] Separation is robust. [pause: short] Capillary assist: Helical grooves on drum inner surface (ZrB₂-SiC) guide liquid metal toward ports via capillary wicking (PROD-09 valve heritage). [pause: short] Groove geometry: 2 mm wide × 1 mm deep, 30° helix angle. [pause: short] [pause: long]

--- The Triune Frame ---

This document — PROD-40: Future Evolution & Roadmap — is the capstone synthesis of the Aegis-Forge Product Document series (PROD-01 through PROD-39). [pause: short] It does not stand alone; it is the recursive closure of the entire specification tree. [pause: short] The three heuristic lenses reveal its nature:

Williams (Architectural Clarity) identifies the Constraint: material closure. [pause: short] The machine cannot be sovereign until it reproduces its own bill of materials. [pause: short] The Necessity: staged closure with external subsidy — Gen-II scale, space feedstocks, waste liabilities as negative-cost inputs. [pause: short] The Commitment: invariant cascade physics, All-Aegis fidelity, open-licensed engineering. [pause: short] Keymaker (Implementation Precision) identifies the Lock: thermal gradient fidelity across 9× volume, 4× diameter, and four extraterrestrial/remediation boundary conditions. [pause: short] The Key: the Recursive Bayesian Thermal Oracle (RBTO) — one computational primitive governing zone control, batch optimization, feed synthesis, and roadmap gate validation across all horizons. [pause: short] The Turn: Theory→History via virtual commissioning; History→Theory via horizon data feeding the universal thermal model [Inline equation: \mathcal{M}_\theta]. [pause: short] El Segundo (Operational Excellence) identifies the Mirror: dual-sensor architecture (physical FBG + virtual RBTO likelihood) reflecting process fidelity and roadmap divergence in real time. [pause: short] The Participation: triad governance (Thermal Architect, Materials Steward, Sovereignty Officer) certifying physics at four recursive ceremonies. [pause: short] The Protocol: Horizon Gate Protocol (HGP) — a mandatory git-enforced sequence of prior extraction, simulation, build, and KL-divergence validation at each scale transition. [pause: short] These three lenses are not perspectives on the roadmap. [pause: short] They are the load-bearing structure of the roadmap. [pause: short] Remove Williams, and the roadmap has no strategic necessity — it becomes a wish list. [pause: short] Remove Keymaker, and the roadmap has no technical credibility — it becomes a cartoon. [pause: short] Remove El Segundo, and the roadmap has no operational reality — it becomes a PowerPoint. [pause: short] [pause: long]
